『続日本紀』[[天平神護]]元年11月条によれば、上野国甘楽郡人の中衛・物部蜷淵ら5人が、同2年5月条によれば、上野国甘楽郡人の外大初位下・礒部牛麻呂ら4人がそれぞれ物部公を賜わっている『続日本紀』。 === 複姓の上毛野氏 === 上毛野氏には複姓の一族（血縁関係はない場合もある）として、上毛野坂本朝臣、上毛野佐位朝臣、上毛野陸奥公、上毛野名取朝臣、上毛野鍬山公、上毛野中山公などがいる。特に名前が見えるのは上毛野坂本朝臣で、『新撰姓氏録』によるとこれは佐太公（豊城入彦命十世孫）の末裔であるとされる。最初に上毛野坂本という氏が確認できるのは[[大宝 (日本)|大宝]]元年（[[701年]]）で、[[碓氷郡]]の[[上毛野坂本登与|石上部登与]]という人物が上毛野坂本君の氏姓を賜ったとされる。[[天平勝宝]]5年（[[753年]]）には、[[碓氷郡]]出身で[[国分寺]]の僧侶であった外従五位下・[[上毛野坂本諸弟|石上部諸弟]]と左京の人で登与の子である[[上毛野坂本男嶋|石上部男嶋]]が上毛野坂本君の氏姓を賜っている。[[神護景雲]]元年（[[767年]]）には、[[碓氷郡]]出身の[[上毛野坂本男嶋|上毛野坂本君男嶋]]と[[上毛野坂本黒益|上毛野坂本君黒益]]が上毛野坂本朝臣の氏姓を賜っている。 上毛野佐位朝臣は[[檜前部老刀自]]が賜った。[[孝謙天皇#重祚：称徳天皇としての治世|称徳朝]]の[[天平神護]]3年（[[767年]]）に上野佐位朝臣を賜姓ている。さらにその翌年の[[神護景雲]]2年（[[768年]]）には、[[上野国]]の[[国造]]に任命されている。なお、[[天平]]13年（[[741年]]）には、揩布屏風袋第二號銘文に「佐位郡佐位郷戸主檜前部黒麻呂」と「正六位上勲十二等（佐位）郡司大領外檜前部君賀味麻呂」の名前が見える。 上毛野陸奥公は、[[神護景雲]]元年（[[767年]]）に[[陸奥国]][[宇多郡]]の吉弥侯部石麻呂が、同3年（[[769年]]）に同郡の吉弥侯部文知が賜っている。同年には、[[名取郡]]の吉弥侯部老人らが上毛野名取朝臣を、[[信夫郡]]の吉弥侯部足山守らが上毛野鍬山公を、[[新田郡]]の吉弥侯部豊庭が上毛野中村公を賜わっている。 == 考証 == === 毛野との関係 === ==== 文献の考証 ==== 『古事記』『日本書紀』では上毛野氏に関して多彩な伝承が記述されるが、7世紀中葉（大化前後）を境として唐突に史録として記載されるため、伝承と史録との間には大きな溝がある。史録の部分からは毛野との関わりをうかがえる記載は少なく、この間をどう扱うかが氏族を把握するための鍵となっている。毛野地域内には、豊城入彦命を始めとした『日本書紀』の伝承にある人物の陵墓と伝わる古墳が多くあり、伝承に何らかの背景があったことが指摘されており、その中で、毛野の地域づくりが東国経営の拠点と位置づけられ、それを世襲的に任された王族がいたことも示唆される「毛野の黎明－三～四世紀における地域形成のあゆみ」（『群馬史再発見』）。。ただし実際のところ、毛野の豪族が在地豪族であったか中央派遣氏族であったかは明らかとなっていない山本博文『あなたの知らない群馬県の歴史』（洋泉社）Q8。。 * 中央派遣氏族か在地豪族かについて *: 前述のように『古事記』『日本書紀』では朝廷から祖先が派遣されたと記すほか、『国造本紀』の上毛野国造条にも他の国造の項にあるはずの「定賜国造」の文言がなく、これらをもって上毛野氏が中央からの派遣氏族だとする主張がある。上毛野国造の記述は史書にはなく存在は不確かであるが、畿外勢力でありながら中級貴族官人となり得た上毛野氏始め東国六腹朝臣は、他の国造グループとは一線を画すものだという指摘もある『古代東国の王者 上毛野氏の研究』第一章。。 *: 一方で、実際には上毛野（上野）・下毛野（下野）に分かれる以前に存在した「毛野政権」の王であった豪族と見る考えもある{{Kotobank|上毛野氏|[[世界大百科事典]]}}。これに関連して、[[武蔵国造の乱]]における上毛野氏の立場から、上毛野氏は6世紀前半期まで大和朝廷に対抗出来るだけの勢力を有していたとみる見解も古くから存在する。後述の古墳の変容を踏まえても、5世紀代に[[ヤマト王権]]と同盟・連合関係にあったと考えられる「毛野政権」は、解体を経て[[6世紀]]前半からヤマト王権の体制に入っていくと見る説がある。 * 紀伊・和泉との関係について *: [[赤城山]]を祀る[[赤城神社]]には、上毛野氏による創祀伝承が残っている。『日本書紀』では豊城入彦命の母が紀伊出身と記載がある。また「赤城」の由来の一説としても、上毛野氏が歴史編纂にあたって祖先と発生地を「紀（き = [[紀伊国|紀伊]]）」地方に求め、祖先の名を「とよき（豊城入彦命）」・信仰する山を「あかき（赤城山）」とした、と関連づける考えがある『群馬県の地名』赤城山項。。 *: これに関連し、『新撰姓氏録』の豊城入彦命後裔として諸蕃雑姓の和泉・摂津・河内のグループがあることに着目し、紀伊に始まって5世紀まではこれらの地で勢力を築き、のち6・7世紀は東国に移住して勢力を伸ばし、8世紀以後は中央貴族として活躍したという説が提唱されている。 * 三輪山との関係について *: 豊城入彦命が夢の中で御諸山（= [[三輪山]]）に登ったという伝承や、御諸別王の名、田道の墓から大蛇が出たという説話、形名の妻が弓弦を鳴らさせて蝦夷を破ったという説話から、[[大物主|御諸山の神]]を奉じて東国経営を行なったことが示唆される『国史大辞典』上毛野氏項。。また[[上毛野国造]]、[[下毛野国造]]の両国には[[式内社]]で大神神社や美和神社、大国神社が見られ、赤城神社においても[[大己貴神]]を祀るなどしている。これは、[[大物主|御諸山の神]]が軍神的な役割を果たしていた{{efn|『[[筑前国]][[風土記]]』逸文によれば、[[神功皇后]]が三韓を征伐しようとして兵士を集めて出発すると、兵士が道の途中で消え失せてしまった。その理由を占うと大三輪神の祟りだと出たため、筑前国に神社を建て、[[三韓征伐]]は成功したという。}}{{efn|『日本書紀』[[仲哀天皇]]9年9月条には「時に軍卒集い難し。皇后曰わく、必ず神の心ならむとのりたまひて、即ち大三輪社を建てて、刀矛を奉りたまふ。軍集自づから聚る」とある}}ことと関連しているとする説がある鈴木正信『大神氏の研究』雄山閣、2014年）『大神と石上　神体山と禁足地』（筑摩書房、1988年）。 ==== 考古資料による考証 ==== [[ファイル:Ōtatenjinnyama-kofun zenkei.JPG|thumb|right|[[太田天神山古墳]]（[[群馬県]][[太田市]]）
[[毛野]]を象徴する東日本最大の古墳。]] 毛野地域（群馬県・栃木県南西部）は、[[古墳時代]]に多くの[[古墳]]が築かれたことが知られる。特に上毛野地域（群馬県）においては、東日本最大の[[太田天神山古墳]]（群馬県[[太田市]]、全長210mで全国26位）なお、以前には太田天神山古墳以上の規模と推考される古墳の議論がなされていた。1つには、推定全長220m以上として雷電山古墳（[[栃木県]][[宇都宮市]]）が挙げられることがあったが（『栃木県の地名』雷電山古墳項等）、1990年の調査で推定古墳跡地上で住居跡が見つかり、大規模古墳であることは否定されている。また、米山古墳（栃木県[[佐野市]]）も「米山丘陵全体が古墳」だとして全長約360mとする説があるが（現地説明板等）、現在はほぼ否定されている（[http://www.tochigi-edu.ed.jp/center/bunkazai/2341027.htm 米山古墳]（とちぎの文化財））。を始めとして、全長が80mを越す大型古墳が45基、総数では約1万3000基もの古墳が築かれている群馬県内では、1935年の調査で8,423基の古墳が（『上毛古墳綜覧』）、2012-2015年度の調査で13,249基の古墳が確認されている（[https://web.archive.org/web/20170304223028/http://www.yomiuri.co.jp/local/gunma/news/20170304-OYTNT50245.html "古墳王国裏付け1万3249基"]<読売新聞、2017年3月5日記事>）。。 4世紀初頭には[[前方後方墳]]が築かれ、同地方由来の土器が使用されていた。4世紀中葉以降は[[前方後円墳]]に移行し、畿内の石工による石棺の築造も認められる。これらから毛野では首長連合政権が形成されたと見られ、少なくとも[[5世紀]]前半以降には畿内の豪族と同盟にあり、[[ヤマト政権]]内部で極めて重要な位置を占めたと考える説がある[[白石太一郎]]『古墳とヤマト政権―古代国家はいかに形成されたか』（[[文藝春秋]]［文春新書］、[[1999年]]、ISBN 4166600362）。。5世紀中頃には東日本最大の[[太田天神山古墳]]が築かれ、一帯で最大規模を誇っていた。この太田天神山古墳（群馬県太田市）やお富士山古墳（群馬県伊勢崎市）には、ヤマト王権の王陵に見られる長持形石棺が使用されている山本博文『あなたの知らない群馬県の歴史』（洋泉社）Q3。（詳しくは「[[毛野]]」を参照）。また[[安本美典]]は太田天神山古墳と同時期の築造で、毛野と遠く離れた吉備地方の[[造山古墳]]が殆ど正確に相似形であると指摘している{{要出典|date=2022年8月}}。 後世の上毛野氏の東国六腹朝臣における盟主的立場から上毛野氏と毛野政権との関係が指摘されるが、この当時にいた豪族の詳細は明らかではない。 6世紀後半からは、地域内の各地に大型古墳の林立が顕著となる。これら各地に豪族が割拠していたと見られ、上毛野氏の本拠地としては『[[続日本紀]]』の「上野国勢多郡小領」の文言『続日本紀』天平勝宝元年閏5月20日条。や赤城信仰の中核である[[赤城神社]]の存在を基として{{underline|「赤城山南麓」}}と見るのが定説とされ、その地にある[[大室古墳群 (前橋市)|大室古墳群]]（群馬県前橋市）が注目されている『古代東国の王者 上毛野氏の研究』第三章。。 一方、7世紀に入っても大型の方墳が築かれ続けた{{underline|総社古墳群（群馬県前橋市）}}に本拠地を求める説もある『よみがえる五世紀の世界』（かみつけの里博物館、常設展示解説書）。。この地には山王廃寺（放光寺）があり関係性が指摘されるほか、後世には上野国府が設置されることとなる。 === 氏族の広がり === [[東国六腹朝臣]]」とは上毛野氏、[[下毛野氏]]、大野氏、池田氏、佐味氏、車持氏の総称で、いずれも[[天武天皇]]13年（[[684年]]）に[[八色の姓]]において「[[朝臣]]」の姓を授けられた『日本書紀』天武天皇13年11月条。。「東国六腹朝臣」の名称自体は『[[続日本紀]]』の1条に記載されるのみであるが、その中で池原・上毛野2氏の出自が豊城入彦命であること、豊城入彦命の子孫である「東国六腹朝臣」は居地によって姓と氏を得たことが記載されている『続日本紀』延暦10年4月条。。東国六腹朝臣の特質として、畿外出身ながら「朝臣」という高いカバネの取得、国史編纂・律令撰定への参画、対朝鮮・対蝦夷政策への従事が挙げられる「上毛野国から東国へ」（『群馬史再発見』）。。そしてこれら6氏は各々独自の始祖を持っていたことが『新撰姓氏録』からわかる。 紀伊・和泉系氏族とは、本貫を紀伊・河内・和泉等とする氏族で、東国六腹朝臣グループとの重複も見られる。また、このグループにのみ[[八綱田|八綱田命]]の記載が見られることや、皇別を称しながら未定雑姓に組み込まれた氏族があることも特徴である。 これらに関して、豊城入彦命の母が紀伊の豪族出身であったことに着目し、第3グループを氏族の発生地と見た以下のモデルが提唱されている『古代東国の王者 上毛野氏の研究』終章。。 * 500年頃以前 - 紀伊・和泉において文化・軍事両面で対朝鮮交渉に活躍。 * 6・7世紀 - 蝦夷との戦いのため東国に派遣され東国六腹朝臣としての勢力を構築。 * 700年頃以降 - 中央官人として活躍。 また、上毛野氏が対朝鮮で活躍する過程で渡来してきたのが第2グループであろう、と考察が加えられる。ただしモデルには不明な点も多く、実態の解明には更なる考証が必要とされる。 == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} === 注 === {{reflist|group="注"}} === 注釈 === {{reflist|group="注釈"}} === 原典 === {{Reflist|group="原"|2}} === 出典 === {{Reflist|2}} == 参考文献 == '''百科事典''' * 『日本古代史大辞典』（[[大和書房]]）上毛野氏項、下毛野氏項 * 『国史大辞典』（[[吉川弘文館]]）上毛野氏項、下毛野氏項 * 『世界大百科事典』（[[平凡社]]）上毛野氏項、下毛野氏項 - 朝日新聞社コトバンクに該当記事（[https://kotobank.jp/word/%E4%B8%8A%E6%AF%9B%E9%87%8E%E6%B0%8F-1155660 上毛野氏]、[https://kotobank.jp/word/%E4%B8%8B%E6%AF%9B%E9%87%8E%E6%B0%8F-1172624 下毛野氏]） * 『日本歴史地名体系 revision.text:
{{Ancient Japanese Clans | Clan Name = Kamitsukeno Clan | Image = [[File:Akagi-jinja (Miyosawa) torii.JPG|280px]]
Shrine associated with the clan: [[Akagi Shrine]] ({{ill|Gunma Prefecture|ja|群馬県}}, {{ill|Maebashi|ja|前橋市}}) | Title = Kamitsukeno no Kimi (公)
Later Kamitsukeno no Asomi | Founder = '''Claimed''': {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命}}
({{ill|Emperor Sujin|ja|崇神天皇}}'s son) | Lineage = Imperial | Origin = Kamitsukeno Province (modern-day {{ill|Gunma Prefecture|ja|群馬県}})
Later relocated to Yamashiro Province | Notable Members = See [[Kamitsukeno Clan#Notable Figures|Notable Figures Section]] | Descendants = See [[Kamitsukeno Clan#Related Clans|Related Clans Section]] }} The '''Kamitsukeno Clan''' (上毛野氏, also read as ''Kamitsukenu'')While the reading ''Kamitsukenu'' has been used since the Edo period, some scholars argue this is a misreading. See [[Kenō#Origin and Pronunciation]]. was a [[Japanese clan]] that took its name from the region of Kamitsukeno. Members of the clan often served as [[kuni no miyatsuko]] (provincial governors). The clan claimed descent from {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命}}, a son of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|ja|崇神天皇}}, and was categorized as an imperial lineage (皇別). Over time, the clan adopted the titles "Kamitsukeno no Kimi (公)" and later "Kamitsukeno no Asomi (朝臣)." The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records the clan's lineage and traditions, which are also shared with other related clans. This article provides an overview of the Kamitsukeno Clan and its related clans. == Overview == The Kamitsukeno Clan was based in the ancient Kamitsukeno region (modern {{ill|Gunma Prefecture|ja|群馬県}}), as indicated by its name. The term ''Kenō'' (毛野) referred to the areas of modern-day Gunma and Tochigi Prefectures in ancient times.{{Kotobank|毛野|MyPedia|ja}} The region was later divided into {{ill|Kōzuke Province|ja|上野国}} (Gunma) and {{ill|Shimotsuke Province|ja|下野国}} (Tochigi). Gunma Prefecture, in particular, is home to many [[kofun]] (ancient burial mounds), indicating the region's significance in early Japan (see [[Kenō]]). The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records that the clan originated from {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命}}, who was dispatched to govern the eastern provinces under imperial command. The text also describes the Kamitsukeno Clan's military and diplomatic activities, particularly concerning interactions with the [[Emishi]] and [[Korea]]. However, whether the clan was a local ruling family or one dispatched from the central court remains unclear.Hirofumi Yamamoto, "History of Gunma You Don't Know" (Yōsensha). Archaeological evidence and later texts support the clan's involvement in regional governance and foreign relations.Toru Wakasa, "Regional Administration in the Ancient Kofun Period" (Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2021). By the late 7th century, the Kamitsukeno Clan became one of the "Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces" (東国六腹朝臣), which included the {{ill|Shimotsukeno Clan|ja|下毛野氏}}, Ōno Clan, Ikeda Clan, Sami Clan, and Kuramochi Clan. These clans played active roles as mid-level aristocrats in the imperial court.{{Kotobank|Kamitsukeno Clan|ja}} == Genealogy == The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records that {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命}}, a son of Emperor Sujin, was dispatched to govern the eastern provinces. It also states that he was the ancestor of the {{ill|Kamitsukeno no Kimi|ja|上毛野君}} and {{ill|Shimotsukeno no Kimi|ja|下毛野君}}.''Nihon Shoki,'' Emperor Sujin, 48th Year. The {{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記}} contains similar records.''Kojiki,'' Emperor Sujin. The {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|ja|新撰姓氏録}} states that the Kamitsukeno Asomi (Upper Capital Courtier) lineage was descended from Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto.''Shinsen Shōjiroku,'' Kamitsukeno Asomi, Imperial Lineage (Right Capital). Furthermore, the {{ill|Kokuzō Hongi|ja|国造本紀}} mentions that Toyoki Iribiko's grandson, {{ill|Hikosashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島王}}, was appointed as the first {{ill|kuni no miyatsuko|ja|国造}} of the Kamitsukeno region after pacifying twelve eastern provinces.''Kokuzō Hongi,'' Kamitsukeno Kuni no Miyatsuko. == Historical Overview == The Kamitsukeno Clan's transition from regional power to court aristocracy is evident in both textual and archaeological records. During the early Kofun period, the region saw the construction of large burial mounds, such as the {{ill|Ōtatenjin'yama Kofun|ja|太田天神山古墳}}, indicating a powerful local authority.Taichirō Shiraishi, "Kofun and the Yamato Court" (Bungeishunjū). The clan's later prominence in the central court suggests their integration into the Yamato polity. By the mid-7th century, members of the Kamitsukeno Clan held positions as provincial governors, military leaders, and diplomats. The clan's influence waned in the Heian period, with members becoming lower-ranking court officials and regional administrators.{{Kotobank|Kamitsukeno Clan|Encyclopedia Nipponica|ja}} == Notable Figures == Notable descendants of {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命}} include: * {{ill|Hikosashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島王}} - Appointed governor of 15 eastern provinces. * {{ill|Mimorowake no Mikoto|ja|御諸別命}} - Military leader who fought the Emishi. * {{ill|Aratawake|ja|荒田別}} - Diplomat to Korea. * {{ill|Takihase|ja|竹葉瀬}} - Contributed to Korean diplomacy. * {{ill|Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko|ja|上毛野稚子}} - General in the Baekje campaigns. == Related Clans == The Kamitsukeno Clan's descendants include several related families, categorized as the "Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces." These clans shared genealogical and geographical ties with the Kamitsukeno lineage. == See Also == * {{ill|Kenō|ja|毛野}} * {{ill|Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces|ja|東国六腹朝臣}} ** {{ill|Shimotsukeno Clan|ja|下毛野氏}} * {{ill|Kamitsukeno no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|上毛野国造}} * {{ill|Akagi Shrine|ja|赤城神社}} [[Category:Kamitsukeno Clan]] [[Category:Clans]] [[Category:Japanese clans]] [[Category:Clans of Kantō region]] [[Category:History of Gunma Prefecture]] [[ja:上毛野氏]]

Gunma Prefecture, in particular, is home to many [[kofun]] (ancient burial mounds), indicating the region's significance in early Japan (see [[Kenō]]). The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records that the clan originated from {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命}}, who was dispatched to govern the eastern provinces under imperial command. The text also describes the Kamitsukeno Clan's military and diplomatic activities, particularly concerning interactions with the [[Emishi]] and [[Korea]]. However, whether the clan was a local ruling family or one dispatched from the central court remains unclear.Hirofumi Yamamoto, "History of Gunma You Don't Know" (Yōsensha). Archaeological evidence and later texts support the clan's involvement in regional governance and foreign relations.Toru Wakasa, "Regional Administration in the Ancient Kofun Period" (Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2021). By the late 7th century, the Kamitsukeno Clan became one of the "Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces" (東国六腹朝臣), which included the {{ill|Shimotsukeno Clan|ja|下毛野氏}}, Ōno Clan, Ikeda Clan, Sami Clan, and Kuramochi Clan. These clans played active roles as mid-level aristocrats in the imperial court.{{Kotobank|Kamitsukeno Clan|ja}} == Genealogy == The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records that {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命}}, a son of Emperor Sujin, was dispatched to govern the eastern provinces. It also states that he was the ancestor of the {{ill|Kamitsukeno no Kimi|ja|上毛野君}} and {{ill|Shimotsukeno no Kimi|ja|下毛野君}}.''Nihon Shoki,'' Emperor Sujin, 48th Year. The {{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記}} contains similar records.''Kojiki,'' Emperor Sujin. The {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|ja|新撰姓氏録}} states that the Kamitsukeno Asomi (Upper Capital Courtier) lineage was descended from Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto.''Shinsen Shōjiroku,'' Kamitsukeno Asomi, Imperial Lineage (Right Capital). Furthermore, the {{ill|Kokuzō Hongi|ja|国造本紀}} mentions that Toyoki Iribiko's grandson, {{ill|Hikosashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島王}}, was appointed as the first {{ill|kuni no miyatsuko|ja|国造}} of the Kamitsukeno region after pacifying twelve eastern provinces.''Kokuzō Hongi,'' Kamitsukeno Kuni no Miyatsuko. == Historical Overview == The Kamitsukeno Clan's transition from regional power to court aristocracy is evident in both textual and archaeological records. During the early Kofun period, the region saw the construction of large burial mounds, such as the {{ill|Ōtatenjin'yama Kofun|ja|太田天神山古墳}}, indicating a powerful local authority.Taichirō Shiraishi, "Kofun and the Yamato Court" (Bungeishunjū). The clan's later prominence in the central court suggests their integration into the Yamato polity. By the mid-7th century, members of the Kamitsukeno Clan held positions as provincial governors, military leaders, and diplomats. The clan's influence waned in the Heian period, with members becoming lower-ranking court officials and regional administrators.{{Kotobank|Kamitsukeno Clan|Encyclopedia Nipponica|ja}} == Notable Figures == Notable descendants of {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命}} include: * {{ill|Hikosashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島王}} - Appointed governor of 15 eastern provinces. * {{ill|Mimorowake no Mikoto|ja|御諸別命}} - Military leader who fought the Emishi. * {{ill|Aratawake|ja|荒田別}} - Diplomat to Korea. * {{ill|Takihase|ja|竹葉瀬}} - Contributed to Korean diplomacy. * {{ill|Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko|ja|上毛野稚子}} - General in the Baekje campaigns. == Related Clans == The Kamitsukeno Clan's descendants include several related families, categorized as the "Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces." These clans shared genealogical and geographical ties with the Kamitsukeno lineage. == See Also == * {{ill|Kenō|ja|毛野}} * {{ill|Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces|ja|東国六腹朝臣}} ** {{ill|Shimotsukeno Clan|ja|下毛野氏}} * {{ill|Kamitsuke no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|上毛野国造}} * {{ill|Akagi Shrine|ja|赤城神社}} [[Category:original pages]][[Category:Kamitsukeno Clan]] [[Category:original pages]][[Category:Clans]] [[Category:original pages]][[Category:Japanese clans]] [[Category:original pages]][[Category:Clans of Kantō region]] [[Category:original pages]][[Category:History of Gunma Prefecture]] [[ja:上毛野氏]]

See [[Kenō#Origin and Pronunciation]]. was a [[Japanese clan]] that took its name from the region of Kamitsukeno. Members of the clan often served as [[kuni no miyatsuko]] (provincial governors). The clan claimed descent from {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命}}, a son of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|ja|崇神天皇}}, and was categorized as an imperial lineage (皇別). Over time, the clan adopted the titles "Kamitsukeno no Kimi (公)" and later "Kamitsukeno no Asomi (朝臣)." The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records the clan's lineage and traditions, which are also shared with other related clans. This article provides an overview of the Kamitsukeno Clan and its related clans. == Overview == The Kamitsukeno Clan was based in the ancient Kamitsukeno region (modern {{ill|Gunma Prefecture|ja|群馬県}}), as indicated by its name. The term ''Kenō'' (毛野) referred to the areas of modern-day Gunma and Tochigi Prefectures in ancient times.{{Kotobank|毛野|MyPedia|ja}} The region was later divided into {{ill|Kōzuke Province|ja|上野国}} (Gunma) and {{ill|Shimotsuke Province|ja|下野国}} (Tochigi). Gunma Prefecture, in particular, is home to many [[kofun]] (ancient burial mounds), indicating the region's significance in early Japan (see [[Kenō]]). The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records that the clan originated from {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命}}, who was dispatched to govern the eastern provinces under imperial command. The text also describes the Kamitsukeno Clan's military and diplomatic activities, particularly concerning interactions with the [[Emishi]] and [[Korea]]. However, whether the clan was a local ruling family or one dispatched from the central court remains unclear.Hirofumi Yamamoto, "History of Gunma You Don't Know" (Yōsensha). Archaeological evidence and later texts support the clan's involvement in regional governance and foreign relations.Toru Wakasa, "Regional Administration in the Ancient Kofun Period" (Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2021). By the late 7th century, the Kamitsukeno Clan became one of the "Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces" (東国六腹朝臣), which included the {{ill|Shimotsukeno Clan|ja|下毛野氏}}, Ōno Clan, Ikeda Clan, Sami Clan, and Kuramochi Clan. These clans played active roles as mid-level aristocrats in the imperial court.{{Kotobank|Kamitsukeno Clan|ja}} == Genealogy == The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records that {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命}}, a son of Emperor Sujin, was dispatched to govern the eastern provinces. It also states that he was the ancestor of the {{ill|Kamitsukeno no Kimi|ja|上毛野君}} and {{ill|Shimotsukeno no Kimi|ja|下毛野君}}.''Nihon Shoki,'' Emperor Sujin, 48th Year. The {{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記}} contains similar records.''Kojiki,'' Emperor Sujin. The {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|ja|新撰姓氏録}} states that the Kamitsukeno Asomi (Upper Capital Courtier) lineage was descended from Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto.''Shinsen Shōjiroku,'' Kamitsukeno Asomi, Imperial Lineage (Right Capital). Furthermore, the {{ill|Kokuzō Hongi|ja|国造本紀}} mentions that Toyoki Iribiko's grandson, {{ill|Hikosashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島王}}, was appointed as the first {{ill|kuni no miyatsuko|ja|国造}} of the Kamitsukeno region after pacifying twelve eastern provinces.''Kokuzō Hongi,'' Kamitsukeno Kuni no Miyatsuko. == Historical Overview == The Kamitsukeno Clan's transition from regional power to court aristocracy is evident in both textual and archaeological records. During the early Kofun period, the region saw the construction of large burial mounds, such as the {{ill|Ōtatenjin'yama Kofun|ja|太田天神山古墳}}, indicating a powerful local authority.Taichirō Shiraishi, "Kofun and the Yamato Court" (Bungeishunjū). The clan's later prominence in the central court suggests their integration into the Yamato polity. By the mid-7th century, members of the Kamitsukeno Clan held positions as provincial governors, military leaders, and diplomats. The clan's influence waned in the Heian period, with members becoming lower-ranking court officials and regional administrators.{{Kotobank|Kamitsukeno Clan|Encyclopedia Nipponica|ja}} == Notable Figures == Notable descendants of {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命}} include: * {{ill|Hikosashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島王}} - Appointed governor of 15 eastern provinces. * {{ill|Mimorowake no Mikoto|ja|御諸別命}} - Military leader who fought the Emishi. * {{ill|Aratawake|ja|荒田別}} - Diplomat to Korea. * {{ill|Takihase|ja|竹葉瀬}} - Contributed to Korean diplomacy. * {{ill|Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko|ja|上毛野稚子}} - General in the Baekje campaigns. == Related Clans == The Kamitsukeno Clan's descendants include several related families, categorized as the "Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces." {{Ancient Japanese Clans | Clan Name = Kamitsukeno Clan | Image = [[File:Akagi-jinja (Miyosawa) torii.JPG|280px]]
Shrine associated with the clan: [[Akagi Shrine]] ({{ill|Gunma Prefecture|ja|群馬県}}, {{ill|Maebashi|ja|前橋市}}) | Title = Kamitsukeno no Kimi (公)
Later Kamitsukeno no Asomi | Founder = '''Claimed''': {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命}}
({{ill|Emperor Sujin|ja|崇神天皇}}'s son) | Lineage = Imperial | Origin = Kamitsukeno Province (modern-day {{ill|Gunma Prefecture|ja|群馬県}})
Later relocated to Yamashiro Province | Notable Members = See [[Kamitsukeno Clan#Notable Figures|Notable Figures Section]] | Descendants = See [[Kamitsukeno Clan#Related Clans|Related Clans Section]] }} The '''Kamitsukeno Clan''' (上毛野氏, also read as ''Kamitsukenu'')While the reading ''Kamitsukenu'' has been used since the Edo period, some scholars argue this is a misreading. See [[Kenō#Origin and Pronunciation]]. was a [[Japanese clan]] that took its name from the region of Kamitsukeno. Members of the clan often served as [[kuni no miyatsuko]] (provincial governors). The clan claimed descent from {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命}}, a son of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|ja|崇神天皇}}, and was categorized as an imperial lineage (皇別). Over time, the clan adopted the titles "Kamitsukeno no Kimi (公)" and later "Kamitsukeno no Asomi (朝臣)." The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records the clan's lineage and traditions, which are also shared with other related clans. This article provides an overview of the Kamitsukeno Clan and its related clans. == Overview == The Kamitsukeno Clan was based in the ancient Kamitsukeno region (modern {{ill|Gunma Prefecture|ja|群馬県}}), as indicated by its name. The term ''Kenō'' (毛野) referred to the areas of modern-day Gunma and Tochigi Prefectures in ancient times.{{Kotobank|毛野|MyPedia|ja}} The region was later divided into {{ill|Kōzuke Province|ja|上野国}} (Gunma) and {{ill|Shimotsuke Province|ja|下野国}} (Tochigi). Gunma Prefecture, in particular, is home to many [[kofun]] (ancient burial mounds), indicating the region's significance in early Japan (see [[Kenō]]). The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records that the clan originated from {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命}}, who was dispatched to govern the eastern provinces under imperial command. The text also describes the Kamitsukeno Clan's military and diplomatic activities, particularly concerning interactions with the [[Emishi]] and [[Korea]]. However, whether the clan was a local ruling family or one dispatched from the central court remains unclear.Hirofumi Yamamoto, "History of Gunma You Don't Know" (Yōsensha). Archaeological evidence and later texts support the clan's involvement in regional governance and foreign relations.Toru Wakasa, "Regional Administration in the Ancient Kofun Period" (Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2021). By the late 7th century, the Kamitsukeno Clan became one of the "Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces" (東国六腹朝臣), which included the {{ill|Shimotsukeno Clan|ja|下毛野氏}}, Ōno Clan, Ikeda Clan, Sami Clan, and Kuramochi Clan. These clans played active roles as mid-level aristocrats in the imperial court.{{Kotobank|Kamitsukeno Clan|ja}} == Genealogy == The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records that {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命}}, a son of Emperor Sujin, was dispatched to govern the eastern provinces. It also states that he was the ancestor of the {{ill|Kamitsukeno no Kimi|ja|上毛野君}} and {{ill|Shimotsukeno no Kimi|ja|下毛野君}}.''Nihon Shoki,'' Emperor Sujin, 48th Year. The {{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記}} contains similar records.''Kojiki,'' Emperor Sujin. The {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|ja|新撰姓氏録}} states that the Kamitsukeno Asomi (Upper Capital Courtier) lineage was descended from Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto.''Shinsen Shōjiroku,'' Kamitsukeno Asomi, Imperial Lineage (Right Capital). Furthermore, the {{ill|Kokuzō Hongi|ja|国造本紀}} mentions that Toyoki Iribiko's grandson, {{ill|Hikosashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島王}}, was appointed as the first {{ill|kuni no miyatsuko|ja|国造}} of the Kamitsukeno region after pacifying twelve eastern provinces.''Kokuzō Hongi,'' Kamitsukeno Kuni no Miyatsuko. == Historical Overview == The Kamitsukeno Clan's transition from regional power to court aristocracy is evident in both textual and archaeological records. During the early Kofun period, the region saw the construction of large burial mounds, such as the {{ill|Ōtatenjin'yama Kofun|ja|太田天神山古墳}}, indicating a powerful local authority.Taichirō Shiraishi, "Kofun and the Yamato Court" (Bungeishunjū). The clan's later prominence in the central court suggests their integration into the Yamato polity. By the mid-7th century, members of the Kamitsukeno Clan held positions as provincial governors, military leaders, and diplomats. The clan's influence waned in the Heian period, with members becoming lower-ranking court officials and regional administrators.{{Kotobank|Kamitsukeno Clan|Encyclopedia Nipponica|ja}} == Notable Figures == Notable descendants of {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命}} include: * {{ill|Hikosashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島王}} - Appointed governor of 15 eastern provinces. * {{ill|Mimorowake no Mikoto|ja|御諸別命}} - Military leader who fought the Emishi. * {{ill|Aratawake|ja|荒田別}} - Diplomat to Korea. * {{ill|Takihase|ja|竹葉瀬}} - Contributed to Korean diplomacy. * {{ill|Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko|ja|上毛野稚子}} - General in the Baekje campaigns. == Related Clans == The Kamitsukeno Clan's descendants include several related families, categorized as the "Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces." These clans shared genealogical and geographical ties with the Kamitsukeno lineage. == See Also == * {{ill|Kenō|ja|毛野}} * {{ill|Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces|ja|東国六腹朝臣}} ** {{ill|Shimotsukeno Clan|ja|下毛野氏}} * {{ill|Kamitsuke no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|上毛野国造}} * {{ill|Akagi Shrine|ja|赤城神社}} [[Category:original pages]][[Category:Kamitsukeno Clan]] [[Category:original pages]][[Category:Clans]] [[Category:original pages]][[Category:Japanese clans]] [[Category:original pages]][[Category:Clans of Kantō region]] [[Category:original pages]][[Category:History of Gunma Prefecture]] [[Category:bump]] [[Category:ファイル]] [[Category:dardar]] [[ja:上毛野氏]]

It also states that he was the ancestor of the {{ill|Kamitsukeno no Kimi|ja|上毛野君}} and {{ill|Shimotsukeno no Kimi|ja|下毛野君}}.''Nihon Shoki,'' Emperor Sujin, 48th Year. The {{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記}} contains similar records.''Kojiki,'' Emperor Sujin. The {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|ja|新撰姓氏録}} states that the Kamitsukeno Asomi (Upper Capital Courtier) lineage was descended from Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto.''Shinsen Shōjiroku,'' Kamitsukeno Asomi, Imperial Lineage (Right Capital). Furthermore, the {{ill|Kokuzō Hongi|ja|国造本紀}} mentions that Toyoki Iribiko's grandson, {{ill|Hikosashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島王}}, was appointed as the first {{ill|kuni no miyatsuko|ja|国造}} of the Kamitsukeno region after pacifying twelve eastern provinces.''Kokuzō Hongi,'' Kamitsukeno Kuni no Miyatsuko. == Historical Overview == The Kamitsukeno Clan's transition from regional power to court aristocracy is evident in both textual and archaeological records. During the early Kofun period, the region saw the construction of large burial mounds, such as the {{ill|Ōtatenjin'yama Kofun|ja|太田天神山古墳}}, indicating a powerful local authority.Taichirō Shiraishi, "Kofun and the Yamato Court" (Bungeishunjū). The clan's later prominence in the central court suggests their integration into the Yamato polity. By the mid-7th century, members of the Kamitsukeno Clan held positions as provincial governors, military leaders, and diplomats. The clan's influence waned in the Heian period, with members becoming lower-ranking court officials and regional administrators.{{Kotobank|Kamitsukeno Clan|Encyclopedia Nipponica|ja}} == Notable Figures == Notable descendants of {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命}} include: * {{ill|Hikosashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島王}} - Appointed governor of 15 eastern provinces. * {{ill|Mimorowake no Mikoto|ja|御諸別命}} - Military leader who fought the Emishi. * {{ill|Aratawake|ja|荒田別}} - Diplomat to Korea. * {{ill|Takihase|ja|竹葉瀬}} - Contributed to Korean diplomacy. * {{ill|Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko|ja|上毛野稚子}} - General in the Baekje campaigns. == Related Clans == The Kamitsukeno Clan's descendants include several related families, categorized as the "Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces." The clan claimed descent from {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命}}, a son of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|ja|崇神天皇}}, and was categorized as an imperial lineage (皇別). Over time, the clan adopted the titles "Kamitsukeno no Kimi (公)" and later "Kamitsukeno no Asomi (朝臣)." The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records the clan's lineage and traditions, which are also shared with other related clans. This article provides an overview of the Kamitsukeno Clan and its related clans. == Overview == The Kamitsukeno Clan was based in the ancient Kamitsukeno region (modern {{ill|Gunma Prefecture|ja|群馬県}}), as indicated by its name. The term ''Kenō'' (毛野) referred to the areas of modern-day Gunma and Tochigi Prefectures in ancient times.{{Kotobank|毛野|MyPedia|ja}} The region was later divided into {{ill|Kōzuke Province|ja|上野国}} (Gunma) and {{ill|Shimotsuke Province|ja|下野国}} (Tochigi). Gunma Prefecture, in particular, is home to many [[kofun]] (ancient burial mounds), indicating the region's significance in early Japan (see [[Kenō]]). The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records that the clan originated from {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命}}, who was dispatched to govern the eastern provinces under imperial command. The text also describes the Kamitsukeno Clan's military and diplomatic activities, particularly concerning interactions with the [[Emishi]] and [[Korea]]. However, whether the clan was a local ruling family or one dispatched from the central court remains unclear.Hirofumi Yamamoto, "History of Gunma You Don't Know" (Yōsensha). Archaeological evidence and later texts support the clan's involvement in regional governance and foreign relations.Toru Wakasa, "Regional Administration in the Ancient Kofun Period" (Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2021). By the late 7th century, the Kamitsukeno Clan became one of the "Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces" (東国六腹朝臣), which included the {{ill|Shimotsukeno Clan|ja|下毛野氏}}, Ōno Clan, Ikeda Clan, Sami Clan, and Kuramochi Clan. These clans played active roles as mid-level aristocrats in the imperial court.{{Kotobank|Kamitsukeno Clan|ja}} == Genealogy == The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records that {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命}}, a son of Emperor Sujin, was dispatched to govern the eastern provinces. It also states that he was the ancestor of the {{ill|Kamitsukeno no Kimi|ja|上毛野君}} and {{ill|Shimotsukeno no Kimi|ja|下毛野君}}.''Nihon Shoki,'' Emperor Sujin, 48th Year. The {{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記}} contains similar records.''Kojiki,'' Emperor Sujin. The {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|ja|新撰姓氏録}} states that the Kamitsukeno Asomi (Upper Capital Courtier) lineage was descended from Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto.''Shinsen Shōjiroku,'' Kamitsukeno Asomi, Imperial Lineage (Right Capital). Furthermore, the {{ill|Kokuzō Hongi|ja|国造本紀}} mentions that Toyoki Iribiko's grandson, {{ill|Hikosashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島王}}, was appointed as the first {{ill|kuni no miyatsuko|ja|国造}} of the Kamitsukeno region after pacifying twelve eastern provinces.''Kokuzō Hongi,'' Kamitsukeno Kuni no Miyatsuko. == Historical Overview == The Kamitsukeno Clan's transition from regional power to court aristocracy is evident in both textual and archaeological records. During the early Kofun period, the region saw the construction of large burial mounds, such as the {{ill|Ōtatenjin'yama Kofun|ja|太田天神山古墳}}, indicating a powerful local authority.Taichirō Shiraishi, "Kofun and the Yamato Court" (Bungeishunjū). The clan's later prominence in the central court suggests their integration into the Yamato polity. By the mid-7th century, members of the Kamitsukeno Clan held positions as provincial governors, military leaders, and diplomats. The clan's influence waned in the Heian period, with members becoming lower-ranking court officials and regional administrators.{{Kotobank|Kamitsukeno Clan|Encyclopedia Nipponica|ja}} == Notable Figures == Notable descendants of {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命}} include: * {{ill|Hikosashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島王}} - Appointed governor of 15 eastern provinces. * {{ill|Mimorowake no Mikoto|ja|御諸別命}} - Military leader who fought the Emishi. * {{ill|Aratawake|ja|荒田別}} - Diplomat to Korea. * {{ill|Takihase|ja|竹葉瀬}} - Contributed to Korean diplomacy. * {{ill|Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko|ja|上毛野稚子}} - General in the Baekje campaigns. == Related Clans == The Kamitsukeno Clan's descendants include several related families, categorized as the "Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces." These clans shared genealogical and geographical ties with the Kamitsukeno lineage. == See Also == * {{ill|Kenō|ja|毛野}} * {{ill|Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces|ja|東国六腹朝臣}} ** {{ill|Shimotsukeno Clan|ja|下毛野氏}} * {{ill|Kamitsuke no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|上毛野国造}} * {{ill|Akagi Shrine|ja|赤城神社}} [[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[category:unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:Kamitsukeno Clan]] [[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[category:unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:Clans]] [[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[category:unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:Japanese clans]] [[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[category:unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:Clans of Kantō region]] [[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[category:unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:History of Gunma Prefecture]] [[Category:bump]] [[Category:bump-01-18]] [[ja:上毛野氏]]

{{Ancient Japanese Clans | Clan Name = Kamitsukeno Clan | Image = [[File:Akagi-jinja (Miyosawa) torii.JPG|280px]]
Shrine associated with the clan: [[Akagi Shrine]] ({{ill|Gunma Prefecture|ja|群馬県}}, {{ill|Maebashi|ja|前橋市}}) | Title = Kamitsukeno no Kimi (公)
Later Kamitsukeno no Asomi | Founder = '''Claimed''': {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命}}
({{ill|Emperor Sujin|ja|崇神天皇}}'s son) | Lineage = Imperial | Origin = Kamitsukeno Province (modern-day {{ill|Gunma Prefecture|ja|群馬県}})
Later relocated to Yamashiro Province | Notable Members = See [[Kamitsukeno Clan#Notable Figures|Notable Figures Section]] | Descendants = See [[Kamitsukeno Clan#Related Clans|Related Clans Section]] }} The '''Kamitsukeno Clan''' (上毛野氏, also read as ''Kamitsukenu'')While the reading ''Kamitsukenu'' has been used since the Edo period, some scholars argue this is a misreading. See [[Kenō#Origin and Pronunciation]]. was a [[Japanese clan]] that took its name from the region of Kamitsukeno. Members of the clan often served as [[kuni no miyatsuko]] (provincial governors). The clan claimed descent from {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命}}, a son of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|ja|崇神天皇}}, and was categorized as an imperial lineage (皇別). Over time, the clan adopted the titles "Kamitsukeno no Kimi (公)" and later "Kamitsukeno no Asomi (朝臣)." The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records the clan's lineage and traditions, which are also shared with other related clans. This article provides an overview of the Kamitsukeno Clan and its related clans. == Overview == The Kamitsukeno Clan was based in the ancient Kamitsukeno region (modern {{ill|Gunma Prefecture|ja|群馬県}}), as indicated by its name. The term ''Kenō'' (毛野) referred to the areas of modern-day Gunma and Tochigi Prefectures in ancient times.{{Kotobank|毛野|MyPedia|ja}} The region was later divided into {{ill|Kōzuke Province|ja|上野国}} (Gunma) and {{ill|Shimotsuke Province|ja|下野国}} (Tochigi). Gunma Prefecture, in particular, is home to many [[kofun]] (ancient burial mounds), indicating the region's significance in early Japan (see [[Kenō]]). The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records that the clan originated from {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命}}, who was dispatched to govern the eastern provinces under imperial command. The text also describes the Kamitsukeno Clan's military and diplomatic activities, particularly concerning interactions with the [[Emishi]] and [[Korea]]. However, whether the clan was a local ruling family or one dispatched from the central court remains unclear.Hirofumi Yamamoto, "History of Gunma You Don't Know" (Yōsensha). Archaeological evidence and later texts support the clan's involvement in regional governance and foreign relations.Toru Wakasa, "Regional Administration in the Ancient Kofun Period" (Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2021). By the late 7th century, the Kamitsukeno Clan became one of the "Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces" (東国六腹朝臣), which included the {{ill|Shimotsukeno Clan|ja|下毛野氏}}, Ōno Clan, Ikeda Clan, Sami Clan, and Kuramochi Clan. These clans played active roles as mid-level aristocrats in the imperial court.{{Kotobank|Kamitsukeno Clan|ja}} == Genealogy == The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records that {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命}}, a son of Emperor Sujin, was dispatched to govern the eastern provinces. It also states that he was the ancestor of the {{ill|Kamitsukeno no Kimi|ja|上毛野君}} and {{ill|Shimotsukeno no Kimi|ja|下毛野君}}.''Nihon Shoki,'' Emperor Sujin, 48th Year. The {{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記}} contains similar records.''Kojiki,'' Emperor Sujin. The {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|ja|新撰姓氏録}} states that the Kamitsukeno Asomi (Upper Capital Courtier) lineage was descended from Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto.''Shinsen Shōjiroku,'' Kamitsukeno Asomi, Imperial Lineage (Right Capital). Furthermore, the {{ill|Kokuzō Hongi|ja|国造本紀}} mentions that Toyoki Iribiko's grandson, {{ill|Hikosashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島王}}, was appointed as the first {{ill|kuni no miyatsuko|ja|国造}} of the Kamitsukeno region after pacifying twelve eastern provinces.''Kokuzō Hongi,'' Kamitsukeno Kuni no Miyatsuko. == Historical Overview == The Kamitsukeno Clan's transition from regional power to court aristocracy is evident in both textual and archaeological records. During the early Kofun period, the region saw the construction of large burial mounds, such as the {{ill|Ōtatenjin'yama Kofun|ja|太田天神山古墳}}, indicating a powerful local authority.Taichirō Shiraishi, "Kofun and the Yamato Court" (Bungeishunjū). The clan's later prominence in the central court suggests their integration into the Yamato polity. By the mid-7th century, members of the Kamitsukeno Clan held positions as provincial governors, military leaders, and diplomats. The clan's influence waned in the Heian period, with members becoming lower-ranking court officials and regional administrators.{{Kotobank|Kamitsukeno Clan|Encyclopedia Nipponica|ja}} == Notable Figures == Notable descendants of {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命}} include: * {{ill|Hikosashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島王}} - Appointed governor of 15 eastern provinces. * {{ill|Mimorowake no Mikoto|ja|御諸別命}} - Military leader who fought the Emishi. * {{ill|Aratawake|ja|荒田別}} - Diplomat to Korea. * {{ill|Takihase|ja|竹葉瀬}} - Contributed to Korean diplomacy. * {{ill|Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko|ja|上毛野稚子}} - General in the Baekje campaigns. == Related Clans == The Kamitsukeno Clan's descendants include several related families, categorized as the "Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces." These clans shared genealogical and geographical ties with the Kamitsukeno lineage. == See Also == * {{ill|Kenō|ja|毛野}} * {{ill|Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces|ja|東国六腹朝臣}} ** {{ill|Shimotsukeno Clan|ja|下毛野氏}} * {{ill|Kamitsuke no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|上毛野国造}} * {{ill|Akagi Shrine|ja|赤城神社}} [[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[category:unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:Kamitsukeno Clan]] [[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[category:unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:Clans]] [[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[category:unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:Japanese clans]] [[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[category:unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:Clans of Kantō region]] [[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[category:unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:History of Gunma Prefecture]] [[Category:bump]] [[Category:bump-01-18]] [[Category:refreshing imported pages]] [[Category:second attempt at refreshing on January 27 2024]][[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:second attempt at refreshing on January 27 2024]] [[ja:上毛野氏]]

This article provides an overview of the Kamitsukeno Clan and its related clans. == Overview == The Kamitsukeno Clan was based in the ancient Kamitsukeno region (modern {{ill|Gunma Prefecture|ja|群馬県}}), as indicated by its name. The term ''Kenō'' (毛野) referred to the areas of modern-day Gunma and Tochigi Prefectures in ancient times.{{Kotobank|毛野|MyPedia|ja}} The region was later divided into {{ill|Kōzuke Province|ja|上野国}} (Gunma) and {{ill|Shimotsuke Province|ja|下野国}} (Tochigi). Gunma Prefecture, in particular, is home to many [[kofun]] (ancient burial mounds), indicating the region's significance in early Japan (see [[Kenō]]). The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records that the clan originated from {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命}}, who was dispatched to govern the eastern provinces under imperial command. The text also describes the Kamitsukeno Clan's military and diplomatic activities, particularly concerning interactions with the [[Emishi]] and [[Korea]]. However, whether the clan was a local ruling family or one dispatched from the central court remains unclear.Hirofumi Yamamoto, "History of Gunma You Don't Know" (Yōsensha). Archaeological evidence and later texts support the clan's involvement in regional governance and foreign relations.Toru Wakasa, "Regional Administration in the Ancient Kofun Period" (Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2021). By the late 7th century, the Kamitsukeno Clan became one of the "Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces" (東国六腹朝臣), which included the {{ill|Shimotsukeno Clan|ja|下毛野氏}}, Ōno Clan, Ikeda Clan, Sami Clan, and Kuramochi Clan. These clans played active roles as mid-level aristocrats in the imperial court.{{Kotobank|Kamitsukeno Clan|ja}} == Genealogy == The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records that {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命}}, a son of Emperor Sujin, was dispatched to govern the eastern provinces. It also states that he was the ancestor of the {{ill|Kamitsukeno no Kimi|ja|上毛野君}} and {{ill|Shimotsukeno no Kimi|ja|下毛野君}}.''Nihon Shoki,'' Emperor Sujin, 48th Year. The {{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記}} contains similar records.''Kojiki,'' Emperor Sujin. The {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|ja|新撰姓氏録}} states that the Kamitsukeno Asomi (Upper Capital Courtier) lineage was descended from Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto.''Shinsen Shōjiroku,'' Kamitsukeno Asomi, Imperial Lineage (Right Capital). Furthermore, the {{ill|Kokuzō Hongi|ja|国造本紀}} mentions that Toyoki Iribiko's grandson, {{ill|Hikosashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島王}}, was appointed as the first {{ill|kuni no miyatsuko|ja|国造}} of the Kamitsukeno region after pacifying twelve eastern provinces.''Kokuzō Hongi,'' Kamitsukeno Kuni no Miyatsuko. == Historical Overview == The Kamitsukeno Clan's transition from regional power to court aristocracy is evident in both textual and archaeological records. During the early Kofun period, the region saw the construction of large burial mounds, such as the {{ill|Ōtatenjin'yama Kofun|ja|太田天神山古墳}}, indicating a powerful local authority.Taichirō Shiraishi, "Kofun and the Yamato Court" (Bungeishunjū). The clan's later prominence in the central court suggests their integration into the Yamato polity. By the mid-7th century, members of the Kamitsukeno Clan held positions as provincial governors, military leaders, and diplomats. The clan's influence waned in the Heian period, with members becoming lower-ranking court officials and regional administrators.{{Kotobank|Kamitsukeno Clan|Encyclopedia Nipponica|ja}} == Notable Figures == Notable descendants of {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命}} include: * {{ill|Hikosashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島王}} - Appointed governor of 15 eastern provinces. * {{ill|Mimorowake no Mikoto|ja|御諸別命}} - Military leader who fought the Emishi. * {{ill|Aratawake|ja|荒田別}} - Diplomat to Korea. * {{ill|Takihase|ja|竹葉瀬}} - Contributed to Korean diplomacy. * {{ill|Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko|ja|上毛野稚子}} - General in the Baekje campaigns. == Related Clans == The Kamitsukeno Clan's descendants include several related families, categorized as the "Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces." These clans shared genealogical and geographical ties with the Kamitsukeno lineage. == See Also == * {{ill|Kenō|ja|毛野}} * {{ill|Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces|ja|東国六腹朝臣}} ** {{Ancient Japanese Clans | Clan Name = Kamitsukeno Clan | Image = [[File:Akagi-jinja (Miyosawa) torii.JPG|280px]]
Shrine associated with the clan: [[Akagi Shrine]] ({{ill|Gunma Prefecture|ja|群馬県}}, {{ill|Maebashi|ja|前橋市}}) | Title = Kamitsukeno no Kimi (公)
Later Kamitsukeno no Asomi | Founder = '''Claimed''': {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命}}
({{ill|Emperor Sujin|ja|崇神天皇}}'s son) | Lineage = Imperial | Origin = Kamitsukeno Province (modern-day {{ill|Gunma Prefecture|ja|群馬県}})
Later relocated to Yamashiro Province | Notable Members = See [[Kamitsukeno Clan#Notable Figures|Notable Figures Section]] | Descendants = See [[Kamitsukeno Clan#Related Clans|Related Clans Section]] }} The '''Kamitsukeno Clan''' (上毛野氏, also read as ''Kamitsukenu'')While the reading ''Kamitsukenu'' has been used since the Edo period, some scholars argue this is a misreading. See [[Kenō#Origin and Pronunciation]]. was a [[Japanese clan]] that took its name from the region of Kamitsukeno. Members of the clan often served as [[kuni no miyatsuko]] (provincial governors). The clan claimed descent from {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命}}, a son of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|ja|崇神天皇}}, and was categorized as an imperial lineage (皇別). Over time, the clan adopted the titles "Kamitsukeno no Kimi (公)" and later "Kamitsukeno no Asomi (朝臣)." The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records the clan's lineage and traditions, which are also shared with other related clans. This article provides an overview of the Kamitsukeno Clan and its related clans. == Overview == The Kamitsukeno Clan was based in the ancient Kamitsukeno region (modern {{ill|Gunma Prefecture|ja|群馬県}}), as indicated by its name. The term ''Kenō'' (毛野) referred to the areas of modern-day Gunma and Tochigi Prefectures in ancient times.{{Kotobank|毛野|MyPedia|ja}} The region was later divided into {{ill|Kōzuke Province|ja|上野国}} (Gunma) and {{ill|Shimotsuke Province|ja|下野国}} (Tochigi). Gunma Prefecture, in particular, is home to many [[kofun]] (ancient burial mounds), indicating the region's significance in early Japan (see [[Kenō]]). The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records that the clan originated from {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命}}, who was dispatched to govern the eastern provinces under imperial command. The text also describes the Kamitsukeno Clan's military and diplomatic activities, particularly concerning interactions with the [[Emishi]] and [[Korea]]. However, whether the clan was a local ruling family or one dispatched from the central court remains unclear.Hirofumi Yamamoto, "History of Gunma You Don't Know" (Yōsensha). Archaeological evidence and later texts support the clan's involvement in regional governance and foreign relations.Toru Wakasa, "Regional Administration in the Ancient Kofun Period" (Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2021). By the late 7th century, the Kamitsukeno Clan became one of the "Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces" (東国六腹朝臣), which included the {{ill|Shimotsukeno Clan|ja|下毛野氏}}, Ōno Clan, Ikeda Clan, Sami Clan, and Kuramochi Clan. These clans played active roles as mid-level aristocrats in the imperial court.{{Kotobank|Kamitsukeno Clan|ja}} == Genealogy == The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records that {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命}}, a son of Emperor Sujin, was dispatched to govern the eastern provinces. It also states that he was the ancestor of the {{ill|Kamitsukeno no Kimi|ja|上毛野君}} and {{ill|Shimotsukeno no Kimi|ja|下毛野君}}.''Nihon Shoki,'' Emperor Sujin, 48th Year. The {{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記}} contains similar records.''Kojiki,'' Emperor Sujin. The {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|ja|新撰姓氏録}} states that the Kamitsukeno Asomi (Upper Capital Courtier) lineage was descended from Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto.''Shinsen Shōjiroku,'' Kamitsukeno Asomi, Imperial Lineage (Right Capital). Furthermore, the {{ill|Kokuzō Hongi|ja|国造本紀}} mentions that Toyoki Iribiko's grandson, {{ill|Hikosashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島王}}, was appointed as the first {{ill|kuni no miyatsuko|ja|国造}} of the Kamitsukeno region after pacifying twelve eastern provinces.''Kokuzō Hongi,'' Kamitsukeno Kuni no Miyatsuko. == Historical Overview == The Kamitsukeno Clan's transition from regional power to court aristocracy is evident in both textual and archaeological records. During the early Kofun period, the region saw the construction of large burial mounds, such as the {{ill|Ōtatenjin'yama Kofun|ja|太田天神山古墳}}, indicating a powerful local authority.Taichirō Shiraishi, "Kofun and the Yamato Court" (Bungeishunjū). The clan's later prominence in the central court suggests their integration into the Yamato polity. By the mid-7th century, members of the Kamitsukeno Clan held positions as provincial governors, military leaders, and diplomats. The clan's influence waned in the Heian period, with members becoming lower-ranking court officials and regional administrators.{{Kotobank|Kamitsukeno Clan|Encyclopedia Nipponica|ja}} == Notable Figures == Notable descendants of {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命}} include: * {{ill|Hikosashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島王}} - Appointed governor of 15 eastern provinces. * {{ill|Mimorowake no Mikoto|ja|御諸別命}} - Military leader who fought the Emishi. * {{ill|Aratawake|ja|荒田別}} - Diplomat to Korea. * {{ill|Takihase|ja|竹葉瀬}} - Contributed to Korean diplomacy. * {{ill|Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko|ja|上毛野稚子}} - General in the Baekje campaigns. == Related Clans == The Kamitsukeno Clan's descendants include several related families, categorized as the "Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces." These clans shared genealogical and geographical ties with the Kamitsukeno lineage. == See Also == * {{ill|Kenō|ja|毛野}} * {{ill|Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces|ja|東国六腹朝臣}} ** {{ill|Shimotsukeno Clan|ja|下毛野氏}} * {{ill|Kamitsuke no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|上毛野国造}} * {{ill|Akagi Shrine|ja|赤城神社}} [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:Kamitsukeno Clan]] [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:Clans]] [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:Japanese clans]] [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:Clans of Kantō region]] [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:History of Gunma Prefecture]] [[Category:bump]] [[Category:bump-01-18]] [[Category:refreshing imported pages]] [[Category:second attempt at refreshing on January 27 2024]][[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:second attempt at refreshing on January 27 2024]] [[Category:properly attributed pages]][[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:properly attributed pages]] [[Category:refreshing so the massreplace can be done again]] [[Category:kk]] [[Category:fixing the kk issue]] [[ja:上毛野氏]]

Later relocated to Yamashiro Province | Notable Members = See [[Kamitsukeno Clan#Notable Figures|Notable Figures Section]] | Descendants = See [[Kamitsukeno Clan#Related Clans|Related Clans Section]] }} The '''Kamitsukeno Clan''' (上毛野氏, also read as ''Kamitsukenu'')While the reading ''Kamitsukenu'' has been used since the Edo period, some scholars argue this is a misreading. See [[Kenō#Origin and Pronunciation]]. was a [[Japanese clan]] that took its name from the region of Kamitsukeno. Members of the clan often served as [[kuni no miyatsuko]] (provincial governors). The clan claimed descent from {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命}}, a son of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|ja|崇神天皇}}, and was categorized as an imperial lineage (皇別). Over time, the clan adopted the titles "Kamitsukeno no Kimi (公)" and later "Kamitsukeno no Asomi (朝臣)." The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records the clan's lineage and traditions, which are also shared with other related clans. This article provides an overview of the Kamitsukeno Clan and its related clans. == Overview == The Kamitsukeno Clan was based in the ancient Kamitsukeno region (modern {{ill|Gunma Prefecture|ja|群馬県}}), as indicated by its name. The term ''Kenō'' (毛野) referred to the areas of modern-day Gunma and Tochigi Prefectures in ancient times.{{Kotobank|毛野|MyPedia|ja}} The region was later divided into {{ill|Kōzuke Province|ja|上野国}} (Gunma) and {{ill|Shimotsuke Province|ja|下野国}} (Tochigi). Gunma Prefecture, in particular, is home to many [[kofun]] (ancient burial mounds), indicating the region's significance in early Japan (see [[Kenō]]). The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records that the clan originated from {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命}}, who was dispatched to govern the eastern provinces under imperial command. The text also describes the Kamitsukeno Clan's military and diplomatic activities, particularly concerning interactions with the [[Emishi]] and [[Korea]]. However, whether the clan was a local ruling family or one dispatched from the central court remains unclear.Hirofumi Yamamoto, "History of Gunma You Don't Know" (Yōsensha). Archaeological evidence and later texts support the clan's involvement in regional governance and foreign relations.Toru Wakasa, "Regional Administration in the Ancient Kofun Period" (Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2021). By the late 7th century, the Kamitsukeno Clan became one of the "Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces" (東国六腹朝臣), which included the {{ill|Shimotsukeno Clan|ja|下毛野氏}}, Ōno Clan, Ikeda Clan, Sami Clan, and Kuramochi Clan. These clans played active roles as mid-level aristocrats in the imperial court.{{Kotobank|Kamitsukeno Clan|ja}} == Genealogy == The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records that {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命}}, a son of Emperor Sujin, was dispatched to govern the eastern provinces. It also states that he was the ancestor of the {{ill|Kamitsukeno no Kimi|ja|上毛野君}} and {{ill|Shimotsukeno no Kimi|ja|下毛野君}}.''Nihon Shoki,'' Emperor Sujin, 48th Year. The {{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記}} contains similar records.''Kojiki,'' Emperor Sujin. The {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|ja|新撰姓氏録}} states that the Kamitsukeno Asomi (Upper Capital Courtier) lineage was descended from Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto.''Shinsen Shōjiroku,'' Kamitsukeno Asomi, Imperial Lineage (Right Capital). Furthermore, the {{ill|Kokuzō Hongi|ja|国造本紀}} mentions that Toyoki Iribiko's grandson, {{ill|Hikosashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島王}}, was appointed as the first {{ill|kuni no miyatsuko|ja|国造}} of the Kamitsukeno region after pacifying twelve eastern provinces.''Kokuzō Hongi,'' Kamitsukeno Kuni no Miyatsuko. == Historical Overview == The Kamitsukeno Clan's transition from regional power to court aristocracy is evident in both textual and archaeological records. During the early Kofun period, the region saw the construction of large burial mounds, such as the {{ill|Ōtatenjin'yama Kofun|ja|太田天神山古墳}}, indicating a powerful local authority.Taichirō Shiraishi, "Kofun and the Yamato Court" (Bungeishunjū). The clan's later prominence in the central court suggests their integration into the Yamato polity. By the mid-7th century, members of the Kamitsukeno Clan held positions as provincial governors, military leaders, and diplomats. The clan's influence waned in the Heian period, with members becoming lower-ranking court officials and regional administrators.{{Kotobank|Kamitsukeno Clan|Encyclopedia Nipponica|ja}} == Notable Figures == Notable descendants of {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命}} include: * {{ill|Hikosashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島王}} - Appointed governor of 15 eastern provinces. * {{ill|Mimorowake no Mikoto|ja|御諸別命}} - Military leader who fought the Emishi. * {{ill|Aratawake|ja|荒田別}} - Diplomat to Korea. * {{ill|Takihase|ja|竹葉瀬}} - Contributed to Korean diplomacy. * {{ill|Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko|ja|上毛野稚子}} - General in the Baekje campaigns. == Related Clans == The Kamitsukeno Clan's descendants include several related families, categorized as the "Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces." These clans shared genealogical and geographical ties with the Kamitsukeno lineage. == See Also == * {{ill|Kenō|ja|毛野}} * {{ill|Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces|ja|東国六腹朝臣}} ** {{ill|Shimotsukeno Clan|ja|下毛野氏}} * {{ill|Kamitsuke no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|上毛野国造}} * {{ill|Akagi Shrine|ja|赤城神社}} [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-Kamitsukeno clan-qq]] [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:Kamitsukeno Clan]] [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-Kamitsukeno clan-qq]] [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:Clans]] [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-Kamitsukeno clan-qq]] [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:Japanese clans]] [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-Kamitsukeno clan-qq]] [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:Clans of Kantō region]] [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-Kamitsukeno clan-qq]] [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:History of Gunma Prefecture]] [[Category:bump]] [[Category:bump-01-18]] [[Category:refreshing imported pages]] [[Category:second attempt at refreshing on January 27 2024]][[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:second attempt at refreshing on January 27 2024]] [[Category:properly attributed pages]][[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:properly attributed pages]] [[Category:refreshing so the massreplace can be done again]] [[Category:kk]] [[Category:fixing the kk issue]] [[ja:上毛野氏]]

Later relocated to Yamashiro Province | Notable Members = See [[Kamitsukeno Clan#Notable Figures|Notable Figures Section]] | Descendants = See [[Kamitsukeno Clan#Related Clans|Related Clans Section]] }} The '''Kamitsukeno Clan''' (上毛野氏, also read as ''Kamitsukenu'')While the reading ''Kamitsukenu'' has been used since the Edo period, some scholars argue this is a misreading. See [[Kenō#Origin and Pronunciation]]. was a [[Japanese clan]] that took its name from the region of Kamitsukeno. Members of the clan often served as [[kuni no miyatsuko]] (provincial governors). The clan claimed descent from {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命}}, a son of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|ja|崇神天皇}}, and was categorized as an imperial lineage (皇別). Over time, the clan adopted the titles "Kamitsukeno no Kimi (公)" and later "Kamitsukeno no Asomi (朝臣)." The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records the clan's lineage and traditions, which are also shared with other related clans. This article provides an overview of the Kamitsukeno Clan and its related clans. == Overview == The Kamitsukeno Clan was based in the ancient Kamitsukeno region (modern {{ill|Gunma Prefecture|ja|群馬県}}), as indicated by its name. The term ''Kenō'' (毛野) referred to the areas of modern-day Gunma and Tochigi Prefectures in ancient times.{{Kotobank|毛野|MyPedia|ja}} The region was later divided into {{ill|Kōzuke Province|ja|上野国}} (Gunma) and {{ill|Shimotsuke Province|ja|下野国}} (Tochigi). Gunma Prefecture, in particular, is home to many [[kofun]] (ancient burial mounds), indicating the region's significance in early Japan (see [[Kenō]]). The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records that the clan originated from {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命}}, who was dispatched to govern the eastern provinces under imperial command. The text also describes the Kamitsukeno Clan's military and diplomatic activities, particularly concerning interactions with the [[Emishi]] and [[Korea]]. However, whether the clan was a local ruling family or one dispatched from the central court remains unclear.Hirofumi Yamamoto, "History of Gunma You Don't Know" (Yōsensha). Archaeological evidence and later texts support the clan's involvement in regional governance and foreign relations.Toru Wakasa, "Regional Administration in the Ancient Kofun Period" (Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2021). By the late 7th century, the Kamitsukeno Clan became one of the "Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces" (東国六腹朝臣), which included the {{ill|Shimotsukeno Clan|ja|下毛野氏}}, Ōno Clan, Ikeda Clan, Sami Clan, and Kuramochi Clan. These clans played active roles as mid-level aristocrats in the imperial court.{{Kotobank|Kamitsukeno Clan|ja}} == Genealogy == The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records that {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命}}, a son of Emperor Sujin, was dispatched to govern the eastern provinces. It also states that he was the ancestor of the {{ill|Kamitsukeno no Kimi|ja|上毛野君}} and {{ill|Shimotsukeno no Kimi|ja|下毛野君}}.''Nihon Shoki,'' Emperor Sujin, 48th Year. The {{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記}} contains similar records.''Kojiki,'' Emperor Sujin. The {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|ja|新撰姓氏録}} states that the Kamitsukeno Asomi (Upper Capital Courtier) lineage was descended from Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto.''Shinsen Shōjiroku,'' Kamitsukeno Asomi, Imperial Lineage (Right Capital). Furthermore, the {{ill|Kokuzō Hongi|ja|国造本紀}} mentions that Toyoki Iribiko's grandson, {{ill|Hikosashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島王}}, was appointed as the first {{ill|kuni no miyatsuko|ja|国造}} of the Kamitsukeno region after pacifying twelve eastern provinces.''Kokuzō Hongi,'' Kamitsukeno Kuni no Miyatsuko. == Historical Overview == The Kamitsukeno Clan's transition from regional power to court aristocracy is evident in both textual and archaeological records. During the early Kofun period, the region saw the construction of large burial mounds, such as the {{ill|Ōtatenjin'yama Kofun|ja|太田天神山古墳}}, indicating a powerful local authority.Taichirō Shiraishi, "Kofun and the Yamato Court" (Bungeishunjū). The clan's later prominence in the central court suggests their integration into the Yamato polity. By the mid-7th century, members of the Kamitsukeno Clan held positions as provincial governors, military leaders, and diplomats. The clan's influence waned in the Heian period, with members becoming lower-ranking court officials and regional administrators.{{Kotobank|Kamitsukeno Clan|Encyclopedia Nipponica|ja}} == Notable Figures == Notable descendants of {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命}} include: * {{ill|Hikosashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島王}} - Appointed governor of 15 eastern provinces. * {{ill|Mimorowake no Mikoto|ja|御諸別命}} - Military leader who fought the Emishi. * {{ill|Aratawake|ja|荒田別}} - Diplomat to Korea. * {{ill|Takihase|ja|竹葉瀬}} - Contributed to Korean diplomacy. * {{ill|Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko|ja|上毛野稚子}} - General in the Baekje campaigns. == Related Clans == The Kamitsukeno Clan's descendants include several related families, categorized as the "Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces." These clans shared genealogical and geographical ties with the Kamitsukeno lineage. == See Also == * {{ill|Kenō|ja|毛野}} * {{ill|Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces|ja|東国六腹朝臣}} ** {{ill|Shimotsukeno Clan|ja|下毛野氏}} * {{ill|Kamitsuke no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|上毛野国造}} * {{ill|Akagi Shrine|ja|赤城神社}} [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-Kamitsukeno clan-qq]] [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:Kamitsukeno Clan]] [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-Kamitsukeno clan-qq]] [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:Clans]] [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-Kamitsukeno clan-qq]] [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:Japanese clans]] [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-Kamitsukeno clan-qq]] [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:Clans of Kantō region]] [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-Kamitsukeno clan-qq]] [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:History of Gunma Prefecture]] [[Category:bump]] [[Category:bump-01-18]] [[Category:refreshing imported pages]] [[Category:second attempt at refreshing on January 27 2024]][[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:second attempt at refreshing on January 27 2024]] [[Category:properly attributed pages]][[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:properly attributed pages]] [[Category:refreshing so the massreplace can be done again]] [[Category:kk]] [[Category:fixing the kk issue]] [[Category:SuQqqqqq]] [[Category:qqqq]] [[sn:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:qq]][[sn:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:qq]][[sn:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:qq]] [[ja:上毛野氏]] [[Category:New pages]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:Removing this excess]]

{{Ancient Japanese Clans | Clan Name = Kamitsukeno Clan | image = [[File:Akagi-jinja (Miyosawa) torii.JPG|280px]]
Shrine associated with the clan: [[Akagi Shrine]] ({{ill|Gunma Prefecture|ja|群馬県}}, {{ill|Maebashi|ja|前橋市}}) | Title = Kamitsukeno no Kimi (公)
Later Kamitsukeno no Asomi | Founder = '''Claimed''': {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命}}
({{ill|Emperor Sujin|ja|崇神天皇}}'s son) | Lineage = Imperial | Origin = Kamitsukeno Province (modern-day {{ill|Gunma Prefecture|ja|群馬県}})
Later relocated to Yamashiro Province | Notable Members = See [[Kamitsukeno Clan#Notable Figures|Notable Figures Section]] | Descendants = See [[Kamitsukeno Clan#Related Clans|Related Clans Section]] }} The '''Kamitsukeno Clan''' (上毛野氏, also read as ''Kamitsukenu'')While the reading ''Kamitsukenu'' has been used since the Edo period, some scholars argue this is a misreading. See [[Kenō#Origin and Pronunciation]]. was a [[Japanese clan]] that took its name from the region of Kamitsukeno. Members of the clan often served as [[kuni no miyatsuko]] (provincial governors). The clan claimed descent from {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命}}, a son of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|ja|崇神天皇}}, and was categorized as an imperial lineage (皇別). Over time, the clan adopted the titles "Kamitsukeno no Kimi (公)" and later "Kamitsukeno no Asomi (朝臣)." The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records the clan's lineage and traditions, which are also shared with other related clans. This article provides an overview of the Kamitsukeno Clan and its related clans. == Overview == The Kamitsukeno Clan was based in the ancient Kamitsukeno region (modern {{ill|Gunma Prefecture|ja|群馬県}}), as indicated by its name. The term ''Kenō'' (毛野) referred to the areas of modern-day Gunma and Tochigi Prefectures in ancient times.{{Kotobank|毛野|MyPedia|ja}} The region was later divided into {{ill|Kōzuke Province|ja|上野国}} (Gunma) and {{ill|Shimotsuke Province|ja|下野国}} (Tochigi). Gunma Prefecture, in particular, is home to many [[kofun]] (ancient burial mounds), indicating the region's significance in early Japan (see [[Kenō]]). The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records that the clan originated from {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命}}, who was dispatched to govern the eastern provinces under imperial command. The text also describes the Kamitsukeno Clan's military and diplomatic activities, particularly concerning interactions with the [[Emishi]] and [[Korea]]. However, whether the clan was a local ruling family or one dispatched from the central court remains unclear.Hirofumi Yamamoto, "History of Gunma You Don't Know" (Yōsensha). Archaeological evidence and later texts support the clan's involvement in regional governance and foreign relations.Toru Wakasa, "Regional Administration in the Ancient Kofun Period" (Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2021). By the late 7th century, the Kamitsukeno Clan became one of the "Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces" (東国六腹朝臣), which included the {{ill|Shimotsukeno Clan|ja|下毛野氏}}, Ōno Clan, Ikeda Clan, Sami Clan, and Kuramochi Clan. These clans played active roles as mid-level aristocrats in the imperial court.{{Kotobank|Kamitsukeno Clan|ja}} == Genealogy == The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records that {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命}}, a son of Emperor Sujin, was dispatched to govern the eastern provinces. It also states that he was the ancestor of the {{ill|Kamitsukeno no Kimi|ja|上毛野君}} and {{ill|Shimotsukeno no Kimi|ja|下毛野君}}.''Nihon Shoki,'' Emperor Sujin, 48th Year. The {{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記}} contains similar records.''Kojiki,'' Emperor Sujin. The {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|ja|新撰姓氏録}} states that the Kamitsukeno Asomi (Upper Capital Courtier) lineage was descended from Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto.''Shinsen Shōjiroku,'' Kamitsukeno Asomi, Imperial Lineage (Right Capital). Furthermore, the {{ill|Kokuzō Hongi|ja|国造本紀}} mentions that Toyoki Iribiko's grandson, {{ill|Hikosashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島王}}, was appointed as the first {{ill|kuni no miyatsuko|ja|国造}} of the Kamitsukeno region after pacifying twelve eastern provinces.''Kokuzō Hongi,'' Kamitsukeno Kuni no Miyatsuko. == Historical Overview == The Kamitsukeno Clan's transition from regional power to court aristocracy is evident in both textual and archaeological records. During the early Kofun period, the region saw the construction of large burial mounds, such as the {{ill|Ōtatenjin'yama Kofun|ja|太田天神山古墳}}, indicating a powerful local authority.Taichirō Shiraishi, "Kofun and the Yamato Court" (Bungeishunjū). The clan's later prominence in the central court suggests their integration into the Yamato polity. By the mid-7th century, members of the Kamitsukeno Clan held positions as provincial governors, military leaders, and diplomats. The clan's influence waned in the Heian period, with members becoming lower-ranking court officials and regional administrators.{{Kotobank|Kamitsukeno Clan|Encyclopedia Nipponica|ja}} == Notable Figures == Notable descendants of {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命}} include: * {{ill|Hikosashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島王}} - Appointed governor of 15 eastern provinces. * {{ill|Mimorowake no Mikoto|ja|御諸別命}} - Military leader who fought the Emishi. * {{ill|Aratawake|ja|荒田別}} - Diplomat to Korea. * {{ill|Takihase|ja|竹葉瀬}} - Contributed to Korean diplomacy. * {{ill|Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko|ja|上毛野稚子}} - General in the Baekje campaigns. == Related Clans == The Kamitsukeno Clan's descendants include several related families, categorized as the "Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces." These clans shared genealogical and geographical ties with the Kamitsukeno lineage. == See Also == * {{ill|Kenō|ja|毛野}} * {{ill|Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces|ja|東国六腹朝臣}} ** {{ill|Shimotsukeno Clan|ja|下毛野氏}} * {{ill|Kamitsuke no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|上毛野国造}} * {{ill|Akagi Shrine|ja|赤城神社}} [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] {{Ancient Japanese Clans | Clan Name = Kamitsukeno Clan | image = [[File:Akagi-jinja (Miyosawa) torii.JPG|280px]]
Shrine associated with the clan: [[Akagi Shrine]] ({{ill|Gunma Prefecture|ja|群馬県}}, {{ill|Maebashi|ja|前橋市}}) | Title = Kamitsukeno no Kimi (公)
Later Kamitsukeno no Asomi | Founder = '''Claimed''': {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto}}
({{ill|Emperor Sujin|ja|崇神天皇}}'s son) | Lineage = Imperial | Origin = Kamitsukeno Province (modern-day {{ill|Gunma Prefecture|ja|群馬県}})
Later relocated to Yamashiro Province | Notable Members = See [[Kamitsukeno Clan#Notable Figures|Notable Figures Section]] | Descendants = See [[Kamitsukeno Clan#Related Clans|Related Clans Section]] }} The '''Kamitsukeno Clan''' (上毛野氏, also read as ''Kamitsukenu'')While the reading ''Kamitsukenu'' has been used since the Edo period, some scholars argue this is a misreading. See [[Kenō#Origin and Pronunciation]]. was a [[Japanese clan]] that took its name from the region of Kamitsukeno. Members of the clan often served as [[kuni no miyatsuko]] (provincial governors). The clan claimed descent from {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto}}, a son of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|ja|崇神天皇}}, and was categorized as an imperial lineage (皇別). Over time, the clan adopted the titles "Kamitsukeno no Kimi (公)" and later "Kamitsukeno no Asomi (朝臣)." The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records the clan's lineage and traditions, which are also shared with other related clans. This article provides an overview of the Kamitsukeno Clan and its related clans. == Overview == The Kamitsukeno Clan was based in the ancient Kamitsukeno region (modern {{ill|Gunma Prefecture|ja|群馬県}}), as indicated by its name. The term ''Kenō'' (毛野) referred to the areas of modern-day Gunma and Tochigi Prefectures in ancient times.{{Kotobank|毛野|MyPedia|ja}} The region was later divided into {{ill|Kōzuke Province|ja|上野国}} (Gunma) and {{ill|Shimotsuke Province|ja|下野国}} (Tochigi). Gunma Prefecture, in particular, is home to many [[kofun]] (ancient burial mounds), indicating the region's significance in early Japan (see [[Kenō]]). The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records that the clan originated from {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto}}, who was dispatched to govern the eastern provinces under imperial command. The text also describes the Kamitsukeno Clan's military and diplomatic activities, particularly concerning interactions with the [[Emishi]] and [[Korea]]. However, whether the clan was a local ruling family or one dispatched from the central court remains unclear.Hirofumi Yamamoto, "History of Gunma You Don't Know" (Yōsensha). Archaeological evidence and later texts support the clan's involvement in regional governance and foreign relations.Toru Wakasa, "Regional Administration in the Ancient Kofun Period" (Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2021). By the late 7th century, the Kamitsukeno Clan became one of the "Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces" (東国六腹朝臣), which included the {{ill|Shimotsukeno Clan|ja|下毛野氏|lt=Shimotsukeno clan}}, Ōno Clan, Ikeda Clan, Sami Clan, and Kuramochi Clan. These clans played active roles as mid-level aristocrats in the imperial court.{{Kotobank|Kamitsukeno Clan|ja}} == Genealogy == The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records that {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto}}, a son of Emperor Sujin, was dispatched to govern the eastern provinces. It also states that he was the ancestor of the {{ill|Kamitsukeno no Kimi|ja|上毛野君}} and {{ill|Shimotsukeno no Kimi|ja|下毛野君}}.''Nihon Shoki,'' Emperor Sujin, 48th Year. The {{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記}} contains similar records.''Kojiki,'' Emperor Sujin. The {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|ja|新撰姓氏録}} states that the Kamitsukeno Asomi (Upper Capital Courtier) lineage was descended from Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto.''Shinsen Shōjiroku,'' Kamitsukeno Asomi, Imperial Lineage (Right Capital). Furthermore, the {{ill|Kokuzō Hongi|ja|国造本紀}} mentions that Toyoki Iribiko's grandson, {{ill|Hikosashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島王}}, was appointed as the first {{ill|kuni no miyatsuko|ja|国造}} of the Kamitsukeno region after pacifying twelve eastern provinces.''Kokuzō Hongi,'' Kamitsukeno Kuni no Miyatsuko. == Historical Overview == The Kamitsukeno Clan's transition from regional power to court aristocracy is evident in both textual and archaeological records. During the early Kofun period, the region saw the construction of large burial mounds, such as the {{ill|Ōtatenjin'yama Kofun|ja|太田天神山古墳}}, indicating a powerful local authority.Taichirō Shiraishi, "Kofun and the Yamato Court" (Bungeishunjū). The clan's later prominence in the central court suggests their integration into the Yamato polity. By the mid-7th century, members of the Kamitsukeno Clan held positions as provincial governors, military leaders, and diplomats. The clan's influence waned in the Heian period, with members becoming lower-ranking court officials and regional administrators.{{Kotobank|Kamitsukeno Clan|Encyclopedia Nipponica|ja}} == Notable Figures == Notable descendants of {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto}} include: * {{ill|Hikosashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島王}} - Appointed governor of 15 eastern provinces. * {{ill|Mimorowake no Mikoto|ja|御諸別命}} - Military leader who fought the Emishi. * {{ill|Aratawake|ja|荒田別}} - Diplomat to Korea. * {{ill|Takihase|ja|竹葉瀬}} - Contributed to Korean diplomacy. * {{ill|Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko|ja|上毛野稚子}} - General in the Baekje campaigns. == Related Clans == The Kamitsukeno Clan's descendants include several related families, categorized as the "Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces." These clans shared genealogical and geographical ties with the Kamitsukeno lineage. == See Also == * {{ill|Kenō|ja|毛野}} * {{ill|Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces|ja|東国六腹朝臣}} ** {{ill|Shimotsukeno Clan|ja|下毛野氏|lt=Shimotsukeno clan}} * {{ill|Kamitsuke no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|上毛野国造}} * {{ill|Akagi Shrine|ja|赤城神社}} [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:Unsorted completion
