{{Ancient Japanese Clans | Clan Name = Kamitsukeno Clan | image = [[File:Akagi-jinja (Miyosawa) torii.JPG|280px]]
Shrine associated with the clan: [[Akagi Shrine]] ({{ill|Gunma Prefecture|ja|群馬県}}, {{ill|Maebashi|ja|前橋市}}) | Title = Kamitsukeno no Kimi (公)
Later Kamitsukeno no Asomi | Founder = '''Claimed''': {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto}}
({{ill|Emperor Sujin|ja|崇神天皇}}'s son) | Lineage = Imperial | Origin = Kamitsukeno Province (modern-day {{ill|Gunma Prefecture|ja|群馬県}})
Later relocated to Yamashiro Province | Notable Members = See [[Kamitsukeno Clan#Notable Figures|Notable Figures Section]] | Descendants = See [[Kamitsukeno Clan#Related Clans|Related Clans Section]] }} The '''Kamitsukeno Clan''' (上毛野氏, also read as ''Kamitsukenu'')While the reading ''Kamitsukenu'' has been used since the Edo period, some scholars argue this is a misreading. See [[Kenō#Origin and Pronunciation]]. was a [[Japanese clan]] that took its name from the region of Kamitsukeno. Members of the clan often served as [[kuni no miyatsuko]] (provincial governors). The clan claimed descent from {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto}}, a son of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|ja|崇神天皇}}, and was categorized as an imperial lineage (皇別). Over time, the clan adopted the titles "Kamitsukeno no Kimi (公)" and later "Kamitsukeno no Asomi (朝臣)." The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records the clan's lineage and traditions, which are also shared with other related clans. This article provides an overview of the Kamitsukeno Clan and its related clans. == Overview == The Kamitsukeno Clan was based in the ancient Kamitsukeno region (modern {{ill|Gunma Prefecture|ja|群馬県}}), as indicated by its name. The term ''Kenō'' (毛野) referred to the areas of modern-day Gunma and Tochigi Prefectures in ancient times.{{Kotobank|毛野|MyPedia|ja}} The region was later divided into {{ill|Kōzuke Province|ja|上野国}} (Gunma) and {{ill|Shimotsuke Province|ja|下野国}} (Tochigi). Gunma Prefecture, in particular, is home to many [[kofun]] (ancient burial mounds), indicating the region's significance in early Japan (see [[Kenō]]). The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records that the clan originated from {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto}}, who was dispatched to govern the eastern provinces under imperial command. The text also describes the Kamitsukeno Clan's military and diplomatic activities, particularly concerning interactions with the [[Emishi]] and [[Korea]]. However, whether the clan was a local ruling family or one dispatched from the central court remains unclear.Hirofumi Yamamoto, "History of Gunma You Don't Know" (Yōsensha). Archaeological evidence and later texts support the clan's involvement in regional governance and foreign relations.Toru Wakasa, "Regional Administration in the Ancient Kofun Period" (Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2021). By the late 7th century, the Kamitsukeno Clan became one of the "Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces" (東国六腹朝臣), which included the {{ill|Shimotsukeno Clan|ja|下毛野氏|lt=Shimotsukeno clan}}, Ōno Clan, Ikeda Clan, Sami Clan, and Kuramochi Clan. These clans played active roles as mid-level aristocrats in the imperial court.{{Kotobank|Kamitsukeno Clan|ja}} == Genealogy == The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records that {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto}}, a son of Emperor Sujin, was dispatched to govern the eastern provinces. It also states that he was the ancestor of the {{ill|Kamitsukeno no Kimi|ja|上毛野君}} and {{ill|Shimotsukeno no Kimi|ja|下毛野君}}.''Nihon Shoki,'' Emperor Sujin, 48th Year. The {{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記}} contains similar records.''Kojiki,'' Emperor Sujin. The {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|ja|新撰姓氏録}} states that the Kamitsukeno Asomi (Upper Capital Courtier) lineage was descended from Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto.''Shinsen Shōjiroku,'' Kamitsukeno Asomi, Imperial Lineage (Right Capital). Furthermore, the {{ill|Kokuzō Hongi|ja|国造本紀}} mentions that Toyoki Iribiko's grandson, {{ill|Hikosashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島王}}, was appointed as the first {{ill|kuni no miyatsuko|ja|国造}} of the Kamitsukeno region after pacifying twelve eastern provinces.''Kokuzō Hongi,'' Kamitsukeno Kuni no Miyatsuko. == Historical Overview == The Kamitsukeno Clan's transition from regional power to court aristocracy is evident in both textual and archaeological records. During the early Kofun period, the region saw the construction of large burial mounds, such as the {{ill|Ōtatenjin'yama Kofun|ja|太田天神山古墳}}, indicating a powerful local authority.Taichirō Shiraishi, "Kofun and the Yamato Court" (Bungeishunjū). The clan's later prominence in the central court suggests their integration into the Yamato polity. By the mid-7th century, members of the Kamitsukeno Clan held positions as provincial governors, military leaders, and diplomats. The clan's influence waned in the Heian period, with members becoming lower-ranking court officials and regional administrators.{{Kotobank|Kamitsukeno Clan|Encyclopedia Nipponica|ja}} == Notable Figures == Notable descendants of {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto}} include: * {{ill|Hikosashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島王}} - Appointed governor of 15 eastern provinces. * {{ill|Mimorowake no Mikoto|ja|御諸別命}} - Military leader who fought the Emishi. * {{ill|Aratawake|ja|荒田別|1=Aratawake}} - Diplomat to Korea. * {{ill|Takihase|ja|竹葉瀬}} - Contributed to Korean diplomacy. * {{ill|Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko|ja|上毛野稚子|1=Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko}} - General in the Baekje campaigns. == Related Clans == The Kamitsukeno Clan's descendants include several related families, categorized as the "Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces." These clans shared genealogical and geographical ties with the Kamitsukeno lineage. == See Also == * {{ill|Kenō|ja|毛野}} * {{ill|Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces|ja|東国六腹朝臣}} ** {{ill|Shimotsukeno Clan|ja|下毛野氏|lt=Shimotsukeno clan}} * {{ill|Kamitsuke no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|上毛野国造}} * {{ill|Akagi Shrine|ja|赤城神社}} [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:Unsorted completion ({{ill|Emperor Sujin|ja|崇神天皇}}'s son) | Lineage = Imperial | Origin = Kamitsukeno Province (modern-day {{ill|Gunma Prefecture|ja|群馬県}})
Later relocated to Yamashiro Province | Notable Members = See [[Kamitsukeno Clan#Notable Figures|Notable Figures Section]] | Descendants = See [[Kamitsukeno Clan#Related Clans|Related Clans Section]] }} The '''Kamitsukeno Clan''' (上毛野氏, also read as ''Kamitsukenu'')While the reading ''Kamitsukenu'' has been used since the Edo period, some scholars argue this is a misreading. See [[Kenō#Origin and Pronunciation]]. was a [[Japanese clan]] that took its name from the region of Kamitsukeno. Members of the clan often served as [[kuni no miyatsuko]] (provincial governors). The clan claimed descent from {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto}}, a son of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|ja|崇神天皇}}, and was categorized as an imperial lineage (皇別). Over time, the clan adopted the titles "Kamitsukeno no Kimi (公)" and later "Kamitsukeno no Asomi (朝臣)." The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records the clan's lineage and traditions, which are also shared with other related clans. This article provides an overview of the Kamitsukeno Clan and its related clans. == Overview == The Kamitsukeno Clan was based in the ancient Kamitsukeno region (modern {{ill|Gunma Prefecture|ja|群馬県}}), as indicated by its name. The term ''Kenō'' (毛野) referred to the areas of modern-day Gunma and Tochigi Prefectures in ancient times.{{Kotobank|毛野|MyPedia|ja}} The region was later divided into {{ill|Kōzuke Province|ja|上野国}} (Gunma) and {{ill|Shimotsuke Province|ja|下野国}} (Tochigi). Gunma Prefecture, in particular, is home to many [[kofun]] (ancient burial mounds), indicating the region's significance in early Japan (see [[Kenō]]). The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records that the clan originated from {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto}}, who was dispatched to govern the eastern provinces under imperial command. The text also describes the Kamitsukeno Clan's military and diplomatic activities, particularly concerning interactions with the [[Emishi]] and [[Korea]]. However, whether the clan was a local ruling family or one dispatched from the central court remains unclear.Hirofumi Yamamoto, "History of Gunma You Don't Know" (Yōsensha). Archaeological evidence and later texts support the clan's involvement in regional governance and foreign relations.Toru Wakasa, "Regional Administration in the Ancient Kofun Period" (Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2021). By the late 7th century, the Kamitsukeno Clan became one of the "Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces" (東国六腹朝臣), which included the {{ill|Shimotsukeno Clan|ja|下毛野氏|lt=Shimotsukeno clan}}, Ōno Clan, Ikeda Clan, Sami Clan, and Kuramochi Clan. These clans played active roles as mid-level aristocrats in the imperial court.{{Kotobank|Kamitsukeno Clan|ja}} == Genealogy == The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records that {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto}}, a son of Emperor Sujin, was dispatched to govern the eastern provinces. It also states that he was the ancestor of the {{ill|Kamitsukeno no Kimi|ja|上毛野君}} and {{ill|Shimotsukeno no Kimi|ja|下毛野君}}.''Nihon Shoki,'' Emperor Sujin, 48th Year. The {{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記}} contains similar records.''Kojiki,'' Emperor Sujin. The {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|ja|新撰姓氏録}} states that the Kamitsukeno Asomi (Upper Capital Courtier) lineage was descended from Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto.''Shinsen Shōjiroku,'' Kamitsukeno Asomi, Imperial Lineage (Right Capital). Furthermore, the {{ill|Kokuzō Hongi|ja|国造本紀}} mentions that Toyoki Iribiko's grandson, {{ill|Hikosashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島王}}, was appointed as the first {{ill|kuni no miyatsuko|ja|国造}} of the Kamitsukeno region after pacifying twelve eastern provinces.''Kokuzō Hongi,'' Kamitsukeno Kuni no Miyatsuko. == Historical Overview == The Kamitsukeno Clan's transition from regional power to court aristocracy is evident in both textual and archaeological records. During the early Kofun period, the region saw the construction of large burial mounds, such as the {{ill|Ōtatenjin'yama Kofun|ja|太田天神山古墳}}, indicating a powerful local authority.Taichirō Shiraishi, "Kofun and the Yamato Court" (Bungeishunjū). The clan's later prominence in the central court suggests their integration into the Yamato polity. By the mid-7th century, members of the Kamitsukeno Clan held positions as provincial governors, military leaders, and diplomats. The clan's influence waned in the Heian period, with members becoming lower-ranking court officials and regional administrators.{{Kotobank|Kamitsukeno Clan|Encyclopedia Nipponica|ja}} == Notable Figures == Notable descendants of {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto}} include: * {{ill|Hikosashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島王}} - Appointed governor of 15 eastern provinces. * {{ill|Mimorowake no Mikoto|ja|御諸別命|1=Mimorowake|lt=Mimorowake-no-Mikoto}} - Military leader who fought the Emishi. * {{ill|Aratawake|ja|荒田別|1=Aratawake}} - Diplomat to Korea. * {{ill|Takihase|ja|竹葉瀬}} - Contributed to Korean diplomacy. * {{ill|Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko|ja|上毛野稚子|1=Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko}} - General in the Baekje campaigns. == Related Clans == The Kamitsukeno Clan's descendants include several related families, categorized as the "Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces." These clans shared genealogical and geographical ties with the Kamitsukeno lineage. == See Also == * {{ill|Kenō|ja|毛野}} * {{ill|Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces|ja|東国六腹朝臣}} ** {{ill|Shimotsukeno Clan|ja|下毛野氏|lt=Shimotsukeno clan}} * {{ill|Kamitsuke no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|上毛野国造}} * {{ill|Akagi Shrine|ja|赤城神社}} [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq-Kamitsukeno clan-qq]] [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:Kamitsukeno Clan]] [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq-Kamitsukeno clan-qq]] [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:Clans]] [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq-Kamitsukeno clan-qq]] [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:Japanese clans]] [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq-Kamitsukeno clan-qq]] [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:Clans of Kantō region]] [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq-Kamitsukeno clan-qq]] [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:History of Gunma Prefecture]] [[Category:bump]] [[Category:bump-01-18]] [[Category:refreshing imported pages]] [[Category:second attempt at refreshing on January 27 2024]][[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:second attempt at refreshing on January 27 2024]] [[Category:pgoodbye $1]][[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:pgoodbye $1]] [[Category:refreshing so the massreplace can be done again]] [[Category:kk]] [[Category:fixing the kk issue]] [[Category:SuQqqqqq]] [[Category:qqqq]] [[sn:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:qq]][[sn:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:qq]][[sn:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:qq]] [[ja:上毛野氏]] [[Category:New pages]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:Removing this excess]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:Imperial clans]] ==References==

{{Ancient Japanese Clans | Clan Name = Kamitsukeno Clan | image = [[File:Akagi-jinja (Miyosawa) torii.JPG|280px]]
Shrine associated with the clan: [[Akagi Shrine]] ({{ill|Gunma Prefecture|ja|群馬県}}, {{ill|Maebashi|ja|前橋市}}) | Title = Kamitsukeno no Kimi (公)
Later Kamitsukeno no Asomi | Founder = '''Claimed''': {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto}}
({{ill|Emperor Sujin|ja|崇神天皇}}'s son) | Lineage = Imperial | Origin = Kamitsukeno Province (modern-day {{ill|Gunma Prefecture|ja|群馬県}})
Later relocated to Yamashiro Province | Notable Members = See [[Kamitsukeno Clan#Notable Figures|Notable Figures Section]] | Descendants = See [[Kamitsukeno Clan#Related Clans|Related Clans Section]] }} The '''Kamitsukeno Clan''' (上毛野氏, also read as ''Kamitsukenu'')While the reading ''Kamitsukenu'' has been used since the Edo period, some scholars argue this is a misreading. See [[Kenō#Origin and Pronunciation]]. was a [[Japanese clan]] that took its name from the region of Kamitsukeno. Members of the clan often served as [[kuni no miyatsuko]] (provincial governors). The clan claimed descent from {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto}}, a son of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|ja|崇神天皇}}, and was categorized as an imperial lineage (皇別). Over time, the clan adopted the titles "Kamitsukeno no Kimi (公)" and later "Kamitsukeno no Asomi (朝臣)." The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records the clan's lineage and traditions, which are also shared with other related clans. This article provides an overview of the Kamitsukeno Clan and its related clans. == Overview == The Kamitsukeno Clan was based in the ancient Kamitsukeno region (modern {{ill|Gunma Prefecture|ja|群馬県}}), as indicated by its name. The term ''Kenō'' (毛野) referred to the areas of modern-day Gunma and Tochigi Prefectures in ancient times.{{Kotobank|毛野|MyPedia|ja}} The region was later divided into {{ill|Kōzuke Province|ja|上野国}} (Gunma) and {{ill|Shimotsuke Province|ja|下野国}} (Tochigi). Gunma Prefecture, in particular, is home to many [[kofun]] (ancient burial mounds), indicating the region's significance in early Japan (see [[Kenō]]). The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records that the clan originated from {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto}}, who was dispatched to govern the eastern provinces under imperial command. The text also describes the Kamitsukeno Clan's military and diplomatic activities, particularly concerning interactions with the [[Emishi]] and [[Korea]]. However, whether the clan was a local ruling family or one dispatched from the central court remains unclear.Hirofumi Yamamoto, "History of Gunma You Don't Know" (Yōsensha). Archaeological evidence and later texts support the clan's involvement in regional governance and foreign relations.Toru Wakasa, "Regional Administration in the Ancient Kofun Period" (Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2021). By the late 7th century, the Kamitsukeno Clan became one of the "Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces" (東国六腹朝臣), which included the {{ill|Shimotsukeno Clan|ja|下毛野氏|lt=Shimotsukeno clan}}, Ōno Clan, Ikeda Clan, Sami Clan, and Kuramochi Clan. These clans played active roles as mid-level aristocrats in the imperial court.{{Kotobank|Kamitsukeno Clan|ja}} == Genealogy == The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records that {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto}}, a son of Emperor Sujin, was dispatched to govern the eastern provinces. It also states that he was the ancestor of the {{ill|Kamitsukeno no Kimi|ja|上毛野君}} and {{ill|Shimotsukeno no Kimi|ja|下毛野君}}.''Nihon Shoki,'' Emperor Sujin, 48th Year. The {{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記}} contains similar records.''Kojiki,'' Emperor Sujin. The {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|ja|新撰姓氏録}} states that the Kamitsukeno Asomi (Upper Capital Courtier) lineage was descended from Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto.''Shinsen Shōjiroku,'' Kamitsukeno Asomi, Imperial Lineage (Right Capital). Furthermore, the {{ill|Kokuzō Hongi|ja|国造本紀}} mentions that Toyoki Iribiko's grandson, {{ill|Hikosashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島王}}, was appointed as the first {{ill|kuni no miyatsuko|ja|国造}} of the Kamitsukeno region after pacifying twelve eastern provinces.''Kokuzō Hongi,'' Kamitsukeno Kuni no Miyatsuko. == Historical Overview == The Kamitsukeno Clan's transition from regional power to court aristocracy is evident in both textual and archaeological records. During the early Kofun period, the region saw the construction of large burial mounds, such as the {{ill|Ōtatenjin'yama Kofun|ja|太田天神山古墳}}, indicating a powerful local authority.Taichirō Shiraishi, "Kofun and the Yamato Court" (Bungeishunjū). The clan's later prominence in the central court suggests their integration into the Yamato polity. By the mid-7th century, members of the Kamitsukeno Clan held positions as provincial governors, military leaders, and diplomats. The clan's influence waned in the Heian period, with members becoming lower-ranking court officials and regional administrators.{{Kotobank|Kamitsukeno Clan|Encyclopedia Nipponica|ja}} == Notable Figures == Notable descendants of {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto}} include: * {{ill|Hikosashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島王}} - Appointed governor of 15 eastern provinces. * {{ill|Mimorowake no Mikoto|ja|御諸別命|1=Mimorowake|lt=Mimorowake-no-Mikoto}} - Military leader who fought the Emishi. * {{ill|Aratawake|ja|荒田別|1=Aratawake}} - Diplomat to Korea. * {{ill|Takihase|ja|竹葉瀬}} - Contributed to Korean diplomacy. * {{ill|Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko|ja|上毛野稚子|1=Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko}} - General in the Baekje campaigns. == Related Clans == The Kamitsukeno Clan's descendants include several related families, categorized as the "Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces." These clans shared genealogical and geographical ties with the Kamitsukeno lineage. == See Also == * {{ill|Kenō|ja|毛野}} * {{ill|Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces|ja|東国六腹朝臣}} ** {{ill|Shimotsukeno Clan|ja|下毛野氏|lt=Shimotsukeno clan}} * {{ill|Kamitsuke no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|上毛野国造}} * {{ill|Akagi Shrine|ja|赤城神社}} [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:Unsorted completion ({{ill|Emperor Sujin|ja|崇神天皇}}'s son) | Lineage = Imperial | Origin = Kamitsukeno Province (modern-day {{ill|Gunma Prefecture|ja|群馬県}})
Later relocated to Yamashiro Province | Notable Members = See [[Kamitsukeno Clan#Notable Figures|Notable Figures Section]] | Descendants = See [[Kamitsukeno Clan#Related Clans|Related Clans Section]] }} The '''Kamitsukeno Clan''' (上毛野氏, also read as ''Kamitsukenu'')While the reading ''Kamitsukenu'' has been used since the Edo period, some scholars argue this is a misreading. See [[Kenō#Origin and Pronunciation]]. was a [[Japanese clan]] that took its name from the region of Kamitsukeno. Members of the clan often served as [[kuni no miyatsuko]] (provincial governors). The clan claimed descent from {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto}}, a son of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|ja|崇神天皇}}, and was categorized as an imperial lineage (皇別). Over time, the clan adopted the titles "Kamitsukeno no Kimi (公)" and later "Kamitsukeno no Asomi (朝臣)." The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records the clan's lineage and traditions, which are also shared with other related clans. This article provides an overview of the Kamitsukeno Clan and its related clans. == Overview == The Kamitsukeno Clan was based in the ancient Kamitsukeno region (modern {{ill|Gunma Prefecture|ja|群馬県}}), as indicated by its name. The term ''Kenō'' (毛野) referred to the areas of modern-day Gunma and Tochigi Prefectures in ancient times.{{Kotobank|毛野|MyPedia|ja}} The region was later divided into {{ill|Kōzuke Province|ja|上野国}} (Gunma) and {{ill|Shimotsuke Province|ja|下野国}} (Tochigi). Gunma Prefecture, in particular, is home to many [[kofun]] (ancient burial mounds), indicating the region's significance in early Japan (see [[Kenō]]). The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records that the clan originated from {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto}}, who was dispatched to govern the eastern provinces under imperial command. The text also describes the Kamitsukeno Clan's military and diplomatic activities, particularly concerning interactions with the [[Emishi]] and [[Korea]]. However, whether the clan was a local ruling family or one dispatched from the central court remains unclear.Hirofumi Yamamoto, "History of Gunma You Don't Know" (Yōsensha). Archaeological evidence and later texts support the clan's involvement in regional governance and foreign relations.Toru Wakasa, "Regional Administration in the Ancient Kofun Period" (Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2021). By the late 7th century, the Kamitsukeno Clan became one of the "Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces" (東国六腹朝臣), which included the {{ill|Shimotsukeno Clan|ja|下毛野氏|lt=Shimotsukeno clan}}, Ōno Clan, Ikeda Clan, Sami Clan, and Kuramochi Clan. These clans played active roles as mid-level aristocrats in the imperial court.{{Kotobank|Kamitsukeno Clan|ja}} == Genealogy == The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records that {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto}}, a son of Emperor Sujin, was dispatched to govern the eastern provinces. It also states that he was the ancestor of the {{ill|Kamitsukeno no Kimi|ja|上毛野君}} and {{ill|Shimotsukeno no Kimi|ja|下毛野君}}.''Nihon Shoki,'' Emperor Sujin, 48th Year. The {{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記}} contains similar records.''Kojiki,'' Emperor Sujin. The {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|ja|新撰姓氏録}} states that the Kamitsukeno Asomi (Upper Capital Courtier) lineage was descended from Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto.''Shinsen Shōjiroku,'' Kamitsukeno Asomi, Imperial Lineage (Right Capital). Furthermore, the {{ill|Kokuzō Hongi|ja|国造本紀}} mentions that Toyoki Iribiko's grandson, {{ill|Hikosashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島王}}, was appointed as the first {{ill|kuni no miyatsuko|ja|国造}} of the Kamitsukeno region after pacifying twelve eastern provinces.''Kokuzō Hongi,'' Kamitsukeno Kuni no Miyatsuko. == Historical Overview == The Kamitsukeno Clan's transition from regional power to court aristocracy is evident in both textual and archaeological records. During the early Kofun period, the region saw the construction of large burial mounds, such as the {{ill|Ōtatenjin'yama Kofun|ja|太田天神山古墳}}, indicating a powerful local authority.Taichirō Shiraishi, "Kofun and the Yamato Court" (Bungeishunjū). The clan's later prominence in the central court suggests their integration into the Yamato polity. By the mid-7th century, members of the Kamitsukeno Clan held positions as provincial governors, military leaders, and diplomats. The clan's influence waned in the Heian period, with members becoming lower-ranking court officials and regional administrators.{{Kotobank|Kamitsukeno Clan|Encyclopedia Nipponica|ja}} == Notable Figures == Notable descendants of {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto}} include: * {{ill|Hikosashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島王}} - Appointed governor of 15 eastern provinces. * {{ill|Mimorowake no Mikoto|ja|御諸別命|1=Mimorowake|lt=Mimorowake-no-Mikoto}} - Military leader who fought the Emishi. * {{ill|Aratawake|ja|荒田別|1=Aratawake}} - Diplomat to Korea. * {{ill|Takihase|ja|竹葉瀬}} - Contributed to Korean diplomacy. * {{ill|Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko|ja|上毛野稚子|1=Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko}} - General in the Baekje campaigns. == Related Clans == The Kamitsukeno Clan's descendants include several related families, categorized as the "Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces." These clans shared genealogical and geographical ties with the Kamitsukeno lineage. == See Also == * {{ill|Kenō|ja|毛野}} * {{ill|Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces|ja|東国六腹朝臣}} ** {{ill|Shimotsukeno Clan|ja|下毛野氏|lt=Shimotsukeno clan}} * {{ill|Kamitsuke no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|上毛野国造}} * {{ill|Akagi Shrine|ja|赤城神社}} [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq deprecated open]] [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:Kamitsukeno Clan]] [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq deprecated open]] [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:Clans]] [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq deprecated open]] [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:Japanese clans]] [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq deprecated open]] [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:Clans of Kantō region]] [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq deprecated open]] [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:History of Gunma Prefecture]] [[Category:bump]] [[Category:bump-01-18]] [[Category:refreshing imported pages]] [[Category:second attempt at refreshing on January 27 2024]][[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:second attempt at refreshing on January 27 2024]] [[Category:pgoodbye $1]][[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:pgoodbye $1]] [[Category:kk]] [[Category:fixing the kk issue]] [[Category:SuQqqqqq]] [[Category:qqqq]] [[sn:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:qq]][[sn:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:qq]][[sn:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:qq]] [[ja:上毛野氏]] [[Category:New pages]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:Imperial clans]] ==References==

The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records the clan's lineage and traditions, which are also shared with other related clans. This article provides an overview of the Kamitsukeno Clan and its related clans. == Overview == The Kamitsukeno Clan was based in the ancient Kamitsukeno region (modern {{ill|Gunma Prefecture|ja|群馬県}}), as indicated by its name. The term ''Kenō'' (毛野) referred to the areas of modern-day Gunma and Tochigi Prefectures in ancient times.{{Kotobank|毛野|MyPedia|ja}} The region was later divided into {{ill|Kōzuke Province|ja|上野国}} (Gunma) and {{ill|Shimotsuke Province|ja|下野国}} (Tochigi). Gunma Prefecture, in particular, is home to many [[kofun]] (ancient burial mounds), indicating the region's significance in early Japan (see [[Kenō]]). The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records that the clan originated from {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto}}, who was dispatched to govern the eastern provinces under imperial command. The text also describes the Kamitsukeno Clan's military and diplomatic activities, particularly concerning interactions with the [[Emishi]] and [[Korea]]. However, whether the clan was a local ruling family or one dispatched from the central court remains unclear.Hirofumi Yamamoto, "History of Gunma You Don't Know" (Yōsensha). Archaeological evidence and later texts support the clan's involvement in regional governance and foreign relations.Toru Wakasa, "Regional Administration in the Ancient Kofun Period" (Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2021). By the late 7th century, the Kamitsukeno Clan became one of the "Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces" (東国六腹朝臣), which included the {{ill|Shimotsukeno Clan|ja|下毛野氏|lt=Shimotsukeno clan}}, Ōno Clan, Ikeda Clan, Sami Clan, and Kuramochi Clan. These clans played active roles as mid-level aristocrats in the imperial court.{{Kotobank|Kamitsukeno Clan|ja}} == Genealogy == The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records that {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto}}, a son of Emperor Sujin, was dispatched to govern the eastern provinces. It also states that he was the ancestor of the {{ill|Kamitsukeno no Kimi|ja|上毛野君}} and {{ill|Shimotsukeno no Kimi|ja|下毛野君}}.''Nihon Shoki,'' Emperor Sujin, 48th Year. The {{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記}} contains similar records.''Kojiki,'' Emperor Sujin. The {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|ja|新撰姓氏録}} states that the Kamitsukeno Asomi (Upper Capital Courtier) lineage was descended from Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto.''Shinsen Shōjiroku,'' Kamitsukeno Asomi, Imperial Lineage (Right Capital). Furthermore, the {{ill|Kokuzō Hongi|ja|国造本紀}} mentions that Toyoki Iribiko's grandson, {{ill|Hikosashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島王}}, was appointed as the first {{ill|kuni no miyatsuko|ja|国造}} of the Kamitsukeno region after pacifying twelve eastern provinces.''Kokuzō Hongi,'' Kamitsukeno Kuni no Miyatsuko. == Historical Overview == The Kamitsukeno Clan's transition from regional power to court aristocracy is evident in both textual and archaeological records. During the early Kofun period, the region saw the construction of large burial mounds, such as the {{ill|Ōtatenjin'yama Kofun|ja|太田天神山古墳}}, indicating a powerful local authority.Taichirō Shiraishi, "Kofun and the Yamato Court" (Bungeishunjū). The clan's later prominence in the central court suggests their integration into the Yamato polity. By the mid-7th century, members of the Kamitsukeno Clan held positions as provincial governors, military leaders, and diplomats. The clan's influence waned in the Heian period, with members becoming lower-ranking court officials and regional administrators.{{Kotobank|Kamitsukeno Clan|Encyclopedia Nipponica|ja}} == Notable Figures == Notable descendants of {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto}} include: * {{ill|Hikosashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島王}} - Appointed governor of 15 eastern provinces. * {{ill|Mimorowake no Mikoto|ja|御諸別命|1=Mimorowake|lt=Mimorowake-no-Mikoto}} - Military leader who fought the Emishi. * {{ill|Aratawake|ja|荒田別|1=Aratawake}} - Diplomat to Korea. * {{ill|Takihase|ja|竹葉瀬}} - Contributed to Korean diplomacy. * {{ill|Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko|ja|上毛野稚子|1=Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko}} - General in the Baekje campaigns. == Related Clans == The Kamitsukeno Clan's descendants include several related families, categorized as the "Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces." These clans shared genealogical and geographical ties with the Kamitsukeno lineage. == See Also == * {{ill|Kenō|ja|毛野}} * {{ill|Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces|ja|東国六腹朝臣}} ** The term ''Kenō'' (毛野) referred to the areas of modern-day Gunma and Tochigi Prefectures in ancient times.{{Kotobank|毛野|MyPedia|ja}} The region was later divided into {{ill|Kōzuke Province|ja|上野国}} (Gunma) and {{ill|Shimotsuke Province|ja|下野国}} (Tochigi). Gunma Prefecture, in particular, is home to many [[kofun]] (ancient burial mounds), indicating the region's significance in early Japan (see [[Kenō]]). The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records that the clan originated from {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto}}, who was dispatched to govern the eastern provinces under imperial command. The text also describes the Kamitsukeno Clan's military and diplomatic activities, particularly concerning interactions with the [[Emishi]] and [[Korea]]. However, whether the clan was a local ruling family or one dispatched from the central court remains unclear.Hirofumi Yamamoto, "History of Gunma You Don't Know" (Yōsensha). Archaeological evidence and later texts support the clan's involvement in regional governance and foreign relations.Toru Wakasa, "Regional Administration in the Ancient Kofun Period" (Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2021). By the late 7th century, the Kamitsukeno Clan became one of the "Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces" (東国六腹朝臣), which included the {{ill|Shimotsukeno Clan|ja|下毛野氏|lt=Shimotsukeno clan}}, Ōno Clan, Ikeda Clan, Sami Clan, and Kuramochi Clan. These clans played active roles as mid-level aristocrats in the imperial court.{{Kotobank|Kamitsukeno Clan|ja}} == Genealogy == The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records that {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto}}, a son of Emperor Sujin, was dispatched to govern the eastern provinces. It also states that he was the ancestor of the {{ill|Kamitsukeno no Kimi|ja|上毛野君}} and {{ill|Shimotsukeno no Kimi|ja|下毛野君}}.''Nihon Shoki,'' Emperor Sujin, 48th Year. The {{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記}} contains similar records.''Kojiki,'' Emperor Sujin. The {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|ja|新撰姓氏録}} states that the Kamitsukeno Asomi (Upper Capital Courtier) lineage was descended from Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto.''Shinsen Shōjiroku,'' Kamitsukeno Asomi, Imperial Lineage (Right Capital). Furthermore, the {{ill|Kokuzō Hongi|ja|国造本紀}} mentions that Toyoki Iribiko's grandson, {{ill|Hikosashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島王}}, was appointed as the first {{ill|kuni no miyatsuko|ja|国造}} of the Kamitsukeno region after pacifying twelve eastern provinces.''Kokuzō Hongi,'' Kamitsukeno Kuni no Miyatsuko. == Historical Overview == The Kamitsukeno Clan's transition from regional power to court aristocracy is evident in both textual and archaeological records. During the early Kofun period, the region saw the construction of large burial mounds, such as the {{ill|Ōtatenjin'yama Kofun|ja|太田天神山古墳}}, indicating a powerful local authority.Taichirō Shiraishi, "Kofun and the Yamato Court" (Bungeishunjū). The clan's later prominence in the central court suggests their integration into the Yamato polity. By the mid-7th century, members of the Kamitsukeno Clan held positions as provincial governors, military leaders, and diplomats. The clan's influence waned in the Heian period, with members becoming lower-ranking court officials and regional administrators.{{Kotobank|Kamitsukeno Clan|Encyclopedia Nipponica|ja}} == Notable Figures == Notable descendants of {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto}} include: * {{ill|Hikosashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島王}} - Appointed governor of 15 eastern provinces. * {{ill|Mimorowake no Mikoto|ja|御諸別命|1=Mimorowake|lt=Mimorowake-no-Mikoto}} - Military leader who fought the Emishi. * {{ill|Aratawake|ja|荒田別|1=Aratawake}} - Diplomat to Korea. * {{ill|Takihase|ja|竹葉瀬}} - Contributed to Korean diplomacy. * {{ill|Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko|ja|上毛野稚子|1=Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko}} - General in the Baekje campaigns. == Related Clans == The Kamitsukeno Clan's descendants include several related families, categorized as the "Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces." These clans shared genealogical and geographical ties with the Kamitsukeno lineage. == See Also == * {{ill|Kenō|ja|毛野}} * {{ill|Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces|ja|東国六腹朝臣}} ** {{ill|Shimotsukeno Clan|ja|下毛野氏|lt=Shimotsukeno clan}} * {{ill|Kamitsuke no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|上毛野国造}} * {{ill|Akagi Shrine|ja|赤城神社}} [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:Clans]] [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:Japanese clans]] [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:Clans of Kantō region]] [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:History of Gunma Prefecture]] [[Category:bump]] [[Category:bump-01-18]] [[Category:refreshing imported pages]] [[Category:second attempt at refreshing on January 27 2024]][[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:second attempt at refreshing on January 27 2024]] [[Category:pgoodbye $1]][[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:pgoodbye $1]] [[Category:kk]] [[Category:fixing the kk issue]] [[Category:qq]] [[sn:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:qq]][[sn:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:qq]][[sn:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:qq]] [[ja:上毛野氏]] [[Category:New pages]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:Imperial clans]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:qq]] ==References==

The clan claimed descent from {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto}}, a son of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|ja|崇神天皇}}, and was categorized as an imperial lineage (皇別). Over time, the clan adopted the titles "Kamitsukeno no Kimi (公)" and later "Kamitsukeno no Asomi (朝臣)." The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records the clan's lineage and traditions, which are also shared with other related clans. This article provides an overview of the Kamitsukeno Clan and its related clans. == Overview == The Kamitsukeno Clan was based in the ancient Kamitsukeno region (modern {{ill|Gunma Prefecture|ja|群馬県}}), as indicated by its name. The term ''Kenō'' (毛野) referred to the areas of modern-day Gunma and Tochigi Prefectures in ancient times.{{Kotobank|毛野|MyPedia|ja}} The region was later divided into {{ill|Kōzuke Province|ja|上野国}} (Gunma) and {{ill|Shimotsuke Province|ja|下野国}} (Tochigi). Gunma Prefecture, in particular, is home to many [[kofun]] (ancient burial mounds), indicating the region's significance in early Japan (see [[Kenō]]). The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records that the clan originated from {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto}}, who was dispatched to govern the eastern provinces under imperial command. The text also describes the Kamitsukeno Clan's military and diplomatic activities, particularly concerning interactions with the [[Emishi]] and [[Korea]]. However, whether the clan was a local ruling family or one dispatched from the central court remains unclear.Hirofumi Yamamoto, "History of Gunma You Don't Know" (Yōsensha). Archaeological evidence and later texts support the clan's involvement in regional governance and foreign relations.Toru Wakasa, "Regional Administration in the Ancient Kofun Period" (Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2021). By the late 7th century, the Kamitsukeno Clan became one of the "Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces" (東国六腹朝臣), which included the {{ill|Shimotsukeno Clan|ja|下毛野氏|lt=Shimotsukeno clan}}, Ōno Clan, Ikeda Clan, Sami Clan, and Kuramochi Clan. These clans played active roles as mid-level aristocrats in the imperial court.{{Kotobank|Kamitsukeno Clan|ja}} == Genealogy == The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records that {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto}}, a son of Emperor Sujin, was dispatched to govern the eastern provinces. It also states that he was the ancestor of the {{ill|Kamitsukeno no Kimi|ja|上毛野君}} and {{ill|Shimotsukeno no Kimi|ja|下毛野君}}.''Nihon Shoki,'' Emperor Sujin, 48th Year. The {{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記}} contains similar records.''Kojiki,'' Emperor Sujin. The {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|ja|新撰姓氏録}} states that the Kamitsukeno Asomi (Upper Capital Courtier) lineage was descended from Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto.''Shinsen Shōjiroku,'' Kamitsukeno Asomi, Imperial Lineage (Right Capital). Furthermore, the {{ill|Kokuzō Hongi|ja|国造本紀}} mentions that Toyoki Iribiko's grandson, {{ill|Hikosashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島王}}, was appointed as the first {{ill|kuni no miyatsuko|ja|国造}} of the Kamitsukeno region after pacifying twelve eastern provinces.''Kokuzō Hongi,'' Kamitsukeno Kuni no Miyatsuko. == Historical Overview == The Kamitsukeno Clan's transition from regional power to court aristocracy is evident in both textual and archaeological records. During the early Kofun period, the region saw the construction of large burial mounds, such as the {{ill|Ōtatenjin'yama Kofun|ja|太田天神山古墳}}, indicating a powerful local authority.Taichirō Shiraishi, "Kofun and the Yamato Court" (Bungeishunjū). The clan's later prominence in the central court suggests their integration into the Yamato polity. By the mid-7th century, members of the Kamitsukeno Clan held positions as provincial governors, military leaders, and diplomats. The clan's influence waned in the Heian period, with members becoming lower-ranking court officials and regional administrators.{{Kotobank|Kamitsukeno Clan|Encyclopedia Nipponica|ja}} == Notable Figures == Notable descendants of {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto}} include: * {{ill|Hikosashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島王}} - Appointed governor of 15 eastern provinces. * {{ill|Mimorowake no Mikoto|ja|御諸別命|1=Mimorowake|lt=Mimorowake-no-Mikoto}} - Military leader who fought the Emishi. * {{ill|Aratawake|ja|荒田別|1=Aratawake}} - Diplomat to Korea. * {{ill|Takihase|ja|竹葉瀬}} - Contributed to Korean diplomacy. * {{ill|Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko|ja|上毛野稚子|1=Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko}} - General in the Baekje campaigns. == Related Clans == The Kamitsukeno Clan's descendants include several related families, categorized as the "Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces." These clans shared genealogical and geographical ties with the Kamitsukeno lineage. == See Also == * {{ill|Kenō|ja|毛野}} * {{ill|Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces|ja|東国六腹朝臣}} ** {{ill|Shimotsukeno Clan|ja|下毛野氏|lt=Shimotsukeno clan}} * {{ill|Kamitsuke no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|上毛野国造}} * {{ill|Akagi Shrine|ja|赤城神社}} [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:Unsorted completion {{Ancient Japanese Clans | Clan Name = Kamitsukeno Clan | image = [[File:Akagi-jinja (Miyosawa) torii.JPG|280px]]
Shrine associated with the clan: [[Akagi Shrine]] ({{ill|Gunma Prefecture|ja|群馬県}}, {{ill|Maebashi|ja|前橋市}}) | Title = Kamitsukeno no Kimi (公)
Later Kamitsukeno no Asomi | Founder = '''Claimed''': {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto}}
({{ill|Emperor Sujin|ja|崇神天皇}}'s son) | Lineage = Imperial | Origin = Kamitsukeno Province (modern-day {{ill|Gunma Prefecture|ja|群馬県}})
Later relocated to Yamashiro Province | Notable Members = See [[Kamitsukeno Clan#Notable Figures|Notable Figures Section]] | Descendants = See [[Kamitsukeno Clan#Related Clans|Related Clans Section]] }} The '''Kamitsukeno Clan''' (上毛野氏, also read as ''Kamitsukenu'')While the reading ''Kamitsukenu'' has been used since the Edo period, some scholars argue this is a misreading. See [[Kenō#Origin and Pronunciation]]. was a [[Japanese clan]] that took its name from the region of Kamitsukeno. Members of the clan often served as [[kuni no miyatsuko]] (provincial governors). The clan claimed descent from {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto}}, a son of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|ja|崇神天皇}}, and was categorized as an imperial lineage (皇別). Over time, the clan adopted the titles "Kamitsukeno no Kimi (公)" and later "Kamitsukeno no Asomi (朝臣)." The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records the clan's lineage and traditions, which are also shared with other related clans. This article provides an overview of the Kamitsukeno Clan and its related clans. == Overview == The Kamitsukeno Clan was based in the ancient Kamitsukeno region (modern {{ill|Gunma Prefecture|ja|群馬県}}), as indicated by its name. The term ''Kenō'' (毛野) referred to the areas of modern-day Gunma and Tochigi Prefectures in ancient times.{{Kotobank|毛野|MyPedia|ja}} The region was later divided into {{ill|Kōzuke Province|ja|上野国}} (Gunma) and {{ill|Shimotsuke Province|ja|下野国}} (Tochigi). Gunma Prefecture, in particular, is home to many [[kofun]] (ancient burial mounds), indicating the region's significance in early Japan (see [[Kenō]]). The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records that the clan originated from {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto}}, who was dispatched to govern the eastern provinces under imperial command. The text also describes the Kamitsukeno Clan's military and diplomatic activities, particularly concerning interactions with the [[Emishi]] and [[Korea]]. However, whether the clan was a local ruling family or one dispatched from the central court remains unclear.Hirofumi Yamamoto, "History of Gunma You Don't Know" (Yōsensha). Archaeological evidence and later texts support the clan's involvement in regional governance and foreign relations.Toru Wakasa, "Regional Administration in the Ancient Kofun Period" (Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2021). By the late 7th century, the Kamitsukeno Clan became one of the "Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces" (東国六腹朝臣), which included the {{ill|Shimotsukeno Clan|ja|下毛野氏|lt=Shimotsukeno clan}}, Ōno Clan, Ikeda Clan, Sami Clan, and Kuramochi Clan. These clans played active roles as mid-level aristocrats in the imperial court.{{Kotobank|Kamitsukeno Clan|ja}} == Genealogy == The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records that {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto}}, a son of Emperor Sujin, was dispatched to govern the eastern provinces. It also states that he was the ancestor of the {{ill|Kamitsukeno no Kimi|ja|上毛野君}} and {{ill|Shimotsukeno no Kimi|ja|下毛野君}}.''Nihon Shoki,'' Emperor Sujin, 48th Year. The {{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記}} contains similar records.''Kojiki,'' Emperor Sujin. The {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|ja|新撰姓氏録}} states that the Kamitsukeno Asomi (Upper Capital Courtier) lineage was descended from Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto.''Shinsen Shōjiroku,'' Kamitsukeno Asomi, Imperial Lineage (Right Capital). Furthermore, the {{ill|Kokuzō Hongi|ja|国造本紀}} mentions that Toyoki Iribiko's grandson, {{ill|Hikosashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島王}}, was appointed as the first {{ill|kuni no miyatsuko|ja|国造}} of the Kamitsukeno region after pacifying twelve eastern provinces.''Kokuzō Hongi,'' Kamitsukeno Kuni no Miyatsuko. == Historical Overview == The Kamitsukeno Clan's transition from regional power to court aristocracy is evident in both textual and archaeological records. During the early Kofun period, the region saw the construction of large burial mounds, such as the {{ill|Ōtatenjin'yama Kofun|ja|太田天神山古墳}}, indicating a powerful local authority.Taichirō Shiraishi, "Kofun and the Yamato Court" (Bungeishunjū). The clan's later prominence in the central court suggests their integration into the Yamato polity. By the mid-7th century, members of the Kamitsukeno Clan held positions as provincial governors, military leaders, and diplomats. The clan's influence waned in the Heian period, with members becoming lower-ranking court officials and regional administrators.{{Kotobank|Kamitsukeno Clan|Encyclopedia Nipponica|ja}} == Notable Figures == Notable descendants of {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto}} include: * {{ill|Hikosashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島王}} - Appointed governor of 15 eastern provinces. * {{ill|Mimorowake no Mikoto|ja|御諸別命|1=Mimorowake|lt=Mimorowake-no-Mikoto}} - Military leader who fought the Emishi. * {{ill|Aratawake|ja|荒田別|1=Aratawake}} - Diplomat to Korea. * {{ill|Takihase|ja|竹葉瀬}} - Contributed to Korean diplomacy. * {{ill|Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko|ja|上毛野稚子|1=Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko}} - General in the Baekje campaigns. == Related Clans == The Kamitsukeno Clan's descendants include several related families, categorized as the "Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces." These clans shared genealogical and geographical ties with the Kamitsukeno lineage. == See Also == * {{ill|Kenō|ja|毛野}} * {{ill|Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces|ja|東国六腹朝臣}} ** {{ill|Shimotsukeno Clan|ja|下毛野氏|lt=Shimotsukeno clan}} * {{ill|Kamitsuke no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|上毛野国造}} * {{ill|Akagi Shrine|ja|赤城神社}} [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:Completion tier 1]] ({{ill|Emperor Sujin|ja|崇神天皇}}'s son) | Lineage = Imperial | Origin = Kamitsukeno Province (modern-day {{ill|Gunma Prefecture|ja|群馬県}})
Later relocated to Yamashiro Province | Notable Members = See [[Kamitsukeno Clan#Notable Figures|Notable Figures Section]] | Descendants = See [[Kamitsukeno Clan#Related Clans|Related Clans Section]] }} The '''Kamitsukeno Clan''' (上毛野氏, also read as ''Kamitsukenu'')While the reading ''Kamitsukenu'' has been used since the Edo period, some scholars argue this is a misreading. See [[Kenō#Origin and Pronunciation]]. was a [[Japanese clan]] that took its name from the region of Kamitsukeno. Members of the clan often served as [[kuni no miyatsuko]] (provincial governors). The clan claimed descent from {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto}}, a son of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|ja|崇神天皇}}, and was categorized as an imperial lineage (皇別). Over time, the clan adopted the titles "Kamitsukeno no Kimi (公)" and later "Kamitsukeno no Asomi (朝臣)." The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records the clan's lineage and traditions, which are also shared with other related clans. This article provides an overview of the Kamitsukeno Clan and its related clans. == Overview == The Kamitsukeno Clan was based in the ancient Kamitsukeno region (modern {{ill|Gunma Prefecture|ja|群馬県}}), as indicated by its name. The term ''Kenō'' (毛野) referred to the areas of modern-day Gunma and Tochigi Prefectures in ancient times.{{Kotobank|毛野|MyPedia|ja}} The region was later divided into {{ill|Kōzuke Province|ja|上野国}} (Gunma) and {{ill|Shimotsuke Province|ja|下野国}} (Tochigi). Gunma Prefecture, in particular, is home to many [[kofun]] (ancient burial mounds), indicating the region's significance in early Japan (see [[Kenō]]). The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records that the clan originated from {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto}}, who was dispatched to govern the eastern provinces under imperial command. The text also describes the Kamitsukeno Clan's military and diplomatic activities, particularly concerning interactions with the [[Emishi]] and [[Korea]]. However, whether the clan was a local ruling family or one dispatched from the central court remains unclear.Hirofumi Yamamoto, "History of Gunma You Don't Know" (Yōsensha). Archaeological evidence and later texts support the clan's involvement in regional governance and foreign relations.Toru Wakasa, "Regional Administration in the Ancient Kofun Period" (Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2021). By the late 7th century, the Kamitsukeno Clan became one of the "Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces" (東国六腹朝臣), which included the {{ill|Shimotsukeno Clan|ja|下毛野氏|lt=Shimotsukeno clan}}, Ōno Clan, Ikeda Clan, Sami Clan, and Kuramochi Clan. These clans played active roles as mid-level aristocrats in the imperial court.{{Kotobank|Kamitsukeno Clan|ja}} == Genealogy == The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records that {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto}}, a son of Emperor Sujin, was dispatched to govern the eastern provinces. It also states that he was the ancestor of the {{ill|Kamitsukeno no Kimi|ja|上毛野君}} and {{ill|Shimotsukeno no Kimi|ja|下毛野君}}.''Nihon Shoki,'' Emperor Sujin, 48th Year. The {{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記}} contains similar records.''Kojiki,'' Emperor Sujin. The {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|ja|新撰姓氏録}} states that the Kamitsukeno Asomi (Upper Capital Courtier) lineage was descended from Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto.''Shinsen Shōjiroku,'' Kamitsukeno Asomi, Imperial Lineage (Right Capital). Furthermore, the {{ill|Kokuzō Hongi|ja|国造本紀}} mentions that Toyoki Iribiko's grandson, {{ill|Hikosashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島王}}, was appointed as the first {{ill|kuni no miyatsuko|ja|国造}} of the Kamitsukeno region after pacifying twelve eastern provinces.''Kokuzō Hongi,'' Kamitsukeno Kuni no Miyatsuko. == Historical Overview == The Kamitsukeno Clan's transition from regional power to court aristocracy is evident in both textual and archaeological records. During the early Kofun period, the region saw the construction of large burial mounds, such as the {{ill|Ōtatenjin'yama Kofun|ja|太田天神山古墳}}, indicating a powerful local authority.Taichirō Shiraishi, "Kofun and the Yamato Court" (Bungeishunjū). The clan's later prominence in the central court suggests their integration into the Yamato polity. By the mid-7th century, members of the Kamitsukeno Clan held positions as provincial governors, military leaders, and diplomats. The clan's influence waned in the Heian period, with members becoming lower-ranking court officials and regional administrators.{{Kotobank|Kamitsukeno Clan|Encyclopedia Nipponica|ja}} == Notable Figures == Notable descendants of {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto}} include: * {{ill|Hikosashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島王}} - Appointed governor of 15 eastern provinces. * {{ill|Mimorowake no Mikoto|ja|御諸別命|1=Mimorowake|lt=Mimorowake-no-Mikoto}} - Military leader who fought the Emishi. * {{ill|Aratawake|ja|荒田別|1=Aratawake}} - Diplomat to Korea. * {{ill|Takihase|ja|竹葉瀬}} - Contributed to Korean diplomacy. * {{ill|Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko|ja|上毛野稚子|1=Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko}} - General in the Baekje campaigns. == Related Clans == The Kamitsukeno Clan's descendants include several related families, categorized as the "Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces." These clans shared genealogical and geographical ties with the Kamitsukeno lineage. == See Also == * {{ill|Kenō|ja|毛野}} * {{ill|Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces|ja|東国六腹朝臣}} ** The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records the clan's lineage and traditions, which are also shared with other related clans. This article provides an overview of the Kamitsukeno Clan and its related clans. == Overview == The Kamitsukeno Clan was based in the ancient Kamitsukeno region (modern {{ill|Gunma Prefecture|ja|群馬県}}), as indicated by its name. The term ''Kenō'' (毛野) referred to the areas of modern-day Gunma and Tochigi Prefectures in ancient times.{{Kotobank|毛野|MyPedia|ja}} The region was later divided into {{ill|Kōzuke Province|ja|上野国}} (Gunma) and {{ill|Shimotsuke Province|ja|下野国}} (Tochigi). Gunma Prefecture, in particular, is home to many [[kofun]] (ancient Kofuns), indicating the region's significance in early Japan (see [[Kenō]]). The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records that the clan originated from {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto}}, who was dispatched to govern the eastern provinces under imperial command. The text also describes the Kamitsukeno Clan's military and diplomatic activities, particularly concerning interactions with the [[Emishi]] and [[Korea]]. However, whether the clan was a local ruling family or one dispatched from the central court remains unclear.Hirofumi Yamamoto, "History of Gunma You Don't Know" (Yōsensha). Archaeological evidence and later texts support the clan's involvement in regional governance and foreign relations.Toru Wakasa, "Regional Administration in the Ancient Kofun Period" (Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2021). By the late 7th century, the Kamitsukeno Clan became one of the "Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces" (東国六腹朝臣), which included the {{ill|Shimotsukeno Clan|ja|下毛野氏|lt=Shimotsukeno clan}}, Ōno Clan, Ikeda Clan, Sami Clan, and Kuramochi Clan. These clans played active roles as mid-level aristocrats in the imperial court.{{Kotobank|Kamitsukeno Clan|ja}} == Genealogy == The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records that {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto}}, a son of Emperor Sujin, was dispatched to govern the eastern provinces. It also states that he was the ancestor of the {{ill|Kamitsukeno no Kimi|ja|上毛野君}} and {{ill|Shimotsukeno no Kimi|ja|下毛野君}}.''Nihon Shoki,'' Emperor Sujin, 48th Year. The {{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記}} contains similar records.''Kojiki,'' Emperor Sujin. The {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|ja|新撰姓氏録}} states that the Kamitsukeno Asomi (Upper Capital Courtier) lineage was descended from Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto.''Shinsen Shōjiroku,'' Kamitsukeno Asomi, Imperial Lineage (Right Capital). Furthermore, the {{ill|Kokuzō Hongi|ja|国造本紀}} mentions that Toyoki Iribiko's grandson, {{ill|Hikosashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島王}}, was appointed as the first {{ill|kuni no miyatsuko|ja|国造}} of the Kamitsukeno region after pacifying twelve eastern provinces.''Kokuzō Hongi,'' Kamitsukeno Kuni no Miyatsuko. == Historical Overview == The Kamitsukeno Clan's transition from regional power to court aristocracy is evident in both textual and archaeological records. During the early Kofun period, the region saw the construction of large Kofuns, such as the {{ill|Ōtatenjin'yama Kofun|ja|太田天神山古墳}}, indicating a powerful local authority.Taichirō Shiraishi, "Kofun and the Yamato Court" (Bungeishunjū). The clan's later prominence in the central court suggests their integration into the Yamato polity. By the mid-7th century, members of the Kamitsukeno Clan held positions as provincial governors, military leaders, and diplomats. The clan's influence waned in the Heian period, with members becoming lower-ranking court officials and regional administrators.{{Kotobank|Kamitsukeno Clan|Encyclopedia Nipponica|ja}} == Notable Figures == Notable descendants of {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto}} include: * {{ill|Hikosashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島王}} - Appointed governor of 15 eastern provinces. * {{ill|Mimorowake no Mikoto|ja|御諸別命|1=Mimorowake|lt=Mimorowake-no-Mikoto}} - Military leader who fought the Emishi. * {{ill|Aratawake|ja|荒田別|1=Aratawake}} - Diplomat to Korea. * {{ill|Takihase|ja|竹葉瀬}} - Contributed to Korean diplomacy. * {{ill|Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko|ja|上毛野稚子|1=Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko}} - General in the Baekje campaigns. == Related Clans == The Kamitsukeno Clan's descendants include several related families, categorized as the "Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces." {{Ancient Japanese Clans | Clan Name = Kamitsukeno Clan | image = [[File:Akagi-jinja (Miyosawa) torii.JPG|280px]]
Shrine associated with the clan: {{ill|Miyosawa Akagi Shrine|ja|赤城神社_(前橋市三夜沢町)}} ({{ill|Gunma Prefecture|ja|群馬県}}, {{ill|Maebashi|ja|前橋市}}) | Title = Kamitsukeno no Kimi (公)
Later Kamitsukeno no Asomi | Founder = '''Claimed''': {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto}}
({{ill|Emperor Sujin|ja|崇神天皇}}'s son) | Lineage = Imperial | Origin = Kamitsukeno Province (modern-day {{ill|Gunma Prefecture|ja|群馬県}})
Later relocated to Yamashiro Province | Notable Members = See [[Kamitsukeno Clan#Notable Figures|Notable Figures Section]] | Descendants = See [[Kamitsukeno Clan#Related Clans|Related Clans Section]] }} The '''Kamitsukeno Clan''' (上毛野氏, also read as ''Kamitsukenu'')While the reading ''Kamitsukenu'' has been used since the Edo period, some scholars argue this is a misreading. See [[Kenō#Origin and Pronunciation]]. was a [[Japanese clan]] that took its name from the region of Kamitsukeno. Members of the clan often served as [[kuni no miyatsuko]] (provincial governors). The clan claimed descent from {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto}}, a son of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|ja|崇神天皇}}, and was categorized as an imperial lineage (皇別). Over time, the clan adopted the titles "Kamitsukeno no Kimi (公)" and later "Kamitsukeno no Asomi (朝臣)." The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records the clan's lineage and traditions, which are also shared with other related clans. This article provides an overview of the Kamitsukeno Clan and its related clans. == Overview == The Kamitsukeno Clan was based in the ancient Kamitsukeno region (modern {{ill|Gunma Prefecture|ja|群馬県}}), as indicated by its name. The term ''Kenō'' (毛野) referred to the areas of modern-day Gunma and Tochigi Prefectures in ancient times.{{Kotobank|毛野|MyPedia|ja}} The region was later divided into {{ill|Kōzuke Province|ja|上野国}} (Gunma) and {{ill|Shimotsuke Province|ja|下野国}} (Tochigi). Gunma Prefecture, in particular, is home to many [[kofun]] (ancient Kofuns), indicating the region's significance in early Japan (see [[Kenō]]). The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records that the clan originated from {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto}}, who was dispatched to govern the eastern provinces under imperial command. The text also describes the Kamitsukeno Clan's military and diplomatic activities, particularly concerning interactions with the [[Emishi]] and [[Korea]]. However, whether the clan was a local ruling family or one dispatched from the central court remains unclear.Hirofumi Yamamoto, "History of Gunma You Don't Know" (Yōsensha). Archaeological evidence and later texts support the clan's involvement in regional governance and foreign relations.Toru Wakasa, "Regional Administration in the Ancient Kofun Period" (Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2021). By the late 7th century, the Kamitsukeno Clan became one of the "Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces" (東国六腹朝臣), which included the {{ill|Shimotsukeno Clan|ja|下毛野氏|lt=Shimotsukeno clan}}, Ōno Clan, Ikeda Clan, Sami Clan, and Kuramochi Clan. These clans played active roles as mid-level aristocrats in the imperial court.{{Kotobank|Kamitsukeno Clan|ja}} == Genealogy == The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records that {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto}}, a son of Emperor Sujin, was dispatched to govern the eastern provinces. It also states that he was the ancestor of the {{ill|Kamitsukeno no Kimi|ja|上毛野君}} and {{ill|Shimotsukeno no Kimi|ja|下毛野君}}.''Nihon Shoki,'' Emperor Sujin, 48th Year. The {{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記}} contains similar records.''Kojiki,'' Emperor Sujin. The {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|ja|新撰姓氏録}} states that the Kamitsukeno Asomi (Upper Capital Courtier) lineage was descended from Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto.''Shinsen Shōjiroku,'' Kamitsukeno Asomi, Imperial Lineage (Right Capital). Furthermore, the {{ill|Kokuzō Hongi|ja|国造本紀}} mentions that Toyoki Iribiko's grandson, {{ill|Hikosashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島王}}, was appointed as the first {{ill|kuni no miyatsuko|ja|国造}} of the Kamitsukeno region after pacifying twelve eastern provinces.''Kokuzō Hongi,'' Kamitsukeno Kuni no Miyatsuko. == Historical Overview == The Kamitsukeno Clan's transition from regional power to court aristocracy is evident in both textual and archaeological records. During the early Kofun period, the region saw the construction of large Kofuns, such as the {{ill|Ōtatenjin'yama Kofun|ja|太田天神山古墳}}, indicating a powerful local authority.Taichirō Shiraishi, "Kofun and the Yamato Court" (Bungeishunjū). The clan's later prominence in the central court suggests their integration into the Yamato polity. By the mid-7th century, members of the Kamitsukeno Clan held positions as provincial governors, military leaders, and diplomats. The clan's influence waned in the Heian period, with members becoming lower-ranking court officials and regional administrators.{{Kotobank|Kamitsukeno Clan|Encyclopedia Nipponica|ja}} == Notable Figures == Notable descendants of {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto}} include: * {{ill|Hikosashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島王}} - Appointed governor of 15 eastern provinces. * {{ill|Mimorowake no Mikoto|ja|御諸別命|1=Mimorowake|lt=Mimorowake-no-Mikoto}} - Military leader who fought the Emishi. * {{ill|Aratawake|ja|荒田別|1=Aratawake}} - Diplomat to Korea. * {{ill|Takihase|ja|竹葉瀬}} - Contributed to Korean diplomacy. * {{ill|Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko|ja|上毛野稚子|1=Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko}} - General in the Baekje campaigns. == Related Clans == The Kamitsukeno Clan's descendants include several related families, categorized as the "Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces." These clans shared genealogical and geographical ties with the Kamitsukeno lineage. == See Also == * {{ill|Kenō|ja|毛野}} * {{ill|Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces|ja|東国六腹朝臣}} ** {{ill|Shimotsukeno Clan|ja|下毛野氏|lt=Shimotsukeno clan}} * {{ill|Kamitsuke no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|上毛野国造}} * {{ill|Akagi Shrine|ja|赤城神社}} [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:Completion tier 1]] During the early Kofun period, the region saw the construction of large Kofuns, such as the {{ill|Ōtatenjin'yama Kofun|ja|太田天神山古墳}}, indicating a powerful local authority.Taichirō Shiraishi, "Kofun and the Yamato Court" (Bungeishunjū). The clan's later prominence in the central court suggests their integration into the Yamato polity. By the mid-7th century, members of the Kamitsukeno Clan held positions as provincial governors, military leaders, and diplomats. The clan's influence waned in the Heian period, with members becoming lower-ranking court officials and regional administrators.{{Kotobank|Kamitsukeno Clan|Encyclopedia Nipponica|ja}} == Notable Figures == Notable descendants of {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto}} include: * {{ill|Hikosashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島王}} - Appointed governor of 15 eastern provinces. * {{ill|Mimorowake no Mikoto|ja|御諸別命|1=Mimorowake|lt=Mimorowake-no-Mikoto}} - Military leader who fought the Emishi. * {{ill|Aratawake|ja|荒田別|1=Aratawake}} - Diplomat to Korea. * {{ill|Takihase|ja|竹葉瀬}} - Contributed to Korean diplomacy. * {{ill|Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko|ja|上毛野稚子|1=Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko}} - General in the Baekje campaigns. == Related Clans == The Kamitsukeno Clan's descendants include several related families, categorized as the "Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces." {{Ancient Japanese Clans | Clan Name = Kamitsukeno Clan | image = [[File:Akagi-jinja (Miyosawa) torii.JPG|280px]]
Shrine associated with the clan: {{ill|Miyosawa Akagi Shrine|ja|赤城神社_(前橋市三夜沢町)}} ({{ill|Gunma Prefecture|ja|群馬県}}, {{ill|Maebashi|ja|前橋市}}) | Title = Kamitsukeno no Kimi (公)
Later Kamitsukeno no Asomi | Founder = '''Claimed''': {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto}}
({{ill|Emperor Sujin|ja|崇神天皇}}'s son) | Lineage = Imperial | Origin = Kamitsukeno Province (modern-day {{ill|Gunma Prefecture|ja|群馬県}})
Later relocated to Yamashiro Province | Notable Members = See [[Kamitsukeno Clan#Notable Figures|Notable Figures Section]] | Descendants = See [[Kamitsukeno Clan#Related Clans|Related Clans Section]] }} The '''Kamitsukeno Clan''' (上毛野氏, also read as ''Kamitsukenu'')While the reading ''Kamitsukenu'' has been used since the Edo period, some scholars argue this is a misreading. See [[Kenō#Origin and Pronunciation]]. was a [[Japanese clan]] that took its name from the region of Kamitsukeno. Members of the clan often served as [[kuni no miyatsuko]] (provincial governors). The clan claimed descent from {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto}}, a son of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|ja|崇神天皇}}, and was categorized as an imperial lineage (皇別). Over time, the clan adopted the titles "Kamitsukeno no Kimi (公)" and later "Kamitsukeno no Asomi (朝臣)." The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records the clan's lineage and traditions, which are also shared with other related clans. This article provides an overview of the Kamitsukeno Clan and its related clans. == Overview == The Kamitsukeno Clan was based in the ancient Kamitsukeno region (modern {{ill|Gunma Prefecture|ja|群馬県}}), as indicated by its name. The term ''Kenō'' (毛野) referred to the areas of modern-day Gunma and Tochigi Prefectures in ancient times.{{Kotobank|毛野|MyPedia|ja}} The region was later divided into {{ill|Kōzuke Province|ja|上野国}} (Gunma) and {{ill|Shimotsuke Province|ja|下野国}} (Tochigi). Gunma Prefecture, in particular, is home to many [[kofun]] (ancient Kofuns), indicating the region's significance in early Japan (see [[Kenō]]). The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records that the clan originated from {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto}}, who was dispatched to govern the eastern provinces under imperial command. The text also describes the Kamitsukeno Clan's military and diplomatic activities, particularly concerning interactions with the [[Emishi]] and [[Korea]]. However, whether the clan was a local ruling family or one dispatched from the central court remains unclear.Hirofumi Yamamoto, "History of Gunma You Don't Know" (Yōsensha). Archaeological evidence and later texts support the clan's involvement in regional governance and foreign relations.Toru Wakasa, "Regional Administration in the Ancient Kofun Period" (Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2021). By the late 7th century, the Kamitsukeno Clan became one of the "Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces" (東国六腹朝臣), which included the {{ill|Shimotsukeno Clan|ja|下毛野氏|lt=Shimotsukeno clan}}, Ōno Clan, Ikeda Clan, Sami Clan, and Kuramochi Clan. These clans played active roles as mid-level aristocrats in the imperial court.{{Kotobank|Kamitsukeno Clan|ja}} == Genealogy == The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records that {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto}}, a son of Emperor Sujin, was dispatched to govern the eastern provinces. It also states that he was the ancestor of the {{ill|Kamitsukeno no Kimi|ja|上毛野君}} and {{ill|Shimotsukeno no Kimi|ja|下毛野君}}.''Nihon Shoki,'' Emperor Sujin, 48th Year. The {{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記}} contains similar records.''Kojiki,'' Emperor Sujin. The {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|ja|新撰姓氏録}} states that the Kamitsukeno Asomi (Upper Capital Courtier) lineage was descended from Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto.''Shinsen Shōjiroku,'' Kamitsukeno Asomi, Imperial Lineage (Right Capital). Furthermore, the {{ill|Kokuzō Hongi|ja|国造本紀}} mentions that Toyoki Iribiko's grandson, {{ill|Hikosashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島王}}, was appointed as the first {{ill|kuni no miyatsuko|ja|国造}} of the Kamitsukeno region after pacifying twelve eastern provinces.''Kokuzō Hongi,'' Kamitsukeno Kuni no Miyatsuko. == Historical Overview == The Kamitsukeno Clan's transition from regional power to court aristocracy is evident in both textual and archaeological records. By the mid-7th century, members of the Kamitsukeno Clan held positions as provincial governors, military leaders, and diplomats. The clan's influence waned in the Heian period, with members becoming lower-ranking court officials and regional administrators.{{Kotobank|Kamitsukeno Clan|Encyclopedia Nipponica|ja}} == Notable Figures == Notable descendants of {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto}} include: * {{ill|Hikosashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島王}} - Appointed governor of 15 eastern provinces. * {{ill|Mimorowake no Mikoto|ja|御諸別命|1=Mimorowake|lt=Mimorowake-no-Mikoto}} - Military leader who fought the Emishi. * {{ill|Aratawake|ja|荒田別|1=Aratawake}} - Diplomat to Korea. * {{ill|Takihase|ja|竹葉瀬}} - Contributed to Korean diplomacy. * {{ill|Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko|ja|上毛野稚子|1=Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko}} - General in the Baekje campaigns. == Related Clans == The Kamitsukeno Clan's descendants include several related families, categorized as the "Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces." Later relocated to Yamashiro Province | Notable Members = See [[Kamitsukeno Clan#Notable Figures|Notable Figures Section]] | Descendants = See [[Kamitsukeno Clan#Related Clans|Related Clans Section]] }} The '''Kamitsukeno Clan''' (上毛野氏, also read as ''Kamitsukenu'')While the reading ''Kamitsukenu'' has been used since the Edo period, some scholars argue this is a misreading. See [[Kenō#Origin and Pronunciation]]. was a [[Japanese clan]] that took its name from the region of Kamitsukeno. Members of the clan often served as [[kuni no miyatsuko]] (provincial governors). The clan claimed descent from {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto}}, a son of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|ja|崇神天皇}}, and was categorized as an imperial lineage (皇別). Over time, the clan adopted the titles "Kamitsukeno no Kimi (公)" and later "Kamitsukeno no Asomi (朝臣)." The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records the clan's lineage and traditions, which are also shared with other related clans. This article provides an overview of the Kamitsukeno Clan and its related clans. == Overview == The Kamitsukeno Clan was based in the ancient Kamitsukeno region (modern {{ill|Gunma Prefecture|ja|群馬県}}), as indicated by its name. The term ''Kenō'' (毛野) referred to the areas of modern-day Gunma and Tochigi Prefectures in ancient times.{{Kotobank|毛野|MyPedia|ja}} The region was later divided into {{ill|Kōzuke Province|ja|上野国}} (Gunma) and {{ill|Shimotsuke Province|ja|下野国}} (Tochigi). Gunma Prefecture, in particular, is home to many [[kofun]] (ancient Kofuns), indicating the region's significance in early Japan (see [[Kenō]]). The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records that the clan originated from {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto}}, who was dispatched to govern the eastern provinces under imperial command. The text also describes the Kamitsukeno Clan's military and diplomatic activities, particularly concerning interactions with the [[Emishi]] and [[Korea]]. However, whether the clan was a local ruling family or one dispatched from the central court remains unclear.Hirofumi Yamamoto, "History of Gunma You Don't Know" (Yōsensha). Archaeological evidence and later texts support the clan's involvement in regional governance and foreign relations.Toru Wakasa, "Regional Administration in the Ancient Kofun Period" (Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2021). By the late 7th century, the Kamitsukeno Clan became one of the "Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces" (東国六腹朝臣), which included the {{ill|Shimotsukeno Clan|ja|下毛野氏|lt=Shimotsukeno clan}}, Ōno Clan, Ikeda Clan, Sami Clan, and Kuramochi Clan. These clans played active roles as mid-level aristocrats in the imperial court.{{Kotobank|Kamitsukeno Clan|ja}} == Genealogy == The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} records that {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto}}, a son of Emperor Sujin, was dispatched to govern the eastern provinces. It also states that he was the ancestor of the {{ill|Kamitsukeno no Kimi|ja|上毛野君}} and {{ill|Shimotsukeno no Kimi|ja|下毛野君}}.''Nihon Shoki,'' Emperor Sujin, 48th Year. The {{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記}} contains similar records.''Kojiki,'' Emperor Sujin. The {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|ja|新撰姓氏録}} states that the Kamitsukeno Asomi (Upper Capital Courtier) lineage was descended from Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto.''Shinsen Shōjiroku,'' Kamitsukeno Asomi, Imperial Lineage (Right Capital). Furthermore, the {{ill|Kokuzō Hongi|ja|国造本紀}} mentions that Toyoki Iribiko's grandson, {{ill|Hikosashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島王}}, was appointed as the first {{ill|kuni no miyatsuko|ja|国造}} of the Kamitsukeno region after pacifying twelve eastern provinces.''Kokuzō Hongi,'' Kamitsukeno Kuni no Miyatsuko. == Historical Overview == The Kamitsukeno Clan's transition from regional power to court aristocracy is evident in both textual and archaeological records. During the early Kofun period, the region saw the construction of large Kofuns, such as the {{ill|Ōtatenjin'yama Kofun|ja|太田天神山古墳}}, indicating a powerful local authority.Taichirō Shiraishi, "Kofun and the Yamato Court" (Bungeishunjū). The clan's later prominence in the central court suggests their integration into the Yamato polity. By the mid-7th century, members of the Kamitsukeno Clan held positions as provincial governors, military leaders, and diplomats. The clan's influence waned in the Heian period, with members becoming lower-ranking court officials and regional administrators.{{Kotobank|Kamitsukeno Clan|Encyclopedia Nipponica|ja}} == Notable Figures == Notable descendants of {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto}} include: * {{ill|Hikosashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島王}} - Appointed governor of 15 eastern provinces. * {{ill|Mimorowake no Mikoto|ja|御諸別命|1=Mimorowake|lt=Mimorowake-no-Mikoto}} - Military leader who fought the Emishi. * {{ill|Aratawake|ja|荒田別|1=Aratawake}} - Diplomat to Korea. * {{ill|Takihase|ja|竹葉瀬}} - Contributed to Korean diplomacy. * {{ill|Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko|ja|上毛野稚子|1=Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko}} - General in the Baekje campaigns. == Related Clans == The Kamitsukeno Clan's descendants include several related families, categorized as the "Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces." These clans shared genealogical and geographical ties with the Kamitsukeno lineage. == See Also == * {{ill|Kenō|ja|毛野}} * {{ill|Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces|ja|東国六腹朝臣}} ** {{ill|Shimotsukeno Clan|ja|下毛野氏|lt=Shimotsukeno clan}} * {{ill|Kamitsuke no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|上毛野国造}} * {{ill|Akagi Shrine|ja|赤城神社}} [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]][[Category:Completion tier 2]]
