[[ja:上毛野氏]] [[ja:上毛野氏]] [[ja:上毛野氏]] {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[da:d:Q11547765]] Wikidata name: Kamitsukeno clan [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 07:19, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[da:d:Q11547765]] Wikidata name: Kamitsukeno clan [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 03:58, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Ancient Japanese Clans | Clan Name = Kamitsukeno Clan | image = [[File:Akagi-jinja (Miyosawa) torii.JPG|280px]]
Shrine associated with the clan: {{ill|Miyosawa Akagi Shrine|ja|赤城神社_(前橋市三夜沢町)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miyosawa Akagi Shrine|qq=}} ([[:en:Gunma Prefecture|Gunma Prefecture]], [[:en:Maebashi|Maebashi]]) | Title = Kamitsukeno no Kimi (公)
Later Kamitsukeno no Asomi | Founder = '''Claimed''': {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|qq=}}
([[:en:Emperor Sujin|Emperor Sujin]]'s son) | Lineage = Imperial | Origin = Kamitsukeno Province (modern-day [[:en:Gunma Prefecture|Gunma Prefecture]])
Later relocated to Yamashiro Province | Notable Members = See [[Kamitsukeno Clan#Notable Figures|Notable Figures Section]] | Descendants = See [[Kamitsukeno Clan#Related Clans|Related Clans Section]] }} The '''Kamitsukeno Clan''' (上毛野氏, also read as ''Kamitsukenu'')While the reading ''Kamitsukenu'' has been used since the Edo period, some scholars argue this is a misreading. See [[Kenō#Origin and Pronunciation]]. was a [[Japanese clans|Japanese clan]] that took its name from the region of Kamitsukeno. Members of the clan often served as [[kuni no miyatsuko]] (provincial governors). The clan claimed descent from {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|qq=}}, a son of [[:en:Emperor Sujin|Emperor Sujin]], and was categorized as an imperial lineage (皇別). Over time, the clan adopted the titles "Kamitsukeno no Kimi (公)" and later "Kamitsukeno no Asomi (朝臣)." The [[:en:Nihon Shoki|Nihon Shoki]] records the clan's lineage and traditions, which are also shared with other related clans. This article provides an overview of the Kamitsukeno Clan and its related clans. == Overview == The Kamitsukeno Clan was based in the ancient Kamitsukeno region (modern [[:en:Gunma Prefecture|Gunma Prefecture]]), as indicated by its name. The term ''Kenō'' (毛野) referred to the areas of modern-day Gunma and Tochigi Prefectures in ancient times.{{Kotobank|毛野|MyPedia|ja}} The region was later divided into [[:en:Kōzuke Province|Kōzuke Province]] (Gunma) and [[:en:Shimotsuke Province|Shimotsuke Province]] (Tochigi). Gunma Prefecture, in particular, is home to many [[kofun]] (ancient Kofuns), indicating the region's significance in early Japan (see [[:en:Keno Province|Keno Province]]). The [[:en:Nihon Shoki|Nihon Shoki]] records that the clan originated from {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|qq=}}, who was dispatched to govern the eastern provinces under imperial command. The text also describes the Kamitsukeno Clan's military and diplomatic activities, particularly concerning interactions with the [[:en:Emishi|Emishi]] and [[:en:Korea|Korea]]. However, whether the clan was a local ruling family or one dispatched from the central court remains unclear.Hirofumi Yamamoto, "History of Gunma You Don't Know" (Yōsensha). Archaeological evidence and later texts support the clan's involvement in regional governance and foreign relations.Toru Wakasa, "Regional Administration in the Ancient Kofun Period" (Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2021). By the late 7th century, the Kamitsukeno Clan became one of the "Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces" (東国六腹朝臣), which included the {{ill|Shimotsukeno Clan|ja|下毛野氏|1=Shimotsukeno clan|lt=Shimotsukeno clan|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsukeno Clan|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsukeno clan|qq=}}, Ōno Clan, Ikeda Clan, Sami Clan, and Kuramochi Clan. These clans played active roles as mid-level aristocrats in the imperial court.{{Kotobank|Kamitsukeno Clan|ja}} == Genealogy == The [[:en:Nihon Shoki|Nihon Shoki]] records that {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|qq=}}, a son of Emperor Sujin, was dispatched to govern the eastern provinces. It also states that he was the ancestor of the {{ill|Kamitsukeno clan|lt=Kamitsukeno clan|lt=Kamitsukeno no Kimi|ja|上毛野君|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamitsukeno no Kimi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 上毛野氏}} and {{ill|Shimotsukeno clan|lt=Shimotsukeno clan|lt=Shimotsukeno no Kimi|ja|下毛野君|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsukeno no Kimi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 上毛野氏}}.''Nihon Shoki,'' Emperor Sujin, 48th Year. The [[:en:Kojiki|Kojiki]] contains similar records.''Kojiki,'' Emperor Sujin. The [[:en:Shinsen Shōjiroku|Shinsen Shōjiroku]] states that the Kamitsukeno Asomi (Upper Capital Courtier) lineage was descended from Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto.''Shinsen Shōjiroku,'' Kamitsukeno Asomi, Imperial Lineage (Right Capital). Furthermore, the {{ill|Kokuzō Hongi|ja|国造本紀|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokuzō Hongi|1=Kokuzo Hongi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q133833194}} mentions that Toyoki Iribiko's grandson, {{ill|Hikosashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島王|1=Hikosashima no Ōkimi|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hikosashima no Mikoto|qq=}}, was appointed as the first [[:en:Kuni no miyatsuko|kuni no miyatsuko]] of the Kamitsukeno region after pacifying twelve eastern provinces.''Kokuzō Hongi,'' Kamitsukeno Kuni no Miyatsuko. == Historical Overview == The Kamitsukeno Clan's transition from regional power to court aristocracy is evident in both textual and archaeological records. During the early Kofun period, the region saw the construction of large Kofuns, such as the [[:en:Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun]], indicating a powerful local authority.Taichirō Shiraishi, "Kofun and the Yamato Court" (Bungeishunjū). The clan's later prominence in the central court suggests their integration into the Yamato polity. By the mid-7th century, members of the Kamitsukeno Clan held positions as provincial governors, military leaders, and diplomats. The clan's influence waned in the Heian period, with members becoming lower-Ranking court officials and regional administrators.{{Kotobank|Kamitsukeno Clan|Encyclopedia Nipponica|ja}} == Notable Figures == Notable descendants of {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|qq=}} include: * {{ill|Hikosashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島王|1=Hikosashima no Ōkimi|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hikosashima no Mikoto|qq=}} - Appointed governor of 15 eastern provinces. * {{ill|Mimorowake no Mikoto|ja|御諸別命|1=Mimorowake|lt=Mimorowake-no-Mikoto|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mimorowake no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Mimorowake|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 御諸別王}} - Military leader who fought the Emishi. * {{ill|Aratawake|ja|荒田別|1=Aratawake|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aratawake|13=User:Immanuelle/Aratawake|qq=}} - Diplomat to Korea. * {{ill|Takehase|ja|竹葉瀬|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takihase|qq=}} - Contributed to Korean diplomacy. * {{ill|Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko|ja|上毛野稚子|1=Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko|qq=}} - General in the Baekje campaigns. == Related Clans == The Kamitsukeno Clan's descendants include several related families, categorized as the "Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces." These clans shared genealogical and geographical ties with the Kamitsukeno lineage. == See Also == * [[:en:Keno Province|Kenō]] * {{ill|Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces|ja|東国六腹朝臣|1=Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces|2=ja|3=東国六腹朝臣|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces|13=User:Immanuelle/Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces|qq=}} ** {{ill|Shimotsukeno Clan|ja|下毛野氏|1=Shimotsukeno clan|lt=Shimotsukeno clan|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsukeno Clan|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsukeno clan|qq=}} * {{ill|Kamitsuke no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|上毛野国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamitsuke no Kuni no Miyatsuko|qq=}} * {{ill|Akagi Shrine|ja|赤城神社|1=Akagi Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akagi Shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/Akagi Shrines|qq=}} *{{ill|List of Shikinaisha in Kōzuke Province|ja|上野国の式内社一覧|lt_ja=上野国|qq=Kōzuke|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of Shikinaisha in Kōzuke Province|qq=}} *{{ill|List of Shikinaisha in Shimotsuke Province|ja|下野国の式内社一覧|lt_ja=下野国|qq=Shimotsuke|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of Shikinaisha in Shimotsuke Province|qq=}} ==References== == Bibliography == {{translated page|ja|上毛野氏|version=99202847|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Completion tier 8]] [[Category:Japanese clans]] [[Category:History of Gunma Prefecture]] }} [[ja:上毛野氏]] [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]] [[Category:Uji]] [[Category:Clans of Kantō Region]] {{wikidata link|Q11547765}} [[Category:Wikidata no short description]] [[Category:Wikidata has English label]]

[[ja:上毛野氏]] [[ja:上毛野氏]] [[ja:上毛野氏]] [[ja:上毛野氏]] {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[da:d:Q11547765]] Wikidata name: Kamitsukeno clan [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 07:19, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[da:d:Q11547765]] Wikidata name: Kamitsukeno clan [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 03:58, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Ancient Japanese Clans | Clan Name = Kamitsukeno Clan | image = [[File:Akagi-jinja (Miyosawa) torii.JPG|280px]]
Shrine associated with the clan: {{ill|Miyosawa Akagi Shrine|ja|赤城神社_(前橋市三夜沢町)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miyosawa Akagi Shrine|qq=}} ([[:en:Gunma Prefecture|Gunma Prefecture]], [[:en:Maebashi|Maebashi]]) | Title = Kamitsukeno no Kimi (公)
Later Kamitsukeno no Asomi | Founder = '''Claimed''': {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|qq=}}
([[:en:Emperor Sujin|Emperor Sujin]]'s son) | Lineage = Imperial | Origin = Kamitsukeno Province (modern-day [[:en:Gunma Prefecture|Gunma Prefecture]])
Later relocated to Yamashiro Province | Notable Members = See [[Kamitsukeno Clan#Notable Figures|Notable Figures Section]] | Descendants = See [[Kamitsukeno Clan#Related Clans|Related Clans Section]] }} The '''Kamitsukeno Clan''' (上毛野氏, also read as ''Kamitsukenu'')While the reading ''Kamitsukenu'' has been used since the Edo period, some scholars argue this is a misreading. See [[Kenō#Origin and Pronunciation]]. was a [[Japanese clans|Japanese clan]] that took its name from the region of Kamitsukeno. Members of the clan often served as [[kuni no miyatsuko]] (provincial governors). The clan claimed descent from {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|qq=}}, a son of [[:en:Emperor Sujin|Emperor Sujin]], and was categorized as an imperial lineage (皇別). Over time, the clan adopted the titles "Kamitsukeno no Kimi (公)" and later "Kamitsukeno no Asomi (朝臣)." The [[:en:Nihon Shoki|Nihon Shoki]] records the clan's lineage and traditions, which are also shared with other related clans. This article provides an overview of the Kamitsukeno Clan and its related clans. == Overview == The Kamitsukeno Clan was based in the ancient Kamitsukeno region (modern [[:en:Gunma Prefecture|Gunma Prefecture]]), as indicated by its name. The term ''Kenō'' (毛野) referred to the areas of modern-day Gunma and Tochigi Prefectures in ancient times.{{Kotobank|毛野|MyPedia|ja}} The region was later divided into [[:en:Kōzuke Province|Kōzuke Province]] (Gunma) and [[:en:Shimotsuke Province|Shimotsuke Province]] (Tochigi). Gunma Prefecture, in particular, is home to many [[kofun]] (ancient Kofuns), indicating the region's significance in early Japan (see [[:en:Keno Province|Keno Province]]). The [[:en:Nihon Shoki|Nihon Shoki]] records that the clan originated from {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|qq=}}, who was dispatched to govern the eastern provinces under imperial command. The text also describes the Kamitsukeno Clan's military and diplomatic activities, particularly concerning interactions with the [[:en:Emishi|Emishi]] and [[:en:Korea|Korea]]. However, whether the clan was a local ruling family or one dispatched from the central court remains unclear.Hirofumi Yamamoto, "History of Gunma You Don't Know" (Yōsensha). Archaeological evidence and later texts support the clan's involvement in regional governance and foreign relations.Toru Wakasa, "Regional Administration in the Ancient Kofun Period" (Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2021). By the late 7th century, the Kamitsukeno Clan became one of the "Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces" (東国六腹朝臣), which included the {{ill|Shimotsukeno Clan|ja|下毛野氏|1=Shimotsukeno clan|lt=Shimotsukeno clan|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsukeno Clan|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsukeno clan|qq=}}, Ōno Clan, Ikeda Clan, Sami Clan, and Kuramochi Clan. These clans played active roles as mid-level aristocrats in the imperial court.{{Kotobank|Kamitsukeno Clan|ja}} == Genealogy == The [[:en:Nihon Shoki|Nihon Shoki]] records that {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|qq=}}, a son of Emperor Sujin, was dispatched to govern the eastern provinces. It also states that he was the ancestor of the {{ill|Kamitsukeno clan|lt=Kamitsukeno clan|lt=Kamitsukeno no Kimi|ja|上毛野君|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamitsukeno no Kimi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 上毛野氏}} and {{ill|Shimotsukeno clan|lt=Shimotsukeno clan|lt=Shimotsukeno no Kimi|ja|下毛野君|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsukeno no Kimi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 上毛野氏}}.''Nihon Shoki,'' Emperor Sujin, 48th Year. The [[:en:Kojiki|Kojiki]] contains similar records.''Kojiki,'' Emperor Sujin. The [[:en:Shinsen Shōjiroku|Shinsen Shōjiroku]] states that the Kamitsukeno Asomi (Upper Capital Courtier) lineage was descended from Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto.''Shinsen Shōjiroku,'' Kamitsukeno Asomi, Imperial Lineage (Right Capital). Furthermore, the {{ill|Kokuzō Hongi|ja|国造本紀|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokuzō Hongi|1=Kokuzo Hongi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q133833194}} mentions that Toyoki Iribiko's grandson, {{ill|Hikosashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島王|1=Hikosashima no Ōkimi|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hikosashima no Mikoto|qq=}}, was appointed as the first [[:en:Kuni no miyatsuko|kuni no miyatsuko]] of the Kamitsukeno region after pacifying twelve eastern provinces.''Kokuzō Hongi,'' Kamitsukeno Kuni no Miyatsuko. == Historical Overview == The Kamitsukeno Clan's transition from regional power to court aristocracy is evident in both textual and archaeological records. During the early Kofun period, the region saw the construction of large Kofuns, such as the [[:en:Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun]], indicating a powerful local authority.Taichirō Shiraishi, "Kofun and the Yamato Court" (Bungeishunjū). The clan's later prominence in the central court suggests their integration into the Yamato polity. By the mid-7th century, members of the Kamitsukeno Clan held positions as provincial governors, military leaders, and diplomats. The clan's influence waned in the Heian period, with members becoming lower-Ranking court officials and regional administrators.{{Kotobank|Kamitsukeno Clan|Encyclopedia Nipponica|ja}} == Notable Figures == Notable descendants of {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|qq=}} include: * {{ill|Hikosashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島王|1=Hikosashima no Ōkimi|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hikosashima no Mikoto|qq=}} - Appointed governor of 15 eastern provinces. * {{ill|Mimorowake no Mikoto|ja|御諸別命|1=Mimorowake|lt=Mimorowake-no-Mikoto|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mimorowake no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Mimorowake|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 御諸別王}} - Military leader who fought the Emishi. * {{ill|Aratawake|ja|荒田別|1=Aratawake|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aratawake|13=User:Immanuelle/Aratawake|qq=}} - Diplomat to Korea. * {{ill|Takehase|ja|竹葉瀬|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takihase|qq=}} - Contributed to Korean diplomacy. * {{ill|Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko|ja|上毛野稚子|1=Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko|qq=}} - General in the Baekje campaigns. == Related Clans == The Kamitsukeno Clan's descendants include several related families, categorized as the "Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces." These clans shared genealogical and geographical ties with the Kamitsukeno lineage. == See Also == * [[:en:Keno Province|Kenō]] * {{ill|Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces|ja|東国六腹朝臣|1=Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces|2=ja|3=東国六腹朝臣|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces|13=User:Immanuelle/Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces|qq=}} ** {{ill|Shimotsukeno Clan|ja|下毛野氏|1=Shimotsukeno clan|lt=Shimotsukeno clan|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsukeno Clan|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsukeno clan|qq=}} * {{ill|Kamitsuke no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|上毛野国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamitsuke no Kuni no Miyatsuko|qq=}} * {{ill|Akagi Shrine|ja|赤城神社|1=Akagi Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akagi Shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/Akagi Shrines|qq=}} *{{ill|List of Shikinaisha in Kōzuke Province|ja|上野国の式内社一覧|lt_ja=上野国|qq=Kōzuke|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of Shikinaisha in Kōzuke Province|qq=}} *{{ill|List of Shikinaisha in Shimotsuke Province|ja|下野国の式内社一覧|lt_ja=下野国|qq=Shimotsuke|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of Shikinaisha in Shimotsuke Province|qq=}} ==References== == Bibliography == {{translated page|ja|上毛野氏|version=99202847|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| }} [[ja:上毛野氏]] {{wikidata link|Q11547765}} [[Category:Clans of Kantō Region]] [[Category:Completion tier 8]] [[Category:History of Gunma Prefecture]] [[Category:Japanese clans]] [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]] [[Category:Uji]] [[Category:Wikidata has English label]] [[Category:Wikidata no short description]]

[[ja:上毛野氏]] [[ja:上毛野氏]] [[ja:上毛野氏]] [[ja:上毛野氏]] {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[da:d:Q11547765]] Wikidata name: Kamitsukeno clan [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 07:19, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[da:d:Q11547765]] Wikidata name: Kamitsukeno clan [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 03:58, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Ancient Japanese Clans | Clan Name = Kamitsukeno Clan | image = [[File:Akagi-jinja (Miyosawa) torii.JPG|280px]]
Shrine associated with the clan: {{ill|Miyosawa Akagi Shrine|ja|赤城神社_(前橋市三夜沢町)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miyosawa Akagi Shrine|qq=}} ([[:en:Gunma Prefecture|Gunma Prefecture]], [[:en:Maebashi|Maebashi]]) | Title = Kamitsukeno no Kimi (公)
Later Kamitsukeno no Asomi | Founder = '''Claimed''': {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|qq=}}
([[:en:Emperor Sujin|Emperor Sujin]]'s son) | Lineage = Imperial | Origin = Kamitsukeno Province (modern-day [[:en:Gunma Prefecture|Gunma Prefecture]])
Later relocated to Yamashiro Province | Notable Members = See [[Kamitsukeno Clan#Notable Figures|Notable Figures Section]] | Descendants = See [[Kamitsukeno Clan#Related Clans|Related Clans Section]] }} The '''Kamitsukeno Clan''' (上毛野氏, also read as ''Kamitsukenu'')While the reading ''Kamitsukenu'' has been used since the Edo period, some scholars argue this is a misreading. See [[Kenō#Origin and Pronunciation]]. was a [[Japanese clans|Japanese clan]] that took its name from the region of Kamitsukeno. Members of the clan often served as [[kuni no miyatsuko]] (provincial governors). The clan claimed descent from {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|qq=}}, a son of [[:en:Emperor Sujin|Emperor Sujin]], and was categorized as an imperial lineage (皇別). Over time, the clan adopted the titles "Kamitsukeno no Kimi (公)" and later "Kamitsukeno no Asomi (朝臣)." The [[:en:Nihon Shoki|Nihon Shoki]] records the clan's lineage and traditions, which are also shared with other related clans. This article provides an overview of the Kamitsukeno Clan and its related clans. == Overview == The Kamitsukeno Clan was based in the ancient Kamitsukeno region (modern [[:en:Gunma Prefecture|Gunma Prefecture]]), as indicated by its name. The term ''Kenō'' (毛野) referred to the areas of modern-day Gunma and Tochigi Prefectures in ancient times.{{Kotobank|毛野|MyPedia|ja}} The region was later divided into [[:en:Kōzuke Province|Kōzuke Province]] (Gunma) and [[:en:Shimotsuke Province|Shimotsuke Province]] (Tochigi). Gunma Prefecture, in particular, is home to many [[kofun]] (ancient Kofuns), indicating the region's significance in early Japan (see [[:en:Keno Province|Keno Province]]). The [[:en:Nihon Shoki|Nihon Shoki]] records that the clan originated from {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|qq=}}, who was dispatched to govern the eastern provinces under imperial command. The text also describes the Kamitsukeno Clan's military and diplomatic activities, particularly concerning interactions with the [[:en:Emishi|Emishi]] and [[:en:Korea|Korea]]. However, whether the clan was a local ruling family or one dispatched from the central court remains unclear.Hirofumi Yamamoto, "History of Gunma You Don't Know" (Yōsensha). Archaeological evidence and later texts support the clan's involvement in regional governance and foreign relations.Toru Wakasa, "Regional Administration in the Ancient Kofun Period" (Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2021). By the late 7th century, the Kamitsukeno Clan became one of the "Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces" (東国六腹朝臣), which included the {{ill|Shimotsukeno Clan|ja|下毛野氏|1=Shimotsukeno clan|lt=Shimotsukeno clan|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsukeno Clan|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsukeno clan|qq=}}, Ōno Clan, Ikeda Clan, Sami Clan, and Kuramochi Clan. These clans played active roles as mid-level aristocrats in the imperial court.{{Kotobank|Kamitsukeno Clan|ja}} == Genealogy == The [[:en:Nihon Shoki|Nihon Shoki]] records that {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|qq=}}, a son of Emperor Sujin, was dispatched to govern the eastern provinces. It also states that he was the ancestor of the {{ill|Kamitsukeno clan|lt=Kamitsukeno clan|lt=Kamitsukeno no Kimi|ja|上毛野君|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamitsukeno no Kimi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 上毛野氏}} and {{ill|Shimotsukeno clan|lt=Shimotsukeno clan|lt=Shimotsukeno no Kimi|ja|下毛野君|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsukeno no Kimi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 上毛野氏}}.''Nihon Shoki,'' Emperor Sujin, 48th Year. The [[:en:Kojiki|Kojiki]] contains similar records.''Kojiki,'' Emperor Sujin. The [[:en:Shinsen Shōjiroku|Shinsen Shōjiroku]] states that the Kamitsukeno Asomi (Upper Capital Courtier) lineage was descended from Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto.''Shinsen Shōjiroku,'' Kamitsukeno Asomi, Imperial Lineage (Right Capital). Furthermore, the {{ill|Kokuzō Hongi|ja|国造本紀|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokuzō Hongi|1=Kokuzo Hongi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q133833194}} mentions that Toyoki Iribiko's grandson, {{ill|Hikosashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島王|1=Hikosashima no Ōkimi|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hikosashima no Mikoto|qq=}}, was appointed as the first [[:en:Kuni no miyatsuko|kuni no miyatsuko]] of the Kamitsukeno region after pacifying twelve eastern provinces.''Kokuzō Hongi,'' Kamitsukeno Kuni no Miyatsuko. == Historical Overview == The Kamitsukeno Clan's transition from regional power to court aristocracy is evident in both textual and archaeological records. During the early Kofun period, the region saw the construction of large Kofuns, such as the [[:en:Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun]], indicating a powerful local authority.Taichirō Shiraishi, "Kofun and the Yamato Court" (Bungeishunjū). The clan's later prominence in the central court suggests their integration into the Yamato polity. By the mid-7th century, members of the Kamitsukeno Clan held positions as provincial governors, military leaders, and diplomats. The clan's influence waned in the Heian period, with members becoming lower-Ranking court officials and regional administrators.{{Kotobank|Kamitsukeno Clan|Encyclopedia Nipponica|ja}} == Notable Figures == Notable descendants of {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|qq=}} include: * {{ill|Hikosashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島王|1=Hikosashima no Ōkimi|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hikosashima no Mikoto|qq=}} - Appointed governor of 15 eastern provinces. * {{ill|Mimorowake no Mikoto|ja|御諸別命|1=Mimorowake|lt=Mimorowake-no-Mikoto|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mimorowake no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Mimorowake|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 御諸別王}} - Military leader who fought the Emishi. * {{ill|Aratawake|ja|荒田別|1=Aratawake|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aratawake|13=User:Immanuelle/Aratawake|qq=}} - Diplomat to Korea. * {{ill|Takehase|ja|竹葉瀬|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takihase|qq=}} - Contributed to Korean diplomacy. * {{ill|Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko|ja|上毛野稚子|1=Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko|qq=}} - General in the Baekje campaigns. == Related Clans == The Kamitsukeno Clan's descendants include several related families, categorized as the "Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces." These clans shared genealogical and geographical ties with the Kamitsukeno lineage. == See Also == * [[:en:Keno Province|Kenō]] * {{ill|Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces|ja|東国六腹朝臣|1=Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces|2=ja|3=東国六腹朝臣|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces|13=User:Immanuelle/Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces|qq=}} ** {{ill|Shimotsukeno Clan|ja|下毛野氏|1=Shimotsukeno clan|lt=Shimotsukeno clan|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsukeno Clan|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsukeno clan|qq=}} * {{ill|Kamitsuke no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|上毛野国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamitsuke no Kuni no Miyatsuko|qq=}} * {{ill|Akagi Shrine|ja|赤城神社|1=Akagi Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akagi Shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/Akagi Shrines|qq=}} *{{ill|List of Shikinaisha in Kōzuke Province|ja|上野国の式内社一覧|lt_ja=上野国|qq=Kōzuke|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of Shikinaisha in Kōzuke Province|qq=}} *{{ill|List of Shikinaisha in Shimotsuke Province|ja|下野国の式内社一覧|lt_ja=下野国|qq=Shimotsuke|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of Shikinaisha in Shimotsuke Province|qq=}} ==References== == Bibliography == {{translated page|ja|上毛野氏|version=99202847|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| }} [[ja:上毛野氏]] {{wikidata link|Q11547765}} [[Category:Clans of Kantō Region]] [[Category:Completion tier 8]] [[Category:History of Gunma Prefecture]] [[Category:Japanese clans]] [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]] [[Category:Uji]] [[Category:Wikidata has English label]] [[Category:Wikidata no short description]]

[[ja:上毛野氏]] [[ja:上毛野氏]] [[ja:上毛野氏]] [[ja:上毛野氏]] {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[da:d:Q11547765]] Wikidata name: Kamitsukeno clan [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 07:19, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[da:d:Q11547765]] Wikidata name: Kamitsukeno clan [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 03:58, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Ancient Japanese Clans | Clan Name = Kamitsukeno Clan | image = [[File:Akagi-jinja (Miyosawa) torii.JPG|280px]]
Shrine associated with the clan: {{ill|Miyosawa Akagi Shrine|ja|赤城神社_(前橋市三夜沢町)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miyosawa Akagi Shrine|qq=}} ([[:en:Gunma Prefecture|Gunma Prefecture]], [[:en:Maebashi|Maebashi]]) | Title = Kamitsukeno no Kimi (公)
Later Kamitsukeno no Asomi | Founder = '''Claimed''': {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|qq=}}
([[:en:Emperor Sujin|Emperor Sujin]]'s son) | Lineage = Imperial | Origin = Kamitsukeno Province (modern-day [[:en:Gunma Prefecture|Gunma Prefecture]])
Later relocated to Yamashiro Province | Notable Members = See [[Kamitsukeno Clan#Notable Figures|Notable Figures Section]] | Descendants = See [[Kamitsukeno Clan#Related Clans|Related Clans Section]] }} The '''Kamitsukeno Clan''' (上毛野氏, also read as ''Kamitsukenu'')While the reading ''Kamitsukenu'' has been used since the Edo period, some scholars argue this is a misreading. See [[Kenō#Origin and Pronunciation]]. was a [[Japanese clans|Japanese clan]] that took its name from the region of Kamitsukeno. Members of the clan often served as [[kuni no miyatsuko]] (provincial governors). The clan claimed descent from {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|qq=}}, a son of [[:en:Emperor Sujin|Emperor Sujin]], and was categorized as an imperial lineage (皇別). Over time, the clan adopted the titles "Kamitsukeno no Kimi (公)" and later "Kamitsukeno no Asomi (朝臣)." The [[:en:Nihon Shoki|Nihon Shoki]] records the clan's lineage and traditions, which are also shared with other related clans. This article provides an overview of the Kamitsukeno Clan and its related clans. == Overview == The Kamitsukeno Clan was based in the ancient Kamitsukeno region (modern [[:en:Gunma Prefecture|Gunma Prefecture]]), as indicated by its name. The term ''Kenō'' (毛野) referred to the areas of modern-day Gunma and Tochigi Prefectures in ancient times.{{Kotobank|毛野|MyPedia|ja}} The region was later divided into [[:en:Kōzuke Province|Kōzuke Province]] (Gunma) and [[:en:Shimotsuke Province|Shimotsuke Province]] (Tochigi). Gunma Prefecture, in particular, is home to many [[kofun]] (ancient Kofuns), indicating the region's significance in early Japan (see [[:en:Keno Province|Keno Province]]). The [[:en:Nihon Shoki|Nihon Shoki]] records that the clan originated from {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|qq=}}, who was dispatched to govern the eastern provinces under imperial command. The text also describes the Kamitsukeno Clan's military and diplomatic activities, particularly concerning interactions with the [[:en:Emishi|Emishi]] and [[:en:Korea|Korea]]. However, whether the clan was a local ruling family or one dispatched from the central court remains unclear.Hirofumi Yamamoto, "History of Gunma You Don't Know" (Yōsensha). Archaeological evidence and later texts support the clan's involvement in regional governance and foreign relations.Toru Wakasa, "Regional Administration in the Ancient Kofun Period" (Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2021). By the late 7th century, the Kamitsukeno Clan became one of the "Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces" (東国六腹朝臣), which included the {{ill|Shimotsukeno Clan|ja|下毛野氏|1=Shimotsukeno clan|lt=Shimotsukeno clan|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsukeno Clan|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsukeno clan|qq=}}, Ōno Clan, Ikeda Clan, Sami Clan, and Kuramochi Clan. These clans played active roles as mid-level aristocrats in the imperial court.{{Kotobank|Kamitsukeno Clan|ja}} == Genealogy == The [[:en:Nihon Shoki|Nihon Shoki]] records that {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|qq=}}, a son of Emperor Sujin, was dispatched to govern the eastern provinces. It also states that he was the ancestor of the {{ill|Kamitsukeno clan|lt=Kamitsukeno clan|lt=Kamitsukeno no Kimi|ja|上毛野君|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamitsukeno no Kimi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 上毛野氏}} and {{ill|Shimotsukeno clan|lt=Shimotsukeno clan|lt=Shimotsukeno no Kimi|ja|下毛野君|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsukeno no Kimi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 上毛野氏}}.''Nihon Shoki,'' Emperor Sujin, 48th Year. The [[:en:Kojiki|Kojiki]] contains similar records.''Kojiki,'' Emperor Sujin. The [[:en:Shinsen Shōjiroku|Shinsen Shōjiroku]] states that the Kamitsukeno Asomi (Upper Capital Courtier) lineage was descended from Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto.''Shinsen Shōjiroku,'' Kamitsukeno Asomi, Imperial Lineage (Right Capital). Furthermore, the {{ill|Kokuzō Hongi|ja|国造本紀|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokuzō Hongi|1=Kokuzo Hongi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q133833194}} mentions that Toyoki Iribiko's grandson, {{ill|Hikosashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島王|1=Hikosashima no Ōkimi|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hikosashima no Mikoto|qq=}}, was appointed as the first [[:en:Kuni no miyatsuko|kuni no miyatsuko]] of the Kamitsukeno region after pacifying twelve eastern provinces.''Kokuzō Hongi,'' Kamitsukeno Kuni no Miyatsuko. == Historical Overview == The Kamitsukeno Clan's transition from regional power to court aristocracy is evident in both textual and archaeological records. During the early Kofun period, the region saw the construction of large Kofuns, such as the [[:en:Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun]], indicating a powerful local authority.Taichirō Shiraishi, "Kofun and the Yamato Court" (Bungeishunjū). The clan's later prominence in the central court suggests their integration into the Yamato polity. By the mid-7th century, members of the Kamitsukeno Clan held positions as provincial governors, military leaders, and diplomats. The clan's influence waned in the Heian period, with members becoming lower-Ranking court officials and regional administrators.{{Kotobank|Kamitsukeno Clan|Encyclopedia Nipponica|ja}} == Notable Figures == Notable descendants of {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|qq=}} include: * {{ill|Hikosashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島王|1=Hikosashima no Ōkimi|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hikosashima no Mikoto|qq=}} - Appointed governor of 15 eastern provinces. * {{ill|Mimorowake no Mikoto|ja|御諸別命|1=Mimorowake|lt=Mimorowake-no-Mikoto|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mimorowake no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Mimorowake|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 御諸別王}} - Military leader who fought the Emishi. * {{ill|Aratawake|ja|荒田別|1=Aratawake|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aratawake|13=User:Immanuelle/Aratawake|qq=}} - Diplomat to Korea. * {{ill|Takehase|ja|竹葉瀬|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takihase|qq=}} - Contributed to Korean diplomacy. * {{ill|Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko|ja|上毛野稚子|1=Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko|qq=}} - General in the Baekje campaigns. == Related Clans == The Kamitsukeno Clan's descendants include several related families, categorized as the "Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces." These clans shared genealogical and geographical ties with the Kamitsukeno lineage. == See Also == * [[:en:Keno Province|Kenō]] * {{ill|Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces|ja|東国六腹朝臣|1=Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces|2=ja|3=東国六腹朝臣|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces|13=User:Immanuelle/Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces|qq=}} ** {{ill|Shimotsukeno Clan|ja|下毛野氏|1=Shimotsukeno clan|lt=Shimotsukeno clan|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsukeno Clan|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsukeno clan|qq=}} * {{ill|Kamitsuke no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|上毛野国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamitsuke no Kuni no Miyatsuko|qq=}} * {{ill|Akagi Shrine|ja|赤城神社|1=Akagi Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akagi Shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/Akagi Shrines|qq=}} *{{ill|List of Shikinaisha in Kōzuke Province|ja|上野国の式内社一覧|lt_ja=上野国|qq=Kōzuke|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of Shikinaisha in Kōzuke Province|qq=}} *{{ill|List of Shikinaisha in Shimotsuke Province|ja|下野国の式内社一覧|lt_ja=下野国|qq=Shimotsuke|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of Shikinaisha in Shimotsuke Province|qq=}} ==References== == Bibliography == {{translated page|ja|上毛野氏|version=99202847|comment=Imported full ja history}} [[ja:上毛野氏]] {{wikidata link|Q11547765}} [[Category:Clans of Kantō Region]] [[Category:Completion tier 8]] [[Category:History of Gunma Prefecture]] [[Category:Japanese clans]] [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]] [[Category:Uji]] [[Category:Wikidata has English label]] [[Category:Wikidata no short description]]

[[ja:上毛野氏]] [[ja:上毛野氏]] [[ja:上毛野氏]] [[ja:上毛野氏]] {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[da:d:Q11547765]] Wikidata name: Kamitsukeno clan [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 07:19, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[da:d:Q11547765]] Wikidata name: Kamitsukeno clan [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 03:58, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Ancient Japanese Clans | Clan Name = Kamitsukeno Clan | image = [[File:Akagi-jinja (Miyosawa) torii.JPG|280px]]
Shrine associated with the clan: {{ill|Miyosawa Akagi Shrine|ja|赤城神社_(前橋市三夜沢町)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miyosawa Akagi Shrine|qq=}} ({{ill|Gunma Prefecture|en|Gunma Prefecture|WD=Q129499|lt=Gunma Prefecture}}, {{ill|Maebashi|en|Maebashi|WD=Q201613|lt=Maebashi}}) | Title = Kamitsukeno no Kimi (公)
Later Kamitsukeno no Asomi | Founder = '''Claimed''': {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|qq=}}
({{ill|Emperor Sujin|en|Emperor Sujin|WD=Q333530|lt=Emperor Sujin}}'s son) | Lineage = Imperial | Origin = Kamitsukeno Province (modern-day {{ill|Gunma Prefecture|en|Gunma Prefecture|WD=Q129499|lt=Gunma Prefecture}})
Later relocated to Yamashiro Province | Notable Members = See [[Kamitsukeno Clan#Notable Figures|Notable Figures Section]] | Descendants = See [[Kamitsukeno Clan#Related Clans|Related Clans Section]] }} The '''Kamitsukeno Clan''' (上毛野氏, also read as ''Kamitsukenu'')While the reading ''Kamitsukenu'' has been used since the Edo period, some scholars argue this is a misreading. See [[Kenō#Origin and Pronunciation]]. was a [[Japanese clans|Japanese clan]] that took its name from the region of Kamitsukeno. Members of the clan often served as [[kuni no miyatsuko]] (provincial governors). The clan claimed descent from {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|qq=}}, a son of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|en|Emperor Sujin|WD=Q333530|lt=Emperor Sujin}}, and was categorized as an imperial lineage (皇別). Over time, the clan adopted the titles "Kamitsukeno no Kimi (公)" and later "Kamitsukeno no Asomi (朝臣)." The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|WD=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki}} records the clan's lineage and traditions, which are also shared with other related clans. This article provides an overview of the Kamitsukeno Clan and its related clans. == Overview == The Kamitsukeno Clan was based in the ancient Kamitsukeno region (modern {{ill|Gunma Prefecture|en|Gunma Prefecture|WD=Q129499|lt=Gunma Prefecture}}), as indicated by its name. The term ''Kenō'' (毛野) referred to the areas of modern-day Gunma and Tochigi Prefectures in ancient times.{{Kotobank|毛野|MyPedia|ja}} The region was later divided into {{ill|Kōzuke Province|en|Kōzuke Province|WD=Q1054838|lt=Kōzuke Province}} (Gunma) and {{ill|Shimotsuke Province|en|Shimotsuke Province|WD=Q1053699|lt=Shimotsuke Province}} (Tochigi). Gunma Prefecture, in particular, is home to many [[kofun]] (ancient Kofuns), indicating the region's significance in early Japan (see {{ill|Keno Province|en|Keno Province|WD=Q1886428|lt=Keno Province}}). The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|WD=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki}} records that the clan originated from {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|qq=}}, who was dispatched to govern the eastern provinces under imperial command. The text also describes the Kamitsukeno Clan's military and diplomatic activities, particularly concerning interactions with the {{ill|Emishi|en|Emishi|WD=Q932574|lt=Emishi}} and {{ill|Korea|en|Korea|WD=Q18097|lt=Korea}}. However, whether the clan was a local ruling family or one dispatched from the central court remains unclear.Hirofumi Yamamoto, "History of Gunma You Don't Know" (Yōsensha). Archaeological evidence and later texts support the clan's involvement in regional governance and foreign relations.Toru Wakasa, "Regional Administration in the Ancient Kofun Period" (Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2021). By the late 7th century, the Kamitsukeno Clan became one of the "Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces" (東国六腹朝臣), which included the {{ill|Shimotsukeno Clan|ja|下毛野氏|1=Shimotsukeno clan|lt=Shimotsukeno clan|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsukeno Clan|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsukeno clan|qq=}}, Ōno Clan, Ikeda Clan, Sami Clan, and Kuramochi Clan. These clans played active roles as mid-level aristocrats in the imperial court.{{Kotobank|Kamitsukeno Clan|ja}} == Genealogy == The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|WD=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki}} records that {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|qq=}}, a son of Emperor Sujin, was dispatched to govern the eastern provinces. It also states that he was the ancestor of the {{ill|Kamitsukeno clan|lt=Kamitsukeno clan|lt=Kamitsukeno no Kimi|ja|上毛野君|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamitsukeno no Kimi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 上毛野氏}} and {{ill|Shimotsukeno clan|lt=Shimotsukeno clan|lt=Shimotsukeno no Kimi|ja|下毛野君|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsukeno no Kimi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 上毛野氏}}.''Nihon Shoki,'' Emperor Sujin, 48th Year. The {{ill|Kojiki|en|Kojiki|WD=Q813031|lt=Kojiki}} contains similar records.''Kojiki,'' Emperor Sujin. The {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|Shinsen Shōjiroku|WD=Q1045362|lt=Shinsen Shōjiroku}} states that the Kamitsukeno Asomi (Upper Capital Courtier) lineage was descended from Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto.''Shinsen Shōjiroku,'' Kamitsukeno Asomi, Imperial Lineage (Right Capital). Furthermore, the {{ill|Kokuzō Hongi|ja|国造本紀|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokuzō Hongi|1=Kokuzo Hongi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q133833194}} mentions that Toyoki Iribiko's grandson, {{ill|Hikosashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島王|1=Hikosashima no Ōkimi|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hikosashima no Mikoto|qq=}}, was appointed as the first {{ill|Kuni no miyatsuko|en|Kuni no miyatsuko|WD=Q2483673|lt=kuni no miyatsuko}} of the Kamitsukeno region after pacifying twelve eastern provinces.''Kokuzō Hongi,'' Kamitsukeno Kuni no Miyatsuko. == Historical Overview == The Kamitsukeno Clan's transition from regional power to court aristocracy is evident in both textual and archaeological records. During the early Kofun period, the region saw the construction of large Kofuns, such as the {{ill|Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|en|Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|WD=Q11444167|lt=Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun}}, indicating a powerful local authority.Taichirō Shiraishi, "Kofun and the Yamato Court" (Bungeishunjū). The clan's later prominence in the central court suggests their integration into the Yamato polity. By the mid-7th century, members of the Kamitsukeno Clan held positions as provincial governors, military leaders, and diplomats. The clan's influence waned in the Heian period, with members becoming lower-Ranking court officials and regional administrators.{{Kotobank|Kamitsukeno Clan|Encyclopedia Nipponica|ja}} == Notable Figures == Notable descendants of {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|1=Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyokiirihiko-no-Mikoto|qq=}} include: * {{ill|Hikosashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島王|1=Hikosashima no Ōkimi|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hikosashima no Mikoto|qq=}} - Appointed governor of 15 eastern provinces. * {{ill|Mimorowake no Mikoto|ja|御諸別命|1=Mimorowake|lt=Mimorowake-no-Mikoto|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mimorowake no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Mimorowake|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 御諸別王}} - Military leader who fought the Emishi. * {{ill|Aratawake|ja|荒田別|1=Aratawake|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aratawake|13=User:Immanuelle/Aratawake|qq=}} - Diplomat to Korea. * {{ill|Takehase|ja|竹葉瀬|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takihase|qq=}} - Contributed to Korean diplomacy. * {{ill|Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko|ja|上毛野稚子|1=Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko|qq=}} - General in the Baekje campaigns. == Related Clans == The Kamitsukeno Clan's descendants include several related families, categorized as the "Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces." These clans shared genealogical and geographical ties with the Kamitsukeno lineage. == See Also == * {{ill|Keno Province|en|Keno Province|WD=Q1886428|lt=Kenō}} * {{ill|Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces|ja|東国六腹朝臣|1=Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces|2=ja|3=東国六腹朝臣|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces|13=User:Immanuelle/Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces|qq=}} ** {{ill|Shimotsukeno Clan|ja|下毛野氏|1=Shimotsukeno clan|lt=Shimotsukeno clan|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsukeno Clan|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsukeno clan|qq=}} * {{ill|Kamitsuke no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|上毛野国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamitsuke no Kuni no Miyatsuko|qq=}} * {{ill|Akagi Shrine|ja|赤城神社|1=Akagi Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akagi Shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/Akagi Shrines|qq=}} *{{ill|List of Shikinaisha in Kōzuke Province|ja|上野国の式内社一覧|lt_ja=上野国|qq=Kōzuke|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of Shikinaisha in Kōzuke Province|qq=}} *{{ill|List of Shikinaisha in Shimotsuke Province|ja|下野国の式内社一覧|lt_ja=下野国|qq=Shimotsuke|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of Shikinaisha in Shimotsuke Province|qq=}} ==References== == Bibliography == {{translated page|ja|上毛野氏|version=99202847|comment=Imported full ja history}} [[ja:上毛野氏]] {{wikidata link|Q11547765}} [[Category:Clans of Kantō Region]] [[Category:Completion tier 8]] [[Category:History of Gunma Prefecture]] [[Category:Japanese clans]] [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]] [[Category:Uji]] [[Category:qq]] [[Category:Wikidata no short description]]

[[ja:上毛野氏]] [[ja:上毛野氏]] [[ja:上毛野氏]] [[ja:上毛野氏]] {{Ancient Japanese Clans | Clan Name = Kamitsukeno Clan | image = [[File:Akagi-jinja (Miyosawa) torii.JPG|280px]]
Shrine associated with the clan: {{ill|Miyosawa Akagi Shrine|ja|赤城神社_(前橋市三夜沢町)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miyosawa Akagi Shrine|qq=}} ({{ill|Gunma Prefecture|en|Gunma Prefecture|WD=Q129499|lt=Gunma Prefecture}}, {{ill|Maebashi|en|Maebashi|WD=Q201613|lt=Maebashi}}) | Title = Kamitsukeno no Kimi (公)
Later Kamitsukeno no Asomi | Founder = '''Claimed''': {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Prince Toyokiirihiko|1=Prince Toyokiirihiko|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Prince Toyokiirihiko|qq=}}
({{ill|Emperor Sujin|en|Emperor Sujin|WD=Q333530|lt=Emperor Sujin}}'s son) | Lineage = Imperial | Origin = Kamitsukeno Province (modern-day {{ill|Gunma Prefecture|en|Gunma Prefecture|WD=Q129499|lt=Gunma Prefecture}})
Later relocated to Yamashiro Province | Notable Members = See [[Kamitsukeno Clan#Notable Figures|Notable Figures Section]] | Descendants = See [[Kamitsukeno Clan#Related Clans|Related Clans Section]] }} The '''Kamitsukeno Clan''' (上毛野氏, also read as ''Kamitsukenu'')While the reading ''Kamitsukenu'' has been used since the Edo period, some scholars argue this is a misreading. See [[Kenō#Origin and Pronunciation]]. was a [[Japanese clans|Japanese clan]] that took its name from the region of Kamitsukeno. Members of the clan often served as [[kuni no miyatsuko]] (provincial governors). The clan claimed descent from {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Prince Toyokiirihiko|1=Prince Toyokiirihiko|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Prince Toyokiirihiko|qq=}}, a son of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|en|Emperor Sujin|WD=Q333530|lt=Emperor Sujin}}, and was categorized as an imperial lineage (皇別). Over time, the clan adopted the titles "Kamitsukeno no Kimi (公)" and later "Kamitsukeno no Asomi (朝臣)." The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|WD=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki}} records the clan's lineage and traditions, which are also shared with other related clans. This article provides an overview of the Kamitsukeno Clan and its related clans. == Overview == The Kamitsukeno Clan was based in the ancient Kamitsukeno region (modern {{ill|Gunma Prefecture|en|Gunma Prefecture|WD=Q129499|lt=Gunma Prefecture}}), as indicated by its name. The term ''Kenō'' (毛野) referred to the areas of modern-day Gunma and Tochigi Prefectures in ancient times.{{Kotobank|毛野|MyPedia|ja}} The region was later divided into {{ill|Kōzuke Province|en|Kōzuke Province|WD=Q1054838|lt=Kōzuke Province}} (Gunma) and {{ill|Shimotsuke Province|en|Shimotsuke Province|WD=Q1053699|lt=Shimotsuke Province}} (Tochigi). Gunma Prefecture, in particular, is home to many [[kofun]] (ancient Kofuns), indicating the region's significance in early Japan (see {{ill|Keno Province|en|Keno Province|WD=Q1886428|lt=Keno Province}}). The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|WD=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki}} records that the clan originated from {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Prince Toyokiirihiko|1=Prince Toyokiirihiko|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Prince Toyokiirihiko|qq=}}, who was dispatched to govern the eastern provinces under imperial command. The text also describes the Kamitsukeno Clan's military and diplomatic activities, particularly concerning interactions with the {{ill|Emishi|en|Emishi|WD=Q932574|lt=Emishi}} and {{ill|Korea|en|Korea|WD=Q18097|lt=Korea}}. However, whether the clan was a local ruling family or one dispatched from the central court remains unclear.Hirofumi Yamamoto, "History of Gunma You Don't Know" (Yōsensha). Archaeological evidence and later texts support the clan's involvement in regional governance and foreign relations.Toru Wakasa, "Regional Administration in the Ancient Kofun Period" (Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2021). By the late 7th century, the Kamitsukeno Clan became one of the "Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces" (東国六腹朝臣), which included the {{ill|Shimotsukeno Clan|ja|下毛野氏|1=Shimotsukeno clan|lt=Shimotsukeno clan|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsukeno Clan|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsukeno clan|qq=}}, Ōno Clan, Ikeda Clan, Sami Clan, and Kuramochi Clan. These clans played active roles as mid-level aristocrats in the imperial court.{{Kotobank|Kamitsukeno Clan|ja}} == Genealogy == The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|WD=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki}} records that {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Prince Toyokiirihiko|1=Prince Toyokiirihiko|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Prince Toyokiirihiko|qq=}}, a son of Emperor Sujin, was dispatched to govern the eastern provinces. It also states that he was the ancestor of the {{ill|Kamitsukeno clan|lt=Kamitsukeno clan|lt=Kamitsukeno no Kimi|ja|上毛野君|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamitsukeno no Kimi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 上毛野氏}} and {{ill|Shimotsukeno clan|lt=Shimotsukeno clan|lt=Shimotsukeno no Kimi|ja|下毛野君|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsukeno no Kimi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 上毛野氏}}.''Nihon Shoki,'' Emperor Sujin, 48th Year. The {{ill|Kojiki|en|Kojiki|WD=Q813031|lt=Kojiki}} contains similar records.''Kojiki,'' Emperor Sujin. The {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|Shinsen Shōjiroku|WD=Q1045362|lt=Shinsen Shōjiroku}} states that the Kamitsukeno Asomi (Upper Capital Courtier) lineage was descended from Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto.''Shinsen Shōjiroku,'' Kamitsukeno Asomi, Imperial Lineage (Right Capital). Furthermore, the {{ill|Kokuzō Hongi|ja|国造本紀|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokuzō Hongi|1=Kokuzo Hongi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q133833194}} mentions that Toyoki Iribiko's grandson, {{ill|Hikosashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島王|1=Hikosashima no Ōkimi|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hikosashima no Mikoto|qq=}}, was appointed as the first {{ill|Kuni no miyatsuko|en|Kuni no miyatsuko|WD=Q2483673|lt=kuni no miyatsuko}} of the Kamitsukeno region after pacifying twelve eastern provinces.''Kokuzō Hongi,'' Kamitsukeno Kuni no Miyatsuko. == Historical Overview == The Kamitsukeno Clan's transition from regional power to court aristocracy is evident in both textual and archaeological records. During the early Kofun period, the region saw the construction of large Kofuns, such as the {{ill|Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|en|Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|WD=Q11444167|lt=Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun}}, indicating a powerful local authority.Taichirō Shiraishi, "Kofun and the Yamato Court" (Bungeishunjū). The clan's later prominence in the central court suggests their integration into the Yamato polity. By the mid-7th century, members of the Kamitsukeno Clan held positions as provincial governors, military leaders, and diplomats. The clan's influence waned in the Heian period, with members becoming lower-Ranking court officials and regional administrators.{{Kotobank|Kamitsukeno Clan|Encyclopedia Nipponica|ja}} == Notable Figures == Notable descendants of {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Prince Toyokiirihiko|1=Prince Toyokiirihiko|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Prince Toyokiirihiko|qq=}} include: * {{ill|Hikosashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島王|1=Hikosashima no Ōkimi|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hikosashima no Mikoto|qq=}} - Appointed governor of 15 eastern provinces. * {{ill|Mimorowake no Mikoto|ja|御諸別命|1=Mimorowake|lt=Mimorowake-no-Mikoto|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mimorowake no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Mimorowake|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 御諸別王}} - Military leader who fought the Emishi. * {{ill|Aratawake|ja|荒田別|1=Aratawake|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aratawake|13=User:Immanuelle/Aratawake|qq=}} - Diplomat to Korea. * {{ill|Takehase|ja|竹葉瀬|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takihase|qq=}} - Contributed to Korean diplomacy. * {{ill|Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko|ja|上毛野稚子|1=Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko|qq=}} - General in the Baekje campaigns. == Related Clans == The Kamitsukeno Clan's descendants include several related families, categorized as the "Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces." These clans shared genealogical and geographical ties with the Kamitsukeno lineage. == See Also == * {{ill|Keno Province|en|Keno Province|WD=Q1886428|lt=Kenō}} * {{ill|Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces|ja|東国六腹朝臣|1=Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces|2=ja|3=東国六腹朝臣|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces|13=User:Immanuelle/Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces|qq=}} ** {{ill|Shimotsukeno Clan|ja|下毛野氏|1=Shimotsukeno clan|lt=Shimotsukeno clan|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsukeno Clan|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsukeno clan|qq=}} * {{ill|Kamitsuke no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|上毛野国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamitsuke no Kuni no Miyatsuko|qq=}} * {{ill|Akagi Shrine|ja|赤城神社|1=Akagi Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akagi Shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/Akagi Shrines|qq=}} *{{ill|List of Shikinaisha in Kōzuke Province|ja|上野国の式内社一覧|lt_ja=上野国|qq=Kōzuke|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of Shikinaisha in Kōzuke Province|qq=}} *{{ill|List of Shikinaisha in Shimotsuke Province|ja|下野国の式内社一覧|lt_ja=下野国|qq=Shimotsuke|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of Shikinaisha in Shimotsuke Province|qq=}} ==References== == Bibliography == {{translated page|ja|上毛野氏|version=99202847|comment=Imported full ja history}} [[ja:上毛野氏]] {{wikidata link|Q11547765}} [[Category:Clans of Kantō Region]] [[Category:Completion tier 8]] [[Category:History of Gunma Prefecture]] [[Category:Japanese clans]] [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]] [[Category:Uji]] [[Category:qq]] [[Category:Wikidata no short description]]

[[ja:上毛野氏]] [[ja:上毛野氏]] [[ja:上毛野氏]] [[ja:上毛野氏]] {{Ancient Japanese Clans | Clan Name = Kamitsukeno Clan | image = [[File:Akagi-jinja (Miyosawa) torii.JPG|280px]]
Shrine associated with the clan: {{ill|Miyosawa Akagi Shrine|ja|赤城神社_(前橋市三夜沢町)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miyosawa Akagi Shrine|qq=}} ({{ill|Gunma Prefecture|en|Gunma Prefecture|WD=Q129499|lt=Gunma Prefecture}}, {{ill|Maebashi|en|Maebashi|WD=Q201613|lt=Maebashi}}) | Title = Kamitsukeno no Kimi (公)
Later Kamitsukeno no Asomi | Founder = '''Claimed''': {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Prince Toyokiirihiko|2=ja|3=豊城入彦命|WD=Q11633375|1=Prince Toyokiirihiko|1=Prince Toyokiirihiko|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Prince Toyokiirihiko|qq=}}
({{ill|Emperor Sujin|en|Emperor Sujin|WD=Q333530|lt=Emperor Sujin}}'s son) | Lineage = Imperial | Origin = Kamitsukeno Province (modern-day {{ill|Gunma Prefecture|en|Gunma Prefecture|WD=Q129499|lt=Gunma Prefecture}})
Later relocated to Yamashiro Province | Notable Members = See [[Kamitsukeno Clan#Notable Figures|Notable Figures Section]] | Descendants = See [[Kamitsukeno Clan#Related Clans|Related Clans Section]] }} The '''Kamitsukeno Clan''' (上毛野氏, also read as ''Kamitsukenu'')While the reading ''Kamitsukenu'' has been used since the Edo period, some scholars argue this is a misreading. See [[Kenō#Origin and Pronunciation]]. was a [[Japanese clans|Japanese clan]] that took its name from the region of Kamitsukeno. Members of the clan often served as [[kuni no miyatsuko]] (provincial governors). The clan claimed descent from {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Prince Toyokiirihiko|2=ja|3=豊城入彦命|WD=Q11633375|1=Prince Toyokiirihiko|1=Prince Toyokiirihiko|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Prince Toyokiirihiko|qq=}}, a son of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|en|Emperor Sujin|WD=Q333530|lt=Emperor Sujin}}, and was categorized as an imperial lineage (皇別). Over time, the clan adopted the titles "Kamitsukeno no Kimi (公)" and later "Kamitsukeno no Asomi (朝臣)." The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|WD=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki}} records the clan's lineage and traditions, which are also shared with other related clans. This article provides an overview of the Kamitsukeno Clan and its related clans. == Overview == The Kamitsukeno Clan was based in the ancient Kamitsukeno region (modern {{ill|Gunma Prefecture|en|Gunma Prefecture|WD=Q129499|lt=Gunma Prefecture}}), as indicated by its name. The term ''Kenō'' (毛野) referred to the areas of modern-day Gunma and Tochigi Prefectures in ancient times.{{Kotobank|毛野|MyPedia|ja}} The region was later divided into {{ill|Kōzuke Province|en|Kōzuke Province|WD=Q1054838|lt=Kōzuke Province}} (Gunma) and {{ill|Shimotsuke Province|en|Shimotsuke Province|WD=Q1053699|lt=Shimotsuke Province}} (Tochigi). Gunma Prefecture, in particular, is home to many [[kofun]] (ancient Kofuns), indicating the region's significance in early Japan (see {{ill|Keno Province|en|Keno Province|WD=Q1886428|lt=Keno Province}}). The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|WD=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki}} records that the clan originated from {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Prince Toyokiirihiko|2=ja|3=豊城入彦命|WD=Q11633375|1=Prince Toyokiirihiko|1=Prince Toyokiirihiko|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Prince Toyokiirihiko|qq=}}, who was dispatched to govern the eastern provinces under imperial command. The text also describes the Kamitsukeno Clan's military and diplomatic activities, particularly concerning interactions with the {{ill|Emishi|en|Emishi|WD=Q932574|lt=Emishi}} and {{ill|Korea|en|Korea|WD=Q18097|lt=Korea}}. However, whether the clan was a local ruling family or one dispatched from the central court remains unclear.Hirofumi Yamamoto, "History of Gunma You Don't Know" (Yōsensha). Archaeological evidence and later texts support the clan's involvement in regional governance and foreign relations.Toru Wakasa, "Regional Administration in the Ancient Kofun Period" (Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2021). By the late 7th century, the Kamitsukeno Clan became one of the "Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces" (東国六腹朝臣), which included the {{ill|Shimotsukeno Clan|ja|下毛野氏|1=Shimotsukeno clan|lt=Shimotsukeno clan|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsukeno Clan|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsukeno clan|qq=}}, Ōno Clan, Ikeda Clan, Sami Clan, and Kuramochi Clan. These clans played active roles as mid-level aristocrats in the imperial court.{{Kotobank|Kamitsukeno Clan|ja}} == Genealogy == The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|WD=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki}} records that {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Prince Toyokiirihiko|2=ja|3=豊城入彦命|WD=Q11633375|1=Prince Toyokiirihiko|1=Prince Toyokiirihiko|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Prince Toyokiirihiko|qq=}}, a son of Emperor Sujin, was dispatched to govern the eastern provinces. It also states that he was the ancestor of the {{ill|Kamitsukeno clan|lt=Kamitsukeno clan|lt=Kamitsukeno no Kimi|ja|上毛野君|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamitsukeno no Kimi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 上毛野氏}} and {{ill|Shimotsukeno clan|lt=Shimotsukeno clan|lt=Shimotsukeno no Kimi|ja|下毛野君|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsukeno no Kimi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 上毛野氏}}.''Nihon Shoki,'' Emperor Sujin, 48th Year. The {{ill|Kojiki|en|Kojiki|WD=Q813031|lt=Kojiki}} contains similar records.''Kojiki,'' Emperor Sujin. The {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|Shinsen Shōjiroku|WD=Q1045362|lt=Shinsen Shōjiroku}} states that the Kamitsukeno Asomi (Upper Capital Courtier) lineage was descended from Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto.''Shinsen Shōjiroku,'' Kamitsukeno Asomi, Imperial Lineage (Right Capital). Furthermore, the {{ill|Kokuzō Hongi|ja|国造本紀|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokuzō Hongi|1=Kokuzo Hongi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q133833194}} mentions that Toyoki Iribiko's grandson, {{ill|Hikosashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島王|1=Hikosashima no Ōkimi|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hikosashima no Mikoto|qq=}}, was appointed as the first {{ill|Kuni no miyatsuko|en|Kuni no miyatsuko|WD=Q2483673|lt=kuni no miyatsuko}} of the Kamitsukeno region after pacifying twelve eastern provinces.''Kokuzō Hongi,'' Kamitsukeno Kuni no Miyatsuko. == Historical Overview == The Kamitsukeno Clan's transition from regional power to court aristocracy is evident in both textual and archaeological records. During the early Kofun period, the region saw the construction of large Kofuns, such as the {{ill|Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|en|Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|WD=Q11444167|lt=Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun}}, indicating a powerful local authority.Taichirō Shiraishi, "Kofun and the Yamato Court" (Bungeishunjū). The clan's later prominence in the central court suggests their integration into the Yamato polity. By the mid-7th century, members of the Kamitsukeno Clan held positions as provincial governors, military leaders, and diplomats. The clan's influence waned in the Heian period, with members becoming lower-Ranking court officials and regional administrators.{{Kotobank|Kamitsukeno Clan|Encyclopedia Nipponica|ja}} == Notable Figures == Notable descendants of {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Prince Toyokiirihiko|2=ja|3=豊城入彦命|WD=Q11633375|1=Prince Toyokiirihiko|1=Prince Toyokiirihiko|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Prince Toyokiirihiko|qq=}} include: * {{ill|Hikosashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島王|1=Hikosashima no Ōkimi|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hikosashima no Mikoto|qq=}} - Appointed governor of 15 eastern provinces. * {{ill|Mimorowake no Mikoto|ja|御諸別命|1=Mimorowake|lt=Mimorowake-no-Mikoto|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mimorowake no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Mimorowake|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 御諸別王}} - Military leader who fought the Emishi. * {{ill|Aratawake|ja|荒田別|1=Aratawake|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aratawake|13=User:Immanuelle/Aratawake|qq=}} - Diplomat to Korea. * {{ill|Takehase|ja|竹葉瀬|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takihase|qq=}} - Contributed to Korean diplomacy. * {{ill|Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko|ja|上毛野稚子|1=Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko|qq=}} - General in the Baekje campaigns. == Related Clans == The Kamitsukeno Clan's descendants include several related families, categorized as the "Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces." These clans shared genealogical and geographical ties with the Kamitsukeno lineage. == See Also == * {{ill|Keno Province|en|Keno Province|WD=Q1886428|lt=Kenō}} * {{ill|Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces|ja|東国六腹朝臣|1=Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces|2=ja|3=東国六腹朝臣|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces|13=User:Immanuelle/Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces|qq=}} ** {{ill|Shimotsukeno Clan|ja|下毛野氏|1=Shimotsukeno clan|lt=Shimotsukeno clan|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsukeno Clan|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsukeno clan|qq=}} * {{ill|Kamitsuke no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|上毛野国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamitsuke no Kuni no Miyatsuko|qq=}} * {{ill|Akagi Shrine|ja|赤城神社|1=Akagi Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akagi Shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/Akagi Shrines|qq=}} *{{ill|List of Shikinaisha in Kōzuke Province|ja|上野国の式内社一覧|lt_ja=上野国|qq=Kōzuke|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of Shikinaisha in Kōzuke Province|qq=}} *{{ill|List of Shikinaisha in Shimotsuke Province|ja|下野国の式内社一覧|lt_ja=下野国|qq=Shimotsuke|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of Shikinaisha in Shimotsuke Province|qq=}} ==References== == Bibliography == {{translated page|ja|上毛野氏|version=99202847|comment=Imported full ja history}} [[ja:上毛野氏]] {{wikidata link|Q11547765}} [[Category:Clans of Kantō Region]] [[Category:Completion tier 8]] [[Category:History of Gunma Prefecture]] [[Category:Japanese clans]] [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]] [[Category:Uji]] [[Category:Wikidata no short description]]

[[ja:上毛野氏]] [[ja:上毛野氏]] [[ja:上毛野氏]] [[ja:上毛野氏]] {{Ancient Japanese Clans | Clan Name = Kamitsukeno Clan | image = [[File:Akagi-jinja (Miyosawa) torii.JPG|280px]]
Shrine associated with the clan: {{ill|Miyosawa Akagi Shrine|ja|赤城神社_(前橋市三夜沢町)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miyosawa Akagi Shrine|qq=}} ({{ill|Gunma Prefecture|en|Gunma Prefecture|WD=Q129499|lt=Gunma Prefecture}}, {{ill|Maebashi|en|Maebashi|WD=Q201613|lt=Maebashi}}) | Title = Kamitsukeno no Kimi (公)
Later Kamitsukeno no Asomi | Founder = '''Claimed''': {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Prince Toyokiirihiko|2=ja|3=豊城入彦命|WD=Q11633375|1=Prince Toyokiirihiko|1=Prince Toyokiirihiko|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Prince Toyokiirihiko|qq=}}
({{ill|Emperor Sujin|en|Emperor Sujin|WD=Q333530|lt=Emperor Sujin}}'s son) | Lineage = Imperial | Origin = Kamitsukeno Province (modern-day {{ill|Gunma Prefecture|en|Gunma Prefecture|WD=Q129499|lt=Gunma Prefecture}})
Later relocated to Yamashiro Province | Notable Members = See [[Kamitsukeno Clan#Notable Figures|Notable Figures Section]] | Descendants = See [[Kamitsukeno Clan#Related Clans|Related Clans Section]] }} The '''Kamitsukeno Clan''' (上毛野氏, also read as ''Kamitsukenu'')While the reading ''Kamitsukenu'' has been used since the Edo period, some scholars argue this is a misreading. See [[Kenō#Origin and Pronunciation]]. was a [[Japanese clans|Japanese clan]] that took its name from the region of Kamitsukeno. Members of the clan often served as [[kuni no miyatsuko]] (provincial governors). The clan claimed descent from {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Prince Toyokiirihiko|2=ja|3=豊城入彦命|WD=Q11633375|1=Prince Toyokiirihiko|1=Prince Toyokiirihiko|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Prince Toyokiirihiko|qq=}}, a son of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|en|Emperor Sujin|WD=Q333530|lt=Emperor Sujin}}, and was categorized as an imperial lineage (皇別). Over time, the clan adopted the titles "Kamitsukeno no Kimi (公)" and later "Kamitsukeno no Asomi (朝臣)." The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|WD=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki}} records the clan's lineage and traditions, which are also shared with other related clans. This article provides an overview of the Kamitsukeno Clan and its related clans. == Overview == The Kamitsukeno Clan was based in the ancient Kamitsukeno region (modern {{ill|Gunma Prefecture|en|Gunma Prefecture|WD=Q129499|lt=Gunma Prefecture}}), as indicated by its name. The term ''Kenō'' (毛野) referred to the areas of modern-day Gunma and Tochigi Prefectures in ancient times.{{Kotobank|毛野|MyPedia|ja}} The region was later divided into {{ill|Kōzuke Province|en|Kōzuke Province|WD=Q1054838|lt=Kōzuke Province}} (Gunma) and {{ill|Shimotsuke Province|en|Shimotsuke Province|WD=Q1053699|lt=Shimotsuke Province}} (Tochigi). Gunma Prefecture, in particular, is home to many [[kofun]] (ancient Kofuns), indicating the region's significance in early Japan (see {{ill|Keno Province|en|Keno Province|WD=Q1886428|lt=Keno Province}}). The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|WD=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki}} records that the clan originated from {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Prince Toyokiirihiko|2=ja|3=豊城入彦命|WD=Q11633375|1=Prince Toyokiirihiko|1=Prince Toyokiirihiko|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Prince Toyokiirihiko|qq=}}, who was dispatched to govern the eastern provinces under imperial command. The text also describes the Kamitsukeno Clan's military and diplomatic activities, particularly concerning interactions with the {{ill|Emishi|en|Emishi|WD=Q932574|lt=Emishi}} and {{ill|Korea|en|Korea|WD=Q18097|lt=Korea}}. However, whether the clan was a local ruling family or one dispatched from the central court remains unclear.Hirofumi Yamamoto, "History of Gunma You Don't Know" (Yōsensha). Archaeological evidence and later texts support the clan's involvement in regional governance and foreign relations.Toru Wakasa, "Regional Administration in the Ancient Kofun Period" (Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2021). By the late 7th century, the Kamitsukeno Clan became one of the "Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces" (東国六腹朝臣), which included the {{ill|Shimotsukeno Clan|ja|下毛野氏|1=Shimotsukeno clan|lt=Shimotsukeno clan|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsukeno Clan|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsukeno clan|qq=}}, Ōno Clan, Ikeda Clan, Sami Clan, and Kuramochi Clan. These clans played active roles as mid-level aristocrats in the imperial court.{{Kotobank|Kamitsukeno Clan|ja}} == Genealogy == The {{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|WD=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki}} records that {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Prince Toyokiirihiko|2=ja|3=豊城入彦命|WD=Q11633375|1=Prince Toyokiirihiko|1=Prince Toyokiirihiko|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Prince Toyokiirihiko|qq=}}, a son of Emperor Sujin, was dispatched to govern the eastern provinces. It also states that he was the ancestor of the {{ill|Kamitsukeno clan|lt=Kamitsukeno clan|lt=Kamitsukeno no Kimi|ja|上毛野君|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamitsukeno no Kimi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 上毛野氏}} and {{ill|Shimotsukeno clan|lt=Shimotsukeno clan|lt=Shimotsukeno no Kimi|ja|下毛野君|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsukeno no Kimi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 上毛野氏}}.''Nihon Shoki,'' Emperor Sujin, 48th Year. The {{ill|Kojiki|en|Kojiki|WD=Q813031|lt=Kojiki}} contains similar records.''Kojiki,'' Emperor Sujin. The {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|Shinsen Shōjiroku|WD=Q1045362|lt=Shinsen Shōjiroku}} states that the Kamitsukeno Asomi (Upper Capital Courtier) lineage was descended from Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto.''Shinsen Shōjiroku,'' Kamitsukeno Asomi, Imperial Lineage (Right Capital). Furthermore, the {{ill|Kokuzō Hongi|ja|国造本紀|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokuzō Hongi|1=Kokuzo Hongi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q133833194}} mentions that Toyoki Iribiko's grandson, {{ill|Hikosashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島王|1=Hikosashima no Ōkimi|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hikosashima no Mikoto|qq=}}, was appointed as the first {{ill|Kuni no miyatsuko|en|Kuni no miyatsuko|WD=Q2483673|lt=kuni no miyatsuko}} of the Kamitsukeno region after pacifying twelve eastern provinces.''Kokuzō Hongi,'' Kamitsukeno Kuni no Miyatsuko. == Historical Overview == The Kamitsukeno Clan's transition from regional power to court aristocracy is evident in both textual and archaeological records. During the early Kofun period, the region saw the construction of large Kofuns, such as the {{ill|Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|en|Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun|WD=Q11444167|lt=Ōta Tenjinyama Kofun}}, indicating a powerful local authority.Taichirō Shiraishi, "Kofun and the Yamato Court" (Bungeishunjū). The clan's later prominence in the central court suggests their integration into the Yamato polity. By the mid-7th century, members of the Kamitsukeno Clan held positions as provincial governors, military leaders, and diplomats. The clan's influence waned in the Heian period, with members becoming lower-Ranking court officials and regional administrators.{{Kotobank|Kamitsukeno Clan|Encyclopedia Nipponica|ja}} == Notable Figures == Notable descendants of {{ill|Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|豊城入彦命|1=Prince Toyokiirihiko|2=ja|3=豊城入彦命|WD=Q11633375|1=Prince Toyokiirihiko|1=Prince Toyokiirihiko|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Prince Toyokiirihiko|qq=}} include: * {{ill|Hikosashima no Mikoto|ja|彦狭島王|1=Hikosashima no Ōkimi|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hikosashima no Mikoto|qq=}} - Appointed governor of 15 eastern provinces. * {{ill|Mimorowake no Mikoto|ja|御諸別命|1=Mimorowake|lt=Mimorowake-no-Mikoto|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mimorowake no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Mimorowake|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 御諸別王}} - Military leader who fought the Emishi. * {{ill|Aratawake|ja|荒田別|1=Aratawake|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Aratawake|13=User:Immanuelle/Aratawake|qq=}} - Diplomat to Korea. * {{ill|Takehase|ja|竹葉瀬|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takihase|qq=}} - Contributed to Korean diplomacy. * {{ill|Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko|ja|上毛野稚子|1=Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamitsukeno no Wakatoko|qq=}} - General in the Baekje campaigns. == Related Clans == The Kamitsukeno Clan's descendants include several related families, categorized as the "Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces." These clans shared genealogical and geographical ties with the Kamitsukeno lineage. == See Also == * {{ill|Keno Province|en|Keno Province|WD=Q1886428|lt=Kenō}} * {{ill|Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces|ja|東国六腹朝臣|1=Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces|2=ja|3=東国六腹朝臣|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces|13=User:Immanuelle/Six Aristocratic Clans of the Eastern Provinces|qq=}} ** {{ill|Shimotsukeno Clan|ja|下毛野氏|1=Shimotsukeno clan|lt=Shimotsukeno clan|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsukeno Clan|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsukeno clan|qq=}} * {{ill|Kamitsuke no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|上毛野国造|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamitsuke no Kuni no Miyatsuko|qq=}} * {{ill|Akagi Shrine|ja|赤城神社|1=Akagi Shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akagi Shrine|13=User:Immanuelle/Akagi Shrines|qq=}} *{{ill|List of Shikinaisha in Kōzuke Province|ja|上野国の式内社一覧|lt_ja=上野国|qq=Kōzuke|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of Shikinaisha in Kōzuke Province|qq=}} *{{ill|List of Shikinaisha in Shimotsuke Province|ja|下野国の式内社一覧|lt_ja=下野国|qq=Shimotsuke|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of Shikinaisha in Shimotsuke Province|qq=}} ==References== == Bibliography == {{translated page|ja|上毛野氏|version=99202847|comment=Imported full ja history}} [[ja:上毛野氏]] {{wikidata link|Q11547765}} [[Category:Clans of Kantō Region]] [[Category:Completion tier 8]] [[Category:History of Gunma Prefecture]] [[Category:Japanese clans]] [[Category:Kamitsukeno clan]] [[Category:Uji]] [[Category:Wikidata no short description]] [[Category:pages]]
